It restores the 80-D actor, 401-D critic and Adam moments with fresh stage
history. V65 removes the V40 ordering defect: canonical and two center
bridges are followed by hold-at-target, 25/50/75/100-percent center
acquisition, inner/mid/full workspace acquisition, and only then collision-on
juggling. It removes the duplicate full-center retry. The collision-off
predictor lessons retain the 80--100 ms arrival and settle gates and are
reward-identical to V61. Collision-on stages opt into the task-aligned
auxiliary reward described below.

The rejected GPU1 diagnostic continuation is
`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v66`, launched only through
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v66_resume_v64_stage3.sh`.
It resumes the passed V64 ball-quality checkpoint at true step `28672000`,
global/stage update `47`, SHA-256
`2174d9c964090c9cd95da3f8d43d54783121e2b193e83b4aacde603f8a4c1609`.
It restores actor, critic and Adam moments with fresh stage history, skips the
GPU0 collision-off prerequisite, and starts directly in the full-workspace
placed-ball MDP. Its first active 1.35 s lesson retains the 90 ms launch bridge
but requires mean hits above one and a nonzero hit-3 rate; the 60/30/0 ms
lessons preserve recurrent gates. The obsolete one-hit-only commit is absent.
V66 deliberately removes V64's global V54 single-launch actor anchor: the
stopped V64 Stage 4 reached mean hit1 about `0.922` but hit2/hit3 remained
exactly zero over `6755` rows while anchor KL rose about `0.134 -> 0.666`.
That anchor constrained the policy in post-impact states outside the
single-launch actor's demonstrated task.

The underlying defect was an environment reward-composition error, not a
missing scalar tune. Fixed-contact mode replaced the general task reward with
`fixed_contact_reward_sum`, while later profiles continued to configure and
log general post-hit survival, joint lift, racket-Z/stability/cycle,
ball/racket horizontal impact quality and cadence terms. Those terms never
entered PPO. The new default-off field
`fixed_contact_include_task_aligned_auxiliary_reward` adds only that declared
subset; all V1--V64 rewards remain numerically unchanged. Fixed contact
quality, bounded return, predictor-conditioned S0 shaping, terminal penalties
and completion reward retain their existing paths. The inconsistent legacy
tracking-potential previous-target calculation remains unused because V65/V66
keep its weight at zero.

The preregistered 64-lane frozen V64 causal screen is under
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_rootcause_20260907`. The exact baseline produced
one hit in every lane, no second hit, no full episode and mean length about
`113/200`. Disabling only fixed-workspace termination extended mean length to
about `130` but still produced exactly one hit in every lane; most lanes then
fell through the generic racket-low guard. Thus a tighter/looser termination
threshold did not reveal hidden recovery behavior. The auxiliary-reward
replay preserved aggregate one-hit behavior without PPO and confirmed the
new terms contribute to total reward. GPU contact dynamics show small
cross-process numerical divergence, so lane-exact trajectory equality is not
claimed.

Both formal launchers fix 1024 environments, 128 steps and minibatch 16384;
use 64-lane/1200-step block validation with at least 128 episodes; preserve
fixed base, 4.0 g measured-ball interval, 80-D measured-feedback bounded QVEL,
five recovered-RMP ticks plus five MJX ticks, and `recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2`;
and run inside `training_memory_scope.py`. They require process re-execution
at every passed stage so native JAX/XLA mappings cannot accumulate across
stage compilations. V65/V66 remain experimental, simulation-only and inherit
the unresolved real-camera, new-ball outcome and formal RMP/PD coverage
blockers. They are not hardware releases.

## V38 / V39 Host-Memory Protection After Global OOM (2026-09-06)

The 03:39/03:47 formal runs ended in host **global OOM at 07:03:56 CST**.
GPU0 PID 3101498 had 21,896,428 KiB anonymous RSS; 8 GiB swap had only
124 KiB free. The kernel killed GPU0 and systemd-oomd killed the user init
scope, disrupting the desktop/session. No reboot or contemporaneous NVIDIA
Xid is recorded. GPU0 RSS grew within stage 4; repeated validation/compilation
retention is a suspect, not a proven unique allocation source. V38 stopped at
1707 updates and V39 at 1922. Preserve their outputs and source snapshots.

Both checked-in V38/V39 launchers now require `training_memory_scope.py` for
confirmed launches, with verified cgroup v2 MemoryHigh=10 GiB,
MemoryMax=12 GiB and MemorySwapMax=0. Each trainer and its child processes
inherit the same limit. The monitor requests SIGINT at 9.5 GiB, before kernel
throttling, or below 6 GiB host MemAvailable. It also stops after three
one-second samples above cgroup PSI `some avg10=10%` or `full avg10=5%`, or
immediately if `memory.events:high` increments. It escalates its own process
group to TERM/KILL after 2/5 seconds. Preflight refuses less than 10 GiB host
headroom. Every second it logs usage, host headroom/swap, parsed pressure
streak and cgroup events under `RUN_DIR.memory_guard`.
Kernel verification fails closed even if the recursion marker is forged.
Existing cross-stage JAX cache cleanup is enabled. No physics, PPO batch,
reward, observation, stage identity or numerical convergence gate changes.

The prior monitor placed its active stop at 10.25 GiB, above its 10 GiB
`MemoryHigh`. On 2026-09-06 it therefore sent SIGINT only after reclaim PSI
was already high; the 30-second TERM grace let systemd-oomd kill the user
scope first. The ordering and escalation above are the regression-tested
repair. New V55/V56 runs additionally reuse a single compiled validation
rollout within each stage and release it only at the stage boundary.

These are conservative operating budgets, not measured sufficient capacity
for every stage. Budget exhaustion must stop training, not widen limits or
restart automatically. Two 12 GiB caps leave about 7 GiB of physical capacity
on this host, but other processes still require monitoring. A 50-update delay
between GPU launches does not qualify long-run host memory stability. Before
another long dual run, reproduce repeated validation and stage transitions
under the limits and show stable memory; do not resume the old output/W&B
identities without an explicit compatible recovery contract.

Evidence, local W&B resource series, tests and bounded cgroup probes:
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/host_oom_audit_20260906/`. No PPO restarted
as part of this incident diagnosis. The hard-limit probe used only 128 MiB,
with kernel CONSTRAINT_MEMCG evidence; it was not a GPU experiment.

`178090a9ae019c4b854099e0207f782c0cb2dfb851459f546d66b5b3a84db153`,

V52 also exposed a reward/gate mismatch. The stage gated ball VXY at 0.18
m/s, racket VXY at 0.05 m/s and full angular speed at 0.50 rad/s, while its

costs but accidentally retained that positive angular reward. After 64

`0.2708 m`, while racket VXY and angular speed regressed to `0.0861 m/s` and

The first 32-lane V56 formal attempt exposed a distinct initialization bug:

All launchers require verified physical GPU UUIDs and reject a missing NVIDIA

and never allow unconverged advancement. Acceptance still requires frozen

charged after all five existing component scores simultaneously pass their

`tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v57_resume_v55_u3587.sh`.

The formal 1024-environment V57 run is preserved as negative causal evidence.
It completed 98 updates from the pinned source.  The rolling S0 gate became
fully populated and passed its nonblocking fields, but both deterministic
advance probes failed XY: update 47 measured `0.63120 < 0.68`.  More
decisively, the conditional penalty's eligible fraction fell from roughly 4%
to 1.5%, action norm rose, and return improved while the frozen XY score
regressed.  The supposedly lexicographic cost introduced a negative reward
discontinuity exactly when a trajectory crossed all five gates, so PPO learned
to remain just outside the XY gate and avoid the cost.  V57 must not be used as
a continuation source.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v59` is the GPU0 replacement.  It

is zero and the same weight 160 pays
`eligible * (1 - mean(clipped_action^2)) * dt`.  The score is in `[0, 0.8]`
per step, is never negative, is zero outside the unchanged five-component
gate, and has its unique in-gate maximum at zero QVEL.  Entering the accepted
region therefore cannot lower reward.  Every other reward, control,
observation, reset, physics, PPO value, gate and lesson is unchanged.  Its only

`tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v59_resume_v55_u3587.sh`.

V57/V58 opt into compact rollout telemetry. The environment exposes 607

Confirmed launches now use a waitable transient `Type=exec` service with a
dedicated cgroup: 9.5 GiB proactive per-run stop, 10 GiB `MemoryHigh`, 12 GiB

host stop and the existing 78 C GPU limit.  The startup/runtime values match

whole-tree stop are stronger than that historical guard. Only a declared
non-secret launcher-control environment is forwarded;
API keys and unrelated variables are excluded. `systemd-run --pipe` keeps the
tmux pane attached to stdout/stderr. SIGINT/TERM/KILL target the full named
service cgroup, so stopping the outer tmux client cannot orphan Python, XLA,
tee or W&B descendants. The real integration test confirmed the service
limits, Ctrl-C exit 130, and complete unit/process cleanup.

## Reviewed GPU0 V36 / GPU1 V37 Courses (2026-09-05)

Status: implemented, opt-in, simulation-only; no PPO run is started by this
repository change.  V35 and V32 remain immutable evidence sources.

The GPU numbers below are device assignments, not action semantics.  Both new
profiles remain measured-QVEL/bounded-reference/RMP courses; they do not
reinterpret or replace the released GPU1-QACC policy.  A QACC successor would
require its own profile and control-path validation rather than a resume from
these QVEL/RMP checkpoints.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v36` is the corrected GPU0
acquisition-first course.  Its only launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v36_from_scratch.sh`.
It starts a new 80-D actor and 401-D critic rather than reinterpreting a V35
checkpoint.  In five collision-off lessons the racket always starts at the
same calibrated canonical warm pose while the prediction-conditioned contact
target expands over nested X/Y supports: the near-warm `(-0.10,+0.03) m`
hold, registered center, `[-0.10,+0.10] x
[-0.06,+0.06] m`, `[-0.20,+0.10] x [-0.12,+0.12] m`, then the complete
registered `[-0.30,+0.20] x [-0.12,+0.18] m` plane.  Contact time is sampled
from `0.40--0.50 s`; collision is disabled until these lessons pass.

V36 closes two V35 acceptance loopholes.  First, it no longer initializes the
racket by IK at the sampled absolute target and then asks for only a 15--30 mm
local correction.  Second, final-window readiness alone no longer stands in
for early arrival: deterministic self-validation must pass the simultaneous
XY/Z/pose/VXY/full-omega readiness mask in the `80--100 ms` time-to-contact
band and for at least 80% of the final 100 ms.  After this prerequisite, V36
preserves V35's eight collision-on recurrent stages value-for-value except for
their versioned names.  They retain bounded-height, maximum-50-mm inward return,
contact stability, view, survival and safety gates.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v37` is the corrected GPU1 direct
placed-ball course.  Its only launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v37_resume_v9_actor.sh`.
It deliberately skips GPU0's collision-off acquisition prerequisite: every
episode uses V32's pose-preserving full-workspace racket initialization and
places the stationary ball bottom 1 mm above the physical racket surface.
Collision-on launch and recurrent juggling begin in Stage 1.

The V32 run is negative evidence for its original state/reward contract.  It
remained in Stage 1 for more than 1,700 updates: first-hit rate stayed near
`0.39`, mean episode length near `7.7` control ticks (about `38.5 ms`), and
predicted apex stayed near `2.86 m` instead of the `1.33 m` bridge target.
Return-apex score was effectively zero and target-crossing validity was about
`0.002`.  PPO remained numerically stable (finite KL, explained variance about
`0.90`, no qvel/qacc exceedance), so this is not an optimizer-NaN diagnosis.
The fixed-contact reward multiplied its Gaussian return quality by
next-crossing validity; the approximately 1.5 m apex error also put the
Gaussian itself in a vanishing-gradient tail.  None of the seven independent
outcome constraints includes apex height, leaving only delayed termination
credit for this failure.

V37 adds an event-level symmetric pseudo-Huber apex-error cost with 0.10 m
scale and stage weights `0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.50, 0.60, 0.75`.
It is evaluated at every confirmed hit even when the next crossing lies beyond
the predictor's one-second validity horizon.  The derivative is bounded but
does not disappear at gross errors; a zero default weight keeps all prior
profiles numerically unchanged.  V37 migrates only the pinned clean V9 actor
to the x10 target coordinates, then resets the falling-ball critic and Adam
state because V32 showed that preserving that complete state across the
placed-ball reset/reward MDP was not justified.  Target sequence, placed-ball
reset, collision parameters, actor observation, QVEL/bounded-reference/RMP
control, PPO hyperparameters and final gates remain V32-exact.

Both launchers retain the measured 3.9--4.1 g ball-mass evidence check, pinned
GPU UUID, no-preallocation, 78 C guard, RMP-output replay requirement, explicit
experimental-evidence acknowledgement and output-directory overwrite refusal.
V36/V37 are candidates, not convergence or hardware-coverage claims.  Before a
long run, execute the launcher preflight and a bounded environment/reward smoke;
accept V36 only on both early-arrival and sustained-readiness gates, and accept
V37 Stage 1 only if apex contracts toward its bridge target without regressing
first-hit rate, contact pose/VXY/omega, qvel/qacc or workspace/view safety.

## GPU0 Fixed-Contact V35 Explicit-Time Acquisition Repair

Status: opt-in GPU0 continuation after V34 exposed a second Stage-3 route
defect. Profile `fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v35` is launched
only through
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v35_resume_v31.sh`.
It restores the same clean V31 global-update-394 actor, critic and Adam state,
starts a fresh curriculum window, and deliberately replays the missing
`v35_s0_forced_acquire_15_20mm` prerequisite before the 25--30 mm lesson.

The V22/V34 stages declared a 0.40--0.49 s time to contact, but reset code
permitted rising-half initialization only when the reward-mode string matched
two older modes. V22 renamed the reward to
`fixed_contact_outcome_constrained_v22`, so its requested duration was silently
clipped to one descending half-flight, about 0.23 s. With collision disabled,
the ball then crossed the low view bound at about 0.27 s: deterministic
validation reported mean episode fraction about `0.46` of the 0.60 s horizon,
before the declared 0.40--0.49 s target time. Thus neither V22 nor V34
implemented the intended move-then-settle lesson.

V35 adds an explicit `falling_reset_allow_ascending_phase` reset contract. It
defaults false; the old reward-name behavior is retained for bitwise historical
compatibility. V35 enables it only in the three collision-off prerequisites.
The requested endpoints now resolve to at least 0.40 s instead of less than
0.25 s. V35 otherwise retains V34's annulus repair and every reward, gate,
actor/critic, QVEL, bounded-reference, RMP/PD, collision, DR and PPO value.
Collision-on stages keep their historical falling-reset timing.

V34 W&B run `u0llgqr0` was stopped after logged update 86 and is negative
evidence; its last periodic checkpoint is update 50. It must not be resumed as
the repaired route. V35 restarts from clean V31 rather than carrying critic or
optimizer state trained under the invalid shortened episode.

The environment-level V35 audit reconstructed actual reset-to-contact times of
`0.4023--0.4797 s` (mean `0.4403 s`) across sampled lanes. A 64-lane frozen
rollout completed first episodes at mean `95.56/120 = 0.7964`, instead of the
V34 validation's approximately `0.46`, proving the episode crosses the target
window. Formal V35 is active in `pp_gpu0`, physical GPU0, 1024 environments,
W&B online ID `aewx5yjr`; observed updates 11--18 report `conv_len=0.80` and
steady throughput about 36--42k step/s. This is timing-path evidence, not yet
Stage-2 graduation evidence.

At update 47 the first 256-lane same-stage validation completed with mean
length fraction `0.80639`, confirming the formal validation path also crosses
the target window. It correctly failed graduation: XY/Z/pose/VXY/omega scores
were `0.39113/0.12498/0.01942/0.18773/0.42083`, with ready fraction `0.00913`.
The run continued through at least update 60, return improved from about
`-4.7` to `-0.57`, and the update-50 checkpoint was persisted. No parameter
change is authorized from this early result.

Status: stopped negative GPU0 continuation after the V22/V31/V33 Stage-3

`v34_s0_forced_acquire_25_30mm` because reset-distribution semantics changed.
Curriculum-history resume, optimizer/critic reset, another checkpoint and
observation migration are prohibited.

A frozen 256-lane Stage-3 counterfactual measured XY scores
`0.35984/0.41167/0.47830` for zero action, the Stage-2-entry actor and the
Stage-3-update-300 actor; the unchanged gate is `0.55`. Mean final XY error
improved only `22.94 -> 18.77 mm`. The correction points toward the target
(mean cosine `0.8619`), but signed X/Y response gains are only

## Fixed-Contact-Plane V22 Root-Cause Restart

Status: experimental, from-scratch, simulation-only. Profiles V1--V21 and
their negative results remain immutable. The executable profile is
`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v22`; its only formal launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v22.sh`.

V22 retains the measured-QVEL persistent bounded-reference path, five 1 kHz
recovered-RMP ticks plus five MJX ticks per 200 Hz policy action,
`recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2`, fixed-base 4.0 g/V33 finite-mesh physics and the
existing small registered RMP/PD, mount and contact DR from V4. It starts a new
80-D actor and 401-D asymmetric critic; checkpoint resume and observation
migration are prohibited. The actor preserves separate current-ball and
future-contact predictions, measured q/dq, bounded-reference error, previous
executed action, current/target/error racket position and pose, racket twist,
ball-minus-racket XYZ and bounded current/next return targets. It does not add
camera-age or qdd-estimate channels. Seven target-conditioning values use the
V15 10x input scale.

The root-cause changes are opt-in to V22: a held 90 Hz ball sample is
ballistically advanced to the current 200 Hz query tick only for ContactTarget
generation; tracking reward uses the same policy-available target; full-plane
IK reset now solves fixed surface Z 1.075 m as well as XY and reference pose;
all stages use same-stage deterministic advancement probes; and per-impact
height, pose, racket VXY, full angular speed, impact offset, horizontal step and
outward-progress constraints add independent costs plus an all-pass bonus.
Historical profiles retain their target timing, reset and next-stage probe
semantics.

The first three collision-off stages cover absolute X `[-0.30,0.20] m` and Y
`[-0.12,0.18] m` with a 6x6 equal-weight grid while growing only local contact
displacement `0 -> 15 -> 30 mm/axis`. Collision-on stages then grow recurrent
horizons `1.00 -> 1.35 -> 1.85 -> 3.00 -> 6.00 s`, followed by vision bridge,
vision commit and final unchanged-domain acceptance. They never terminate at
one hit. For the 1.075 m racket plane, 20 mm ball radius and 1.40 m apex, the
nominal cycle is about 0.499 s, so the full gate requires hit12 `>=0.80`, full
rate `>=0.90`, apex `1.38--1.42 m`, racket VXY `<=0.05 m/s`, full angular speed
`<=0.50 rad/s`, next horizontal step `<=0.052 m`, and per-bin hit12 success
`>=0.70` in addition to hit/length/view/safety gates.

Formal PPO uses GPU0, 1024 environments, 128 steps, minibatch 16384, four
epochs, LR `2e-4`, gamma `0.9995`, GAE `0.99`, clip `0.15`, target KL `0.008`,
entropy `1e-4`, log-std `[-4.8,-2.8]`, 256-lane block validation, checkpoint
every 50 updates, archive every 500, and W&B online. It has no stage cap and
cannot advance without rolling plus same-stage block gates.

The pre-registered 1024-env S0 bounded run
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_plane_v22_s0_bounded_gpu0_seed20260951_20260905`
converged at update 47. Deterministic validation passed XY/Z/pose/VXY/omega
`0.96338/0.92201/0.66588/0.97707/0.83293` and joint-ready `0.91681`, with zero
qvel/qacc exceedance. Checkpoint SHA-256 is
`dfd31f871fb7d4f5e9f09132d194ddf77c2327d51af94ea9f2d3c5a44efeb2e0`.
Complete diagnosis, observation layout and smoke evidence are recorded in
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_plane_v22_rootcause_20260905/V22_ROOTCAUSE_REDESIGN_AND_S0_EVIDENCE.md`.

The formal from-scratch GPU0 run is active in the existing `pp_gpu0:0` pane:
seed 20260950, output
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v22_gpu0_seed20260950_20260905`,

the initial ball-to-racket contact displacement are separate: the latter is
bounded to 30 mm per axis/50 mm diagonally, while the dynamic next-contact
target keeps the existing 50 mm per-bounce center-return cap. All nine stages
retain the approach, Z, pose, vxy, full-angular-speed and simultaneous-readiness

gates. A 256-lane, 80-update trial reached hit1 `0.9905`, mean XY/Z/pose

retain absolute `0.0/0.01` caps. The bounded search extends to 128 updates so
eight independent rollout blocks may be tested, while rejected actor, critic
and Adam blocks continue to roll back atomically.

Run bounded V102 only through
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v102_cgroup_transaction_trial128.sh`.
At least one four-seed boundary must commit before new 256-lane holdout seeds
`20261029/20261030` are screened. Formal continuation, if promoted, restarts
the protected V97 best at 1024 environments, keeps the four-seed transaction
guard with no update cap, runs in `pp_gpu0`, and resumes only W&B ID
`v72g0s7a1` with a W&B-only step offset. GPU1 remains blocked until that
formal GPU0 run records at least 50 new updates.

## GPU0 Fixed-Contact-Plane Vision-Robust QVEL/RMP V1

The new opt-in, from-scratch course is
`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v1`, launched only through
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v1.sh`.
It is an independent 80-D actor/7-D QVEL experiment. It must not resume or
migrate a 50/57/67-D actor, critic, optimizer, normalization state, curriculum
history, actuator checkpoint, or phase teacher. V97 Stage 32 contributes only
reviewed PPO/control-domain defaults; no learned state crosses this boundary.
The profile name remains exactly the same because no PPO run or checkpoint was
ever created from its superseded 48-D draft; this registry and the tests now
define the only supported V1 schema.

The control and physics contract is `aligned_fixed -> measured-feedback
bounded q_ref -> recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2 -> XML PD`. The profile rejects an
actuator filter, inverse compensation, target-tracking planner, second RMP, or
post-RMP delay stack. Ball-racket contact uses the final V33 `finite_mesh16`,
`condim=3`, robot-dynamic pair with solref
`[0.0021257295539411024,1.0420726994889375]`, solreffriction `[0,0]`, solimp
`[0.6040711874344367,0.6474683100207307,0.00279752137198626,
0.8573868560606173,4.870438987793294]`, and friction
`[0.13268182450948787,0.11820649851379933,0.0001544955787453423,
0.00002013852195789205,0.00002013852195789205]`. S0--S4 use exactly
`0.004 kg`; S5 uses only the measured `[0.0039,0.0041] kg` interval with
geometrically consistent inertia. These ranges remain candidate simulation
inputs, not hardware-coverage evidence.

The actor observation is exactly 80 values, in this order: measured `q[7]`,
`dq[7]`, persistent `q_ref-q[7]`, previous executed normalized QVEL action
`[7]`; latest directly observed current ball position/velocity `[3+3]`;
separately predicted ball position/velocity at the next contact `[3+3]`, time
to contact, validity and a flag saying whether the forecast used an
extrapolated current state `[1+1+1]`; current racket upper-surface
position, current continuous 6-D orientation, surface linear velocity and body
angular velocity `[3+6+3+3]`; dynamic contact-target position and continuous
6-D orientation `[3+6]`; target-minus-current position error and
`log(R_target^T R_current)` orientation error `[3+3]`; currently observed ball
center minus racket
upper-surface-center XYZ `[3]`; target XY relative to the registered workspace
center `[2]`; and the bounded next-crossing target relative to center `[2]`.
The nine future-contact values describe the ball (contact position, incoming
velocity, horizon, validity and extrapolation-source flag); the nine
contact-target values describe the required racket surface pose (position plus
continuous 6-D orientation). The latter is computed from the former, but they
are not two representations of the same physical state.
The current ball slots are never overwritten by the high-ball predictor: they
hold the latest direct 90 Hz sample, while only the explicitly future slots
may be based on extrapolation. The previous action
is the final clipped/filtered/anti-windup normalized action stored after the
preceding control step, not the network's unclipped sample. The schema contains
neither `time_since_last_real_camera_sample` nor `dq(t)-dq(t-1)`/`qdd_est`.
No command state, actuator delay, DR parameter, true state, quaternion, or
critic-only quantity may enter this schema. The asymmetric critic appends true
ball/racket state, true next crossing/target attitude, realized
contact/mass/observation DR and recovered-RMP internal state, for an exact
401-D critic input under this profile.

`contact_target` is recomputed on every control step from the current direct
observation or the internal high-ball extrapolation. Position is the predicted descending crossing of
the ball center with the fixed surface plane `z*=1.075 m` plus the measured ball
radius. Desired post-impact vertical speed is the ballistic speed for a `1.40
m` apex. The next same-height crossing target moves toward `(0.0,-0.49) m` by
at most `0.050 m` per bounce, rather than demanding a one-bounce return. This
is about `0.1002 m/s` at the nominal orbit and retains `0.20 m/s` as an outer
velocity cap. The nominal impulse direction
sets the target racket normal, whose tilt is clipped to `3 deg`; the warm
reference supplies only the in-plane heading. A target is valid only when the
crossing is finite, descending-plane time is in `[0,1.0] s`, the apex is above
the contact plane, and the target lies inside the registered racket workspace.
This is a bounded geometric nominal, not an identified inverse collision model.

The course has 18 explicit stages: S0 through S5, each with `bridge`, `commit`
and unchanged-domain `consolidate`. S0 disables ball-racket collision and uses
only crossing-target potential plus final-window braking. S1 is a centered
single hit, S2 is XY-bin single-hit coverage, S3 is centered multi-hit return,
S4 is full-range recovery, and S5 adds 90 Hz observation, top-of-view
prediction, measured ball/RMP/PD DR, small contact/racket-mount/damping/armature
DR and a final unchanged-domain
consolidation. S2/S4/S5 sample the registered reachable XY grid with 0.60
center-bin probability and at most 15 mm within-bin jitter. Independent
validation disables that prior and jitter, then assigns lanes round-robin to
the center-relative reachable grid. Its X offsets are
`[-0.30,-0.20,-0.10,0,0.10,0.20,0.30] m` and Y offsets are
`[-0.18,-0.12,-0.06,0,0.06,0.12,0.18] m`; 15 mm jitter still leaves the
racket target inside its hard workspace. The launcher uses 196 validation
lanes, so the complete 49-bin grid has exactly four lanes per bin; training frequency is not
acceptance weighting. Advancement also recomputes exact-bin coverage and
requires every expected bin to contain an episode. S2 applies per-bin hit1
gates `0.75 -> 0.85 -> 0.90`; S4 and S5 bridge require per-bin hit3 rate
`0.60`, then commit/consolidation require per-bin hit12 rates `0.75 -> 0.80`.
Aggregate success cannot compensate for one failing
or absent bin. The aggregate lesson ladder is aligned with the nominal
12-contact episode: S3 mean-hit gates are `3 -> 8 -> 10`, with hit12 introduced
only at commit/consolidation as `0.50 -> 0.80`; S4/S5 mean-hit gates are
`4 -> 9 -> 9.6`, with no hit12 requirement in bridge and `0.75 -> 0.80`
afterward. Their mean-length and truncation gates rise with the same lesson
sequence instead of demanding a 90% full rate at bridge entry. Every S3--S5
lesson nevertheless has an explicit full-episode/time-limit-truncation gate;
S1/S2 omit it only because one-hit success deliberately ends the episode.

Every falling-ball reset crosses the world-frame ball-center plane
`1.075 + 0.020 = 1.095 m`, independent of the warm racket pose; episode racket
anchor Z variation is disabled. S0--S4 have no stochastic
DR and retain exact 4.0 g mass, gravity, observation frame and RMP/PD
parameters. Because the shared XML still has its legacy 2.7 g nominal, the
ball-property DR code path remains enabled with singleton `0.004 kg`, `-9.81
m/s^2` and normalized-inertia `0.4` ranges; this changes the compiled episode
mass without introducing randomness. S5 widens only mass to the measured
`[0.0039,0.0041] kg` interval, then enables the established RMP/PD ranges,
`+/-5%` damping and armature, racket-mount translation `+/-2 mm`, mount
rotation `+/-0.5 deg`, V33 contact solref `+/-5%`, tangent friction `+/-10%`,
and the declared observation noise/bias. RMP target-publication hold is exactly
zero in S0--S4; S5 bridge uses `5%` hold starts with a `1.1%` 2--9 tick tail,
and commit/consolidation use `8%` with a `2.2%` tail.
Its incoming reset apex is reduced to `0.20--0.24 m` above the fixed crossing
so every lane starts below the randomized optical edge and must accumulate a
fresh causal history on the post-impact rising arc.
The profile-specific evidence validator and quantifier recompute these actual
S5 maximum ranges; they must not substitute the much wider V2 range table even
though the wall-clock alignment and candidate-stability artifact structure are
shared.

Confirmed contact quality is versioned as five independent values:
`q_z/q_pose/q_vxy/q_omega/q_offset`, with sigmas `0.010 m/2 deg/0.05 m s^-1/
0.50 rad s^-1/0.020 m` and weights `0.30/0.25/0.20/0.15/0.10`. S1--S2 use
their weighted mean; S3--S5 use `0.8*mean + 0.2*min`. Flight quality has a
30 mm score around the bounded per-bounce next-XY target and a 20 mm score
around the `1.40 m` apex; it combines them as
`0.8*(0.55*q_trajectory+0.45*q_apex)+0.2*min(q_trajectory,q_apex)`. A centered
ball is rewarded for zero horizontal displacement; an off-center ball is
rewarded for a step of at most 5 cm toward center. `rel_height_bonus_weight`
is zero. All five contact-quality
components are logged separately and must be checked separately in promotion
evidence; aggregate reward cannot compensate for a failed component. The
`q_pose` component and S0 pose term are target-relative: they compare the
actual racket orientation with the dynamic target computed from the latest
direct observation or explicit high-ball extrapolation available before the
contact interval, not with a
constant horizontal reference. The `3 deg` target-tilt bound plus the `2 deg`
quality scale remains inside the registered `5 deg` absolute-orientation tail.
The rolling S1--S5 gate requires every component to reach 0.40 in each bridge and
`exp(-0.5)` in commit/consolidation. S0 separately gates the final-window
tracking/pose/motion product at `0.20/0.40/0.40`. These mean-score gates are
training safeguards; final promotion still requires the registered raw-value
tail thresholds.

S5's external predictor is the simulation port of the optimized real runtime
contract: nine fresh 90 Hz position frames, four Huber-IRLS refinements for XY
and gravity-compensated Z, upward/top-view activation, quadratic-drag
propagation at 5 ms, 0.50 s maximum horizon, 1.24 m stop height, 0.12 m
reacquisition gate, segment reset after a valid handover, and fail-safe invalid
state after expiration or rejected late handover. A propagated internal state
represents the current query time only for computing the separately encoded
future contact state; it never overwrites the actor's latest-direct-sample
current ball slots. Time to future contact is not re-labelled as stale
measurement age. Racket contact also clears the fit
history so one trajectory segment can never span the impact discontinuity.
S5 bridge samples an effective optical top edge in `[1.43,1.45] m`; commit and
consolidation use `[1.40,1.45] m`. The registered `1.45 m` bound remains the
hard outer envelope; the inward edge is candidate observation-domain
randomization that guarantees predictor handover exposure near the nominal
`1.40 m` apex, not a claim about a newly measured physical FOV.

The registered hard bounds are ball-anchor-relative X/Y
`[-0.30,0.50]/[-0.25,0.20] m`, absolute ball Z `[0.98,1.50] m`, view X/Y/Z
`[-0.35,0.35]/[-0.70,-0.28]/[1.00,1.45] m`, camera depth `[0.35,0.90] m`,
and racket X/Y/Z `[-0.348,0.348]/[-0.70,-0.28]/[1.002,1.120] m`. Time limit is
truncation; workspace, joint, bounded-reference, RMP, non-finite and predictor
fail-safe violations are task failures.

The fixed-contact reward path replaces the inherited dense/event reward rather
than adding to it. Its only positive credits are confirmed hit, the five-part
contact quality, bounded-trajectory/apex flight quality and the small
post-first-hit survival term; S0 instead uses crossing-target potential and
final-window braking. In particular, inherited full-episode completion and
joint-height terminal credits are explicitly zero, as are the historical
relative-height and stacked apex/cadence objectives. Every stage includes the
physical seven-joint QVEL hard clip and the time-scaled action-delta cost with
weight `0.0015`.

The nominal contact ball-center height is `1.095 m`; the `1.40 m` apex therefore
has lift `0.305 m` and an equal-height ballistic period
`2*sqrt(2*0.305/9.8)=0.4990 s`. A 1200-step episode at 5 ms is 6 s, and a
representative first contact at 0.22 s permits 12 contacts. The reward/combo
configuration is bounded at 12, but the fixed reward deliberately sets the
legacy count-growing `hit_reward_combo` to zero: only the first 12 valid hit
events receive the fixed hit/quality/flight event credit, while survival
credit remains active afterward. The physical count debounce is 0.30 s, and
multi-hit stages gate counted intervals in `[0.44,0.56] s` plus mean predicted
apex in `[1.38,1.42] m`. S0 validation no longer requires an impossible hit while
collision is disabled. S0/S1/S2 do not use episode length as a lower success
bound because S0 ends with its deliberate falling ball and S1/S2 terminate on
the first successful hit. A single-hit success is explicitly removed from the
remaining-horizon failure-penalty mask.

The launcher requires the hashed, passing `recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2` output
replay, the registered 4 g mass attestation, GPU0 UUID and manual
`CONFIRM_GPU0_READY=YES`. By explicit user decision on 2026-09-04, this
simulation experiment reuses the previous RMP/PD parameters and small S5
execution DR without coupling its start to the combined RMP/ball-outcome
coverage manifest. It therefore requires the explicit
`ACKNOWLEDGE_INCOMPLETE_RMP_DR_EVIDENCE=YES` experimental bypass. This does
not turn the missing exact-profile pointwise RMP/PD evidence, three diameter
measurements or at least 30 hashed physical new-ball outcome trials into a
pass. Predictor fixed-input sim/runtime parity, those physical evidence items,
S0--S2 fixed-seed training, equal-bin validation, S3--S5 multi-seed evidence
and supervised hardware gates remain outstanding. Do not call this profile
released, deployable, converged, or hardware-covering.

Formal PPO is pinned to GPU0 MJX with 1024 parallel environments, 128 steps per
rollout, minibatch 16384, four epochs, LR `3e-4`, clip `0.2`, target KL `0.012`,
gamma `0.9995`, GAE `0.99`, 256-wide two-layer actor/critic networks and no
stage-update cap. The rolling checkpoint interval is 10 updates and the archive
interval is 100 updates. The first simulation-only run started from scratch on
2026-09-04 in tmux `pp_gpu0`, physical GPU0, seed `20260903`, output directory
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v1_gpu0_seed20260903_20260904`,
and W&B online run `w48bqk6e`. After the 16-environment one-update GPU smoke
passed, the 1024-environment run completed its first four S0 updates without a
numeric safety stop and reached global step `524288` at about 42k steps/s after
JIT warmup.

## GPU0 Fixed-Contact-Plane Vision-Robust QVEL/RMP V2

Profile `fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v2` is the from-scratch
repair successor to V1. Its only launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v2.sh`.
V1 is preserved because its 2026-09-04 W&B run `w48bqk6e` and checkpoints make
its observation, reward, geometry and termination semantics historical. V2
keeps V1's exact 80-D actor, 401-D privileged critic, measured bounded-QVEL ->
`recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2` control boundary, V33 contact, 4 g ball contract,
S1--S5 physics/DR/reward domains and from-scratch/no-resume checks.

The user stopped V1 after 9,427 updates, all in `s0_tracking_bridge`. Its first
row had mean return/length `-6.730/46.79`, unconditional no-hit miss reward
`-0.1165` per sampled step and a nearly zero multiplicative brake score. At
update 9,427 mean length was still `48.10`, the brake-score sum was
`2.9e-12`, entropy had collapsed to `-17.92`, and
`done/racket_z_out_of_bounds` was `0.02087` per step while the associated
racket-limit terminal penalty remained zero. The failure was structural:

- collision-disabled S0 could never generate the hit required to avoid V1's
  inherited no-hit miss penalty;
- fixed X/Y/Z workspace done terms were absent from the racket-limit terminal
  penalty mask, so early workspace exit was a free way to avoid the later miss;
- five tracking/braking scores were multiplied, so one poor component erased
  the gradient from every otherwise useful component;
- V1 used `geom_size[1]` (the 75 mm in-plane radius) as surface-normal half
  thickness instead of `geom_size[0]` (1 mm), shifting represented racket
  surface state and target errors by 74 mm;
- the random-init bridge immediately exposed a displaced XY grid instead of
  first teaching a reachable settled pose.

V2 fixes all five without weakening the success gates. Fixed workspace X/Y/Z
terminations use the registered racket-limit terminal penalty; collision-off S0
requires a prior hit before any no-hit miss penalty can apply; and surface
position uses size axis 0. S0 reward is additive and logged component by
component. Before the final 80 ms it includes signed XY progress
`20*(e_xy_previous-e_xy_current)`. That term is exactly zero in the final
braking window. The bounded absolute terms are:

| component | weight | reward sigma | gate sigma |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| XY position | 4.00 | 0.060 m | 0.040 m |
| surface Z | 0.50 | 0.040 m | 0.020 m |
| target-relative pose | 0.75 | 10 deg | 5 deg |
| final-window racket vxy | 1.25 | 0.250 m/s | 0.120 m/s |
| final-window full omega | 0.75 | 1.50 rad/s | 1.00 rad/s |

Every absolute term is `weight*exp(-0.5*(error/sigma)^2)*dt`; vxy and omega
are active only in the final window. The seven-joint physical QVEL clip and
time-scaled action-delta penalty remain active in every stage. S0 rolling gates
independently require `(XY,Z,pose,vxy,omega)` scores of
`(0.35,0.55,0.45,0.35,0.35)`, then
`(0.55,0.65,0.55,0.50,0.50)`, then
`(0.65,0.75,0.65,0.60,0.60)`; one strong component cannot compensate for a
failed one.

The repaired S0 task-space ladder is warm-reset neighbourhood -> registered
center -> full workspace. Bridge uses the fixed center-relative offset
`(-0.10,+0.03) m`, no bin sampling and no jitter. Commit uses exactly the
registered `(0,0)` offset. Consolidation restores the complete
`[-0.30,+0.30] x [-0.18,+0.18] m` offset support, 0.35 center probability and
15 mm jitter; its later block validation still removes the center prior/jitter
and evaluates the full registered grid. Thus the formal juggling course still
contains a full-domain gate; only the random-init ordering changed.

Same-seed 256-environment bounded trials isolated the reward changes. Trial A
proved that additive absolute terms learned Z/pose/braking but left rolling XY
at `0.128`. Trial B enabled unmasked progress and raised XY to `0.268` while
collapsing final vxy to `0.053`. Trial C disabled progress in the final 80 ms;
vxy recovered to `0.582` but XY remained `0.176`. Trials D--F tightened and
reweighted only the failed XY objective and showed that direct center/grid
starts still plateaued short of target. Trial G introduced the reachable
bridge: it advanced normally at update 45 with rolling five-component scores
`0.967/0.849/0.585/0.519/0.529`, mean tracking error `8.6 mm`, zero workspace
termination, KL `0.00583` and explained variance `0.991`. After transfer to
center commit, 26 more updates moved racket X from about `-0.104` toward
`-0.086 m`; commit had not yet passed when the bounded diagnostic was stopped.
Negative trials and their CSV/checkpoints remain under
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_v2_s0_trial_[a-g]_gpu0_seed20260904_20260904`.

Formal V2 uses GPU0 MJX, 1024 environments, 128 steps, minibatch 16384, four
epochs, LR `3e-4`, clip `0.2`, target KL `0.012`, entropy coefficient `0.001`,
minimum log standard deviation `-4.0`, gamma `0.9995`, GAE `0.99`, no stage
update cap, block validation, rolling save every 20 updates and archive every
200. The larger entropy floor replaces V1's collapsed `0.0002/-4.8` setting;
all bounded V2 trials retained finite entropy, KL and critic statistics. V2
retains the explicit experimental RMP-evidence bypass and remains
simulation-only, unreleased and non-deployable.

The formal V2 run started from scratch on 2026-09-04 in tmux `pp_gpu0`, with
seed `20260904`, physical GPU0/JAX CUDA device 0, output directory
`outputs/rl_sim/fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v2_gpu0_seed20260904_20260904`
and W&B online run `vyimum7j`. Stage 1 advanced normally at update 41/global
step `5373952`: its rolling `(XY,Z,pose,vxy,omega)` scores were approximately
`0.979/0.795/0.848/0.610/0.665`, workspace termination and workspace terminal
penalty were both zero, KL was `0.00381`, and explained variance was `0.995`.
Stage 2 compiled successfully and completed its first two updates at about 42k
steps/s after JIT warmup. This is launch/progression evidence only; the run is
still active and is not evidence that S0 commit or the complete course has
converged.

Formal V48 was started in tmux `pp_gpu0` on 2026-08-24/25 with explicit seed
`20260829` and output directory
`outputs/rl_sim/measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v48_gpu0_seed20260829_20260824_transactional_resume_v39_best95`.
W&B `9acnp70r` resumed with the registered offset. The process-local paired
baseline was length/full `0.92795/0.89453`. At the first update-8 boundary the
candidate reached `0.94257/0.92188`, with full-lane transitions `+11/-4`, zero
secondary/safety gap regressions, qvel exceedance `0`, and qacc exceedance
`0.004428`; actor, critic and Adam were committed. The user authorized a safe
stop on 2026-08-25 after attempted update 107. The complete boundary record
was:

| boundary | incumbent -> candidate length/full | lane +/− | decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | `0.92795/0.89453 -> 0.94257/0.92188` | `+11/-4` | accept |
| 16--72 | incumbent `0.94257/0.92188`; seven candidates | each net negative | reject x7 |
| 80 | `0.94257/0.92188 -> 0.94390/0.92188` | `+5/-5` | accept |
| 88--104 | incumbent `0.94390/0.92188`; three candidates | each net negative | reject x3 |

Thus only two of 13 complete transactions committed. Every boundary retained

`f7ee8ca8dd48347b8c8eb1c96a7b8a02223d329db5b1038f092f3e5a8ad0be07`.
This proves rollback integrity but rejects transactional promotion as the

## Normal Continuous Long-Trend Continuation V49

Profile `goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v49` is the current successor.
Canonical launcher:
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v49_resume_v48.sh`.
It resumes only the V48 accepted update-80 checkpoint above, preserving actor,
critic and complete Adam state while starting a fresh convergence window at
`rmp49_normal_long_trend_polish`. The source profile, stage, true step,
dimensions, ball-mass interval and SHA are fail-closed. Curriculum-history
resume, reset/migration, another source, transaction mode and V46/V47 outcome
weighting are prohibited.

V49 changes only update promotion: the frozen-lane transaction guard is off,
so every numerically valid PPO update feeds the next rollout. The 28-stage
environment is otherwise value-for-value V39/V48: identical reward terms,
graduation gates, bounded q_ref and recovered RMP/PD path, observations,
physics, resets, all non-execution/execution DR ranges and small-before-wide
DR ordering. PPO is also unchanged:

```text
n_envs / n_steps       1024 / 128
minibatch / epochs     16384 / 3
learning rate          1e-4
clip / target KL       0.15 / 0.010
entropy                0.0002
gamma / GAE lambda     0.9995 / 0.99
stage update cap       none
trend window           24 committed normal updates
```

Normal training permits short-term `conv_len/full` regression while learning
hard DR cases. This does not disable quality or safety enforcement: the
ordinary strict rolling gates and 128-lane block validation still control
graduation, and qvel/qacc, view, apex, contact and motion-quality metrics
remain logged and gated. Judge the experiment from sustained 24-update and
longer trends, not individual points and not an expectation of monotonic
updates. No reward, DR or PPO scan should be introduced before this long run
has enough history.

## Joint Absolute-Apex/Flight-Lift Repair V56

Status (2026-08-25): bounded GPU0 reward trial completed; rejected for
insufficient height movement.

Profile `goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v56` is launched only by
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v56_resume_v55_u241.sh`.
It resumes exactly the stopped V55 update-241 checkpoint and preserves its
57-D actor, 368-D complete-DR critic, Adam moments and true optimizer step.
Another profile/stage/step/hash, curriculum-history resume, optimizer or
critic reset, observation migration, transactional promotion and advantage
reweighting fail closed. V56 starts a fresh convergence window at
`rmp56_joint_apex_lift_repair_nominal_execution`.

The V55 Stage-1 attribution found 124 logged reward channels: total and dense
aggregates plus 122 component terms. Of those terms, 87 were identically zero
and 35 were active in this domain. Sparse
positive hit credit was correctly capped at 14, but the inherited height
contract had no effective lower correction: `low_hit_penalty_weight=0`, while
the 1.32 m `hit_height_penalty` admitted a broad 1.25--1.39 m deadband. The
absolute-apex and lift targets each had weight 0.75. Full 15+ episodes could
therefore gain dense alive/survival, compact-path and view/motion-quality
credit while accepting only a small absolute-apex loss. In the frozen V54
source population, full 15+ episodes exceeded full 14-hit return by about
2.29 despite lower apex; the largest favorable terms were dense reward
`+2.91`, including post-first-hit alive `+1.66` and post-hit survival `+0.49`.
The absolute-apex target opposed the behavior by only `-0.70`. Across full
episodes, absolute apex and hit count correlated `-0.44`.

V56 does not optimize absolute height alone. It jointly defines:

| physical quantity | V55 | V56 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| absolute world-z apex target | 1.32 m | 1.32 m |
| absolute target weight / sigma | 0.75 / 0.050 m | 2.5 / 0.040 m |
| one-sided absolute lower edge / weight | inactive | 1.28 m / 2500 m^-2 |
| contact-to-apex lift target | 0.175 m | 0.195 m |
| lift target weight / sigma | 0.75 / 0.040 m | 2.5 / 0.025 m |
| lift barrier interval / weight | 0.130--0.220 m / 100 | 0.175--0.215 m / 1000 |
| counted cadence target / weight | inactive | 0.390 s / 0.5 |
| ball/racket contact-z soft limits | 1.18/10.0 m | 1.18/1.16 m |
| ball/racket contact-z weights | 400/0 | 400/400 |

The two target heights imply a contact ball height of
`1.32 - 0.195 = 1.125 m`, close to the stopped source's measured 1.121 m.
Thus the policy cannot satisfy absolute apex merely by raising the whole
juggling location. A 0.195 m ballistic lift corresponds to about 0.40 s per
cycle, aligning the physical flight with 13--15 contacts over 1200 steps.
The positive hit-event cap remains 14, and no maximum-hit termination or hard
maximum-hit graduation gate is introduced.

All 28 V55 stages and their corrected execution-DR order remain present.
Control, observation, reset, physics, ball/contact DR, RMP/PD values, PPO and
all non-height reward fields are preserved. Only the three height gates are
tightened: minimum absolute apex 1.29 m and lift interval 0.175--0.215 m;
ball/racket contact-height gates remain 1.18/1.16 m. The preregistered bounded
trial uses 1024 environments for 32 updates, one stage, seed `20260919`, W&B
offline and a unique output directory. It must improve both absolute apex and
lift without raising contact height, while protecting full/length, 13--15
hits, cadence, view, racket motion, qvel/qacc, KL and failure distribution.
Return alone cannot select it.

The 32-update trial did not meet the physical-height acceptance threshold.
On a paired seed-`20260920`, 256-lane frozen screen, V56 update 32 versus the
V55 source changed absolute apex by `+0.00190 +/- 0.00084 m`, lift by
`+0.00299 +/- 0.00058 m`, and contact ball height by
`-0.00109 +/- 0.00057 m`. Full rate improved `0.91797 -> 0.92969` and mean
length changed `1128.3 -> 1133.4`, so the direction was safe and did not use
an upward contact-location shortcut. It nevertheless finished at only about
`1.2771 m` absolute apex and `0.1561 m` lift, far below the preregistered
`1.29/0.175 m` thresholds. Do not launch V56 formally or resume its trial
actor. Preserve it as evidence that the coherent height reward is correctly
directed but insufficient under the inherited low-exploration PPO contract.

V56 is experimental, simulation-only and non-deployable and inherits every
unresolved real-camera, replacement-ball and formal RMP/PD coverage blocker.

## Height-Escape PPO Trial V57

Status (2026-08-25): bounded GPU0 optimization trial completed; insufficient
height for formal promotion.

Profile `goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v57` is launched only by
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v57_resume_v55_u241.sh`.
It restarts from the same stopped V55 update-241 checkpoint and must not
inherit the rejected V56 actor. V57 copies every one of V56's 28 environment,
reward, gate, curriculum and DR values exactly. The only changed contract is
the PPO height-escape preset: learning rate `1.5e-4`, clip `0.20`, target KL
`0.012`, entropy coefficient `0.001`, and minimum log standard deviation
`-4.0`; rollout length remains 128, epochs remain three, gamma remains
`0.9995`, and GAE lambda remains `0.99`.

This experiment tests an observed optimization blocker, not a new reward
hypothesis. V55/V56 policy log standard deviations had three dimensions at or
within numerical tolerance of the `-4.8` floor, and V56's physical improvement
stalled after update 20 even though all four new height reward components
improved in paired attribution. The 64-update offline trial must move absolute
apex and lift together to at least `1.29/0.175 m`, retain contact ball/racket
heights below `1.18/1.16 m`, keep hits in the intended 13--15 range, and avoid
material full/length, view, motion, qvel/qacc, KL or failure-distribution
regression. A higher stochastic return or policy entropy is not acceptance.

The 64-update trial remained below the `1.29/0.175 m` acceptance threshold,
so V57 may not be launched formally. It nevertheless produced a materially
better platform. On paired seed-`20260922`, 128-lane frozen evaluation, the
last policy achieved hits/full/length `14.969/0.97656/1177.4`; absolute
apex/lift/contact ball z were `1.28375/0.16212/1.12163 m`. Versus V55, apex
and lift changed `+8.30/+7.60 mm` while contact changed only `+0.69 mm`.
Thus exploration improved survival and both intended height coordinates
without primarily shifting contact height, but event-only lift learning was
too slow. V58 selects the complete update-60 archive rather than the
metadata-poor update-64 last file. V57 remains experimental, simulation-only
and non-deployable and inherits every unresolved real-camera,
replacement-ball and formal RMP/PD coverage blocker.

## Short-Horizon Joint Apex/Lift Credit V58

Status (2026-08-25): rejected bounded GPU0 reward-timing trial.

Profile `goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v58` is launched only by
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v58_resume_v57_u60.sh`.
It resumes the V57 update-60 archive at true step `2233991168`, SHA-256
`0880235d472e8c599f2711707f148409a99251600f8bd15fc9a3ed97d932c8a2`,
with actor, 368-D critic, Adam moments and optimizer time intact. It starts a
fresh V58 convergence window. Another source/profile/stage/step/hash,
curriculum-history resume, optimizer/critic reset or observation migration
fails closed.

V58 changes one reward component only. During the first `0.080 s` after each
of the first 14 counted contacts, while the ball is ascending, it adds a
weight-40 dense term:

`joint_score = absolute_apex_target_score * contact_to_apex_lift_target_score`

The absolute score retains target/sigma `1.32/0.040 m`; the lift score retains
target/sigma `0.195/0.025 m`. A product is used deliberately: raising apex and
contact together retains lift but loses absolute score, while attaining lift
at a low world height loses absolute score. Hits 15+ receive no joint credit.
The existing contact-edge ball/racket height penalties and limits remain
active. Every other V57/V56 reward, gate, environment, control, observation,
physics, DR, curriculum-order and PPO value is unchanged.

The 48-update trial was rejected. In paired 128-lane seed-`20260924` frozen
evaluation, V57-u60 achieved hits/full/length `15.289/0.97656/1177.7` and
absolute apex/lift/contact ball z `1.28233/0.15818/1.12415 m`; V58-u48
achieved `14.508/0.92188/1131.0` and `1.29462/0.16559/1.12903 m`. Thus the
dense credit raised absolute apex, but physical lift still missed 0.175 m,
contact rose 4.88 mm, and full rate regressed 5.47 percentage points. Do not
launch V58 formally or resume its actor. V58 remains experimental,
simulation-only and non-deployable.

## Completion-Conditioned Physical Objective V60

Status (2026-08-25): rejected bounded GPU0 objective-alignment trial.

Profile `goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v60` is launched only by
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v60_resume_v57_u60.sh`.
It restarts from the same complete V57 update-60 archive at true step
`2233991168`, SHA-256
`0880235d472e8c599f2711707f148409a99251600f8bd15fc9a3ed97d932c8a2`.
It preserves actor, 368-D critic and Adam state, starts a fresh convergence
window, and rejects V58/V59 sources, curriculum-history resume, state resets,
observation migration or a mismatched profile/stage/step/hash.

V60 copies V57, not the rejected V58/V59 actors or rewards. It adds one
weight-120 terminal component at the true 1200-step truncation. Credit is
zero unless total counted hits are 13--15. For eligible full episodes:

`completion_score = mean_abs_apex_score(first 14) * mean_lift_score(first 14)`

More precisely, the two Gaussian scores are evaluated on the first 14
rewardable contacts' episode means, with target/sigma `1.32/0.040 m` for
absolute world-z apex and `0.195/0.025 m` for contact-to-apex lift, then
multiplied. Hits 15+ never enter those means; 16+ total hits receive zero
terminal credit. Raising contact and apex together cannot improve lift score,
and obtaining either physical coordinate without the other cannot maximize
the product.

Every V57 dense/event term—including the weight-6 up-drift penalty—alive and
survival rewards, contact-height barriers, PPO, gates, control, observations,
physics, all 28 stages, Stage-1 nominal execution, Stage-20 polish and
Stage-21 execution-DR widening are unchanged. The default 48-update trial
uses seed `20260927`, W&B offline and a unique directory. Frozen acceptance
requires abs/lift `>=1.29/0.175 m`, safe contact height, 13--15 hits and no
material longevity, view, motion, qvel/qacc, KL or failure regression. Only a
passing screen would have permitted no-cap V60 launch in `pp_gpu0`. The trial
was rejected. Paired seed-`20260928` frozen evaluation held full at `0.92188`
and improved length by 9.5 steps, but V60-u48 versus V57-u60 changed
abs/lift/contact by `+10.40/+4.34/+6.06 mm`, ending at
`1.29399/0.16639/1.12760 m`. The terminal term protected longevity but did
not supply enough local lift credit. Do not launch V60 formally or resume its
actor.

## Direct Reflected-Velocity Continuation V61

Status (2026-08-25): preregistered bounded GPU0 local-credit trial.

Profile `goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v61` is launched only by
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v61_resume_v57_u60.sh`.
It restarts from the exact V57 update-60 checkpoint/hash registered for V58
and does not inherit V58, V59 or V60 actors. It retains V60's terminal
completion-conditioned physical objective, then enables the existing
paper-derived pseudo-Huber adaptive reflected-velocity penalty with weight 5,
vertical sigma `0.20 m/s`, and XY sigma `100 m/s`. The large XY sigma makes
the added gradient effectively vertical-only.

For each of the first 14 rewardable contacts, the desired outgoing vertical
velocity is computed from the hit position, gravity and the 1.32 m absolute
apex target. Unlike apex-only outcome credit, it acts at the contact that
caused the flight. V57's absolute-apex and physical-lift targets plus V60's
full/13--15/product term remain active, so satisfying only outgoing velocity,
raising contact height, or failing early cannot maximize the combined reward.
All other rewards, gates, PPO, control, observations, physics, 28 stages and
nominal-small-then-wide DR order remain unchanged.

V61 was stopped at update 17 before a frozen selection screen. Its late
training points stayed near absolute apex/lift `1.284/0.160--0.161 m` with
full near `0.90--0.92`; they did not establish the required direction.
Formula inspection then found that the existing adaptive target computes
desired vertical velocity from delayed confirmation `bpos`, while V25+
physical lift uses cached contact-edge height. Enabling that term before its
coordinate contract was resolved was not justified. V61 is rejected and
incomplete: do not launch it formally, resume its actor or treat it as a
completed causal ablation.

`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v65_cmdp_resume_v29_stage21.sh`.
It resumes the pinned V29 Stage-21 checkpoint at true step `2087190528`,
SHA-256 `8fb721d1a620f7c229676d6381df2a3e86495c9f589f3dd4e64e9f926cd8ed41`.
Stage `rmp65_v29_stage21_cmdp_survival` differs from V29 Stage 21 only in name
and notes. The 57-D actor, 221-D reward critic, environment reward, gates,
control, physics, reset distribution, ball/contact DR and all PPO values are
unchanged.

V65 changes the optimization state explicitly. It appends a zero-output
six-channel cost critic and zero Adam leaves while preserving every source
actor/reward-critic parameter, Adam moment and Adam time. Its undiscounted
episodic costs and upper bounds are:

| cost | episode value | bound |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| failure | `1[true termination]` | `0.07` |
| shortfall | `1[true termination] * (1200-T)/1200` | `65/1200` |
| ball low/high | corresponding terminal indicator | `0.02` each |
| racket low/high | corresponding terminal indicator | `0.02` each |

Each channel has an independent cost value estimate. Cost GAE uses gamma
`1.0`, lambda `0.99`; the cost-value coefficient is `0.5`. The actor advantage
is the normalized reward advantage minus projected nonnegative duals times
independently normalized cost advantages, followed by a final normalization.
Duals initialize at `[0.25,0.25,0.10,0.10,0.10,0.10]`, update at rate `0.1`
from completed-episode empirical costs and are clipped to `[0,2]`. They and
all cost-head optimizer state are checkpointed and logged. Direction-specific
channels prevent satisfying aggregate survival by merely exchanging high and
low terminal modes.

The CMDP path is default-off and restricted to V65. V65 prohibits reward,
PPO, observation, transaction-guard and legacy advantage-focus changes. It
also keeps the V31 seven-field internal-RMP widening out of scope. A CUDA
GPU0 smoke with 16 environments and one update completed successfully at
`outputs/rl_sim/v65_cmdp_20260825/smoke_gpu0_n16_u1_escalated/`; it verified
57/221/7 dimensions, cost-head/dual checkpoint persistence, preserved Adam
time and scalar CMDP telemetry. The smoke is compilation evidence only, not
policy evidence.

The preregistered bounded run uses 1024 environments, rollout 128, minibatch
16384, three epochs, seed `20260936`, at most 32 updates and W&B offline with
a new identity. Frozen deterministic first-episode screens use seeds
`20260932` and `20260933`. A checkpoint may proceed to no-cap `pp_gpu0`
training only if mean/worst full reach `0.93/0.90`, mean/worst length reach
`1135/1110`, mean hits remain 13--15, at least `0.55` of full episodes have
13--15 hits, absolute apex is at least `1.29 m`, lift at least `0.165 m`, view
at least `0.96`, qvel exceedance zero and qacc exceedance at most `0.01`.
Failure preserves the result and blocks formal launch.

The exact V29 Stage-21 screens retained the source's 15% camera/view missing
probabilities. Update 10 was the least-regressed V65 candidate, with
mean/worst full `0.8945/0.8906`, mean/worst length `1115.0/1113.6`, mean hits
`13.953`, full 13--15 fraction `0.6070`, view `0.9640` and absolute apex/lift
`1.2956/0.1683 m`. It fails mean/worst full and mean length. The source was
`0.8945/0.8828` full and `1111.2/1110.5` length; therefore update 10 improved
only the worst seed and length slightly, not aggregate survival. Update 30
regressed to `0.8750/0.8672` full, and no later checkpoint passed.

The 256 paired source episodes ended ball-low/racket-high `8/12` times;
update 10 changed these to `11/9`, so V65 exchanged height-failure direction
rather than satisfying the aggregate failure constraint. Training remained
numerically healthy (reward-critic EV `0.899`, exact KL mean `0.00658`, qvel
exceedance zero, qacc exceedance about `0.00508`), but cost-critic EV after
warmup stayed near zero: failure `-0.0048`, shortfall `-0.0020`, ball-low
`0.0067`, ball-high `-0.0365`, racket-low `-0.0054`, racket-high `0.0428`.
Failure/shortfall duals rose to `0.448/0.370` without producing calibrated
long-horizon risk advantages.

The complete report and hashed exact/zero-missing evidence are at
`outputs/rl_sim/v65_cmdp_20260825/V65_CMDP_BOUNDED_VALIDATION_REPORT.md`.
The zero-missing screens are an ablation, not zero configuration distance;
never substitute them for the 15% missing V29 contract. A future monotonic
successor should pretrain cost values from complete frozen-episode labels and
pass held-out risk calibration before actor training. Increasing terminal
reward/dual weight or merely running V65 longer is not authorized by this
result.

## V29 Stage-21 Bimodal-Failure Causal Diagnostic

Status (2026-08-25): completed frozen GPU0 diagnosis. This is evidence, not a
V66 curriculum profile. CMDP remains disabled; do not resume V65 or start a
formal `pp_gpu0` training run from this diagnostic.

The frozen actor and environment are the V29 Stage-21 checkpoint at true step
`2087190528`, SHA-256
`8fb721d1a620f7c229676d6381df2a3e86495c9f589f3dd4e64e9f926cd8ed41`.
Seeds `20260932/20260933` supplied 128 first episodes each. The full-DR
baseline was strongly bimodal: 227/256 episodes reached 1200 steps, while 29
failures averaged 395.9 steps and none occupied steps 1000--1199. Terminations
were ball-low/racket-high/racket-low/ball-X/ball-Y `13/11/3/1/1`.

Exact same-graph re-execution proved that failure identities are not fixed.
Across the baseline plus three repeats, 205 lanes were always full, 14 always
failed and 37 changed outcome. Aggregate exact-replay full was `0.89063`.
Changing only temporal RNG averaged `0.88281`; four stochastic-action repeats
averaged `0.88574`. Gaussian exploration has no consistent net effect and is
not the primary platform cause. Long MJX contact rollouts amplify tiny
numerical and sensing perturbations near a closed-loop separatrix, so one
deterministic lane result must not be treated as an immutable label.

Paired counterfactuals establish a DR-dependent robustness-margin problem:

| frozen counterfactual | full | length | fail->full / full->fail |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| V29 full DR | 0.88672 | 1108.91 | baseline |
| nominal ball/contact DR | 0.94531 | 1166.77 | 25 / 10 |
| nominal recovered-RMP/PD DR | 0.92969 | 1144.42 | 19 / 8 |
| nominal static observation/racket-mount DR | 0.93750 | 1144.30 | 20 / 7 |
| all episode-constant DR nominal | **1.00000** | **1200.00** | **29 / 0** |
| temporal sensing/missing/target-hold off | 0.94922 | 1154.45 | 21 / 5 |
| centered reset with full DR | 0.90625 | 1136.20 | 15 / 10 |

The joint nominal condition retains the target/reset support and per-step
randomness; mount nominalization necessarily changes the corresponding
physical contact geometry. Centering the reset did not outperform paired
branch-exchange noise. Therefore do not narrow reset/target support, call the
registered DR invalid, or claim an impossible physical population. Three
baseline lanes were persistently DR-sensitive in the limited repeats, but
their count of outer-five-percent DR features was no greater than expected
from the 117 inspected fields. They are hard combinations inside the current
support.

The failed-cycle trace supplies a proximal learning signal that V65 lacked.
At 3446 full-episode hits versus 26 failed-episode final hits, mean intercept
racket-XY error was `0.00886 -> 0.04928 m`; `92.3%` of failed final hits but
only `1.25%` of full hits exceeded the existing `0.025 m` intercept radius.
Contact-point racket VXY exceeded `0.25 m/s` in `61.5%` versus `13.7%`, action
norm exceeded `1.4` in `61.5%` versus `1.86%`, and racket-Z relative to anchor
exceeded `0.14 m` in `38.5%` versus `0.35%`. Median final-hit-to-termination
delay was 86 steps for ball-low and 69 for racket-high. Ball-low failures then
missed/underpowered the next contact; racket-high/low failures drifted
monotonically out of the vertical recovery region.

Do not repeat V45--V53 success anchoring, single-rollout hard indicators,
scalar completion rewards, fixed transactions, or V65 CMDP cost critics. A
future monotonically versioned bounded experiment must instead replicate each
episode-constant DR/reset tuple across independent temporal/action draws,
estimate tuple failure probability, stratify the ball/contact,
observation/mount and RMP/PD families before temporal randomness, and give
empirically hard tuple groups fixed episode-level sampling mass. A code audit
found that `pre_hit_intercept_*` is active only while `hit_count <= 0`, while
27/29 audited failures occur after the first hit. The isolated reward
candidate must therefore use the existing recurrent
`descending_intercept_excess_penalty` with a 0.025 m zero-loss radius; a
failed-contact event candidate must be separate. DR intervals, reset
support, PPO parameters and completion reward stay unchanged in either
ablation. Formal training remains blocked until a bounded repeated-pair screen
passes the complete 1200-step, full/length, 13--15 hit, apex/lift, view,
motion and safety contract.

The complete derivation, exact McNemar comparisons, hashes, lane
classifications, success/failure event table and sampled traces are under
`outputs/rl_sim/v66_bimodal_failure_analysis_20260825/`, with the primary
report `V29_BIMODAL_FAILURE_CAUSAL_REPORT.md`.

## GPU0 V78 Stage-13 Noisy-Observation Survival Repair

Status (2026-08-27): bounded validation accepted for formal GPU0 continuation. V77
was stopped safely after Stage-13 update `9194` / global update `9431`, true
step `3678666752`; W&B run `v72g0s7a1` synced successfully. The interrupted
checkpoint SHA-256 is
`9a9c673928835750ccf46c42f95a6e5deb1bea0fc03abf8393f0e7667c698fca`.
V77 did not have PPO/KL/value divergence: over more than 8000 Stage-13
updates, `conv_len` and full-episode rate oscillated near `0.927/0.863`, while
full racket angular speed remained near `1.48 rad/s` and next-contact anchor
error near `0.13 m`. The original strict joint gate was therefore not a
single survival threshold; its angular and anchor requirements had almost no
continuous overlap with the survival window.

Frozen first-episode-per-lane screens compared V77 Stage-13 updates 600, 750,
800, 5000, the legacy `best`, and the interrupted policy without resampling
fast failures. The selected parent is update 800, true step `2578448384`,
global update `1037`, Adam time `497258`, SHA-256
`c20a4b9178089f007aa8a9cd3401e56cd18484ee775786b3f4066dc517822629`.
Across two 128-lane seeds it produced hits `13.879`, `conv_len=0.9412` and
full rate `0.8867`; on the quality-instrumented seed it had full racket
angular speed `1.448 rad/s`, hit-racket VXY `0.096 m/s`, next-contact anchor
error `0.124 m`, zero qvel exceedance and qacc exceedance `0.00400`. It was
selected from this Pareto evidence, not return or the legacy best score.

Paired causal replay shows the residual failure population is real but not a
single unreachable DR corner. Ball/contact DR nominalization moved full rate
only about `0.883 -> 0.898`; RMP/PD nominalization moved it to `0.945`, and
observation/mount nominalization to `0.961`. Disabling only refresh-sample
ball-position/velocity noise, while retaining dropout, view-missing sampling,
target holds and all episode DR, completed all `128/128` episodes in the
registered two-seed screen. Disabling noise plus dropout gave `127/128` full
episodes. Target-hold-only results were mixed across paired lanes. Thus the
dominant tail is the 57-D feed-forward actor's sensitivity to per-refresh
ball-state noise, amplified by execution/observation DR; it is not exploration
noise or ball contact alone. These candidate noise bounds still lack the
paired real-camera audit required by the V16 contract and must not be called
hardware coverage.

Failure traces show the correct reward target is a local boundary precursor,
not a global height drift penalty. In failed trajectories, sampled
`racket_z_rel` exceeded `0.12 m` in `8.3%` of samples versus `1.9%` for full
episodes; during the last 100 steps its 90/95/99 percentiles were about

## GPU0 V81 Impossible Missing-Exposure Gate Repair

Formal V80 passed Stage 14 and Stage 15, then remained in Stage 16
`rmp80_nonexecution_inview_noise_support` for 4335 updates. This was not an
angular-reward failure. Stage 16 deliberately sets camera/view missing,
refresh dropout and burst dropout probabilities to zero, while it accidentally
inherits `min_ball_obs_missing_refresh_rate=0.006`. The measured refresh
missing rate was exactly zero in all 4335 rows, so the base convergence gate
was mathematically impossible and block validation was never called. Before
the resulting long overtraining tail, updates 169--229 passed every
policy-controlled gate for 61 consecutive updates. Update 200 rolling
hits/`conv_len`/full/angular/anchor were
`13.7029/0.93095/0.89164/1.41072/0.12596`; absolute apex/lift were
`1.29696/0.17217 m`, qvel exceedance was zero and qacc exceedance was
`0.00416`.

The opt-in successor is
`goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v81`. It copies all 32 V80 stages and
changes only the minimum missing-refresh exposure gate: the gate becomes
`None` exactly when every mechanism capable of making a refresh missing is
disabled. Active missing stages retain their exact V80 lower bound. This
repairs Stages 16--32, not only the current stage. Reward, angular target and
weight, anchor reward and guardrail, survival gates, height contract, DR,
observation noise, control, reset, PPO and validation settings remain
V80-identical. In particular, the dense full-angular penalty stays `0.50`,
the Stage-16 angular/anchor gates stay `1.43 rad/s` and `0.130 m`, and the
Stage-16 `conv_len/full` gates stay `0.90/0.82`. The historical pass proves
these actor-controlled values are attainable without weakening survival, so
neither the angular reward nor its gate is changed.

V81 resumes only a frozen V80 Stage-16 checkpoint; it never replays Stages
1--15 and starts a fresh Stage-16 convergence window because the V80 history
contains the impossible gate. The leading source is update 200, true step
`2662072320`, Adam time `506920`, SHA-256
`3efc653bfd82d2af0d6da9a7d72bdce8672d111006b008d7166da10307559e83`.
Its exact selection and fixed-seed screen are registered in
`outputs/rl_sim/v81_missing_gate_repair_20260828/PREREGISTERED_V81_GATE_REPAIR.md`.
The canonical launchers are
`run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v81_resume_v80_stage16_update200.sh` and

Formal shape remains 1024 environments, rollout 128, minibatch 16384, two
