## GPU0 V85 Stage-23/24 Failure-Time Survival Repair

The opt-in successor is
`goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v85`, launched only through
`run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v85_cgroup_resume_v83_stage23_update100.sh`.
It resumes the same exact V83 Stage-23 update-100 checkpoint and preserves
V84 stages, gates, domains, control, observations, physics, DR, PPO and every
other reward.  From Stage 23 onward it adds only:

```text
early_termination_remaining_horizon_penalty = 30
terminal event = -30 * (episode_limit - failure_step) / episode_limit
```

The event is zero on a normal 1200-step truncation.  Its 30-point bound is the
exact maximum full-horizon scale of the existing post-first-hit alive credit:
`5 reward/s * 0.005 s/step * 1200 steps = 30`.  V84's 40-point, >=13-hit
completion event remains responsible for `full`; the new event distinguishes
the failure-time distribution that determines `conv_len`.  Because the event
is emitted at the actual failure, finite-lambda GAE can assign it to the
preceding causal contact cycle instead of attempting to propagate a step-1200
event hundreds of steps backward.  This is a bounded objective-alignment
change, not CMDP, failure oversampling or an update-count workaround.

Promotion requires one bounded 512-env, at-most-64-update Stage-23 trial from
the pinned source.  The registered direction passes only if the 48-update
rolling survival window does not exhibit the V83/V84 joint decline, the late
window is not declining, and frozen paired replay shows no earlier-failure
shift while height, cadence, view, motion quality, qvel/qacc and PPO KL remain
valid.  If accepted, formal training uses 1024 environments, minibatch 16384,
W&B `v72g0s7a1` with `resume=must`, offset `1943011328`, no stage update cap,
and the 13/14 GiB zero-swap cgroup.  V85 remains experimental,
simulation-only and inherits every unresolved deployment evidence blocker.

The preregistered 64-update V85 bounded trial was accepted for direction.
All three post-warmup 16-update windows had positive within-window slopes for
both raw mean length and full rate; the full updates-17--64 slopes were
`+0.3296 steps/update` and `+0.000659/update`.  Final 48-update rolling metrics
were `conv_len=0.921758`, `full=0.866534`, hits `13.8121`, absolute apex
`1.292412 m`, lift `0.164653 m`, mean/RMS racket VXY
`0.107231/0.119998 m/s`, full angular speed `1.323304 rad/s`, qvel exceedance
zero, qacc exceedance `0.004293`, and mean exact KL `0.002119`.  This supports
the reward direction under the requested short experiment; it is not evidence
that future formal curves cannot oscillate.  Formal training must restart
from the pinned V83 source, not from the 512-env trial checkpoint.

## GPU0 V86 Stage-24 Monotone-Survival Transaction Repair

The opt-in successor is
`goal_d455_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v86`, launched only through
`run_gpu0_measured_qvel_rmp_vertical_v86_cgroup_resume_v85_stage23_pass.sh`.
It resumes V85's Stage-23 pass-boundary checkpoint at true step `2900099072`,
Adam time `529643`, SHA-256
`e48c5b50ebfea05df3cd44748eaa13094ce3f0409315a32b31d4914185c0383d`,
and starts a fresh Stage-24 window. V85's Stage-24 best/last checkpoints are
negative continuation evidence and are prohibited sources.

The complete 539-row V85 audit found that Stage 23's rolling
`conv_len/full` peaked at `0.926784/0.875329` and ended at
`0.922111/0.859691`. Stage 24 never approached its `0.95/0.90` gate and
ended at `0.902329/0.832832`; after its first full 48-update window, raw
length/full slopes were `-6.37858e-5/-3.63998e-5` per update. Stage-24
termination probability rose by `0.00772`, led by ball-view Y-low and X-high
failures, while hit-racket mean/RMS VXY rose by about `0.0043/0.0044 m/s`.
Exact KL stayed near `0.0027` below the `0.004` target, explained variance
rose, qvel exceedance was zero and qacc exceedance stayed near `0.0049`.
This is continued policy/optimizer drift on an unchanged domain, not PPO
explosion, a safety stop or a new DR boundary.

V86 preserves all 32 V85 stages and changes no environment, reward, gate,
control, observation, physics, DR or PPO field. Its only optimization-policy
change is mandatory atomic transaction promotion:

```text
candidate block                         = 16 PPO updates
paired evaluation                       = 256 deterministic first episodes
paired seed                             = 20261004
accepted while below Stage-24 gates     = combined survival gap strictly falls
individual conv_len/full gap increase   = prohibited
individual conv_len/full value decrease = prohibited, including above gates
secondary/safety gate-gap increase      = prohibited
qvel/qacc exceedance ceilings           = 0.0 / 0.01
commit unit                             = actor + critic + Adam moments
```

Rejected blocks restore the incumbent state and do not enter convergence
history, best-checkpoint ranking or periodic checkpoint state. Once both
primary metrics are in range, accepted incumbents must remain in range. This
makes survival lexicographically prior to return-shaping trades without
retuning the V85 reward or weakening Stage-24's `0.95/0.90` contract.

Promotion requires a separate offline 512-environment, minibatch-8192,
32-update trial from the pinned source. At least one transaction must be
accepted, every accepted incumbent must be componentwise non-regressing on
the paired survival population, and all secondary/safety gates must remain
non-worse. The formal run restarts the same source with 1024 environments,
minibatch 16384, LR `5e-5`, two epochs, clip `0.10`, target KL `0.004`, a
48-update convergence window, no stage cap, a new W&B ID/history and the
13/14 GiB zero-swap cgroup. V86 remains experimental and simulation-only.

`0.92969/0.87891 -> 0.92380/0.85938` and
`0.92969/0.87891 -> 0.93615/0.87500`. Independent trial 3 rejected

`0.94306/0.89844 -> 0.94323/0.89844` at update 32. The accepted candidate
had zero qvel exceedance, qacc exceedance `0.004870`, and no secondary gate
regression. The formal run must restart the pinned V85 checkpoint; neither
bounded trial is a formal resume source.

## GPU1 V132 Post-Hit Ball-Latency Bridge Continuation

V131 passed one-based Stage 38,
`record_new3_sim2real_v131_impact_full_no_spin_60hz_consolidate`, but its

remained healthy. The executable delta showed the cause was a task jump:
`dr_randomize_latency` sampled 0--2 steps once per reset and delayed the whole
base observation, including joint/base/racket/action-derived state, rather
than modeling intermittent ball-camera latency during juggling.

V132 preserves V131 Stages 1--38 exactly and replaces V131 Stages 39--40 with

support, i.e. 0/5/10 ms. Before the first hit the injected latency is always
zero. Only ball position, ball velocity, ball/racket relative position and
ball age are buffered; q/dq, base state, racket state and action feedback stay

| 43 | exact 60 Hz | 100% | 2.40 | latency consolidation |
| 44--45 | exact 90 Hz | 100% | 2.40 | direct 90 Hz adaptation/consolidation |
| 46--47 | exact 60 Hz | 100% | 2.40 | deployment-rate polish/consolidation |

## GPU1 V135 Timestamp-Consistent Ball-Latency Continuation

The opt-in successor is
`goal_d455_sport_taskspace_record_new3_sim2real_timestamp_latency_v135`,
launched only through
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_record_new3_v135_timestamp_latency_from_v132_stage41.sh`.
It resumes the same clean, naturally passed V132 Stage-41 boundary at true
step `10876059648`, Adam time `1053074`, SHA-256
`7778275b59e5e46dc177792015f75aec258237f00fa80ceafd87208b7ab937cd`.
It restores the 67-D actor, 279-D critic and all Adam moments, starts V135
Stage 42 with a fresh 16-update warm-up and convergence window, and rejects
curriculum-history resume, optimizer/critic reset, observation migration and
every bounded-trial checkpoint. V134 is not reintroduced.

V132/V133 selected delayed ball values from a buffer advanced at 200 Hz, but
labeled them with only the sampled 0/5/10 ms delay. At exact 60 Hz, a selected
buffer entry can belong to the preceding camera frame and continues aging
between refreshes. The actor therefore received a delayed position/velocity
whose `ball_obs_age` contradicted its acquisition time. Since the 67-D actor
has no separate injected-latency feature, that mismatch made the post-hit
state partially unobservable.

hits/length/full/view were `11.6649/0.8442/0.7437/0.9469` against
`11.5/0.90/0.65/0.96`. Mean/RMS hit VXY were `0.1775/0.2211 m/s`; maximum
exact KL was `0.001178`; explained variance was `0.9605`; qacc/qvel
exceedance was `0.00358/0.000096`; there were no PPO rollbacks or raw-action
clips. The final-48 length and view slopes were non-positive. The corrected
reaction/energy entry improved hits and view over V148 but did not remove the
survival/view ceiling, proving that the continuous five-axis bridge was only
a partial cause. Do not use its bounded actor as a source.

The formal V149 launcher,
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_record_new3_v149_reaction_energy_bridge_from_v146_u7345.sh`,
now fails closed before GPU or W&B access. W&B ID `v130g1r1` remains at its
stopped V146 history; no V148/V149 online point was written.

## GPU1 V150 Reset-Family Mixture Bridge

The current opt-in GPU1 repair is
`goal_d455_sport_taskspace_record_new3_sim2real_fixed_base_ball4g_reset_mixture_bridge_v150`.
V150 preserves V146 Stages 1--50 exactly, resumes only the immutable V146 last
checkpoint at true step `14688026624` and SHA-256
`2d7498c3769e42a1b254ed0472ba269e8418eaa50c3de951a6d6d1bdb085e6d4`,
and retains the 67-D actor, 279-D critic, actor/critic parameters, optimizer
time and Adam moments. Reward, gates, PPO, observation, fixed-base physics,
4.0 g nominal ball and measured `[0.0039,0.0041] kg` mass DR are unchanged.

The completed two-seed, 128-lane frozen V146 Stage-50 ablation isolates the
categorical reset transition as the root discontinuity. Main racket-launch
hits/length/full/view were `11.961/0.921/0.844/0.945` and
`13.008/0.952/0.883/0.946`. Changing only `ball_reset_mode` to
falling-contact reduced them to `2.430/0.242/0.125/0.498` and
`2.930/0.281/0.180/0.503`; qacc exceedance rose from about `0.0035` to
`0.0149/0.0178`. Adding V149's corrected reaction/energy trajectory improved
hits only to `3.617/4.336`. The complete V149 entry reached
`10.062/10.258` hits but view remained `0.874/0.852`; exact B2 measured only
`8.664/8.289` hits and `0.744/0.738` view. Contact-plane-only changes were
negligible, while B2 target geometry reduced hits further despite increasing
view. This rejects a missing/incorrect reward and PPO instability as the
primary cause and prohibits using extra view reward to mask lost juggling.

V150 adds the default-off reset mode
`racket_launch_falling_contact_mix`. It samples reset family independently per
episode/lane and logs `reset_falling_contact_active`; that state is not added
to actor or critic observations. Probability-zero and probability-one reset
outputs are regression-tested elementwise against the pure racket-launch and
pure falling-contact modes, including the falling racket-follow IK path. The
main lanes keep the exact V146 final target support and 1 mm racket surface
gap, while falling lanes keep the exact B2 target, trajectory, contact and
follow contracts.

Stages 51--59 use falling probabilities
`0.01,0.025,0.05,0.10,0.20,0.35,0.50,0.75,1.0`; Stage 60 is exact V146 B2.
Stages 61--63 interpolate only the five B2-to-B3 reset supports at fractions
0.25, 0.50 and 0.75; Stage 64 is exact V146 B3. Stages 65--66 repeat the
exact V146 final main-task environment and proof gate as retention and final
proof. The original B2/B3 rewards and graduation gates are retained at every
corresponding stage.

Both bounded and formal validation use 1024 deterministic lanes and
worst-reset-bucket gating. The binary reset-family metric is split directly,
so the roughly ten falling lanes at one percent cannot be hidden by aggregate
means or collapsed tercile boundaries. The bounded launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_record_new3_v150_stage51_mixture_probe_from_v146_u7345.sh`;
it runs only in `pp_gpu1`, uses 1024x128 samples, seed `82731`, LR `1e-5`,
offline W&B, at most 160 updates and the complete original B2 gate. Its
allowlisted `V150_PROBE_VARIANT` values are `p001` and the subsequent
sample-density diagnostic `p005`; no other stage can be selected. A failure
prohibits formal launch and preserves the negative output.

The completed `p001` probe is negative. Final-48 hits/length/full were
`12.1549/0.9186/0.8384`, mean/RMS hit-racket VXY were
`0.1642/0.2039 m/s`, exact KL was `0.000705`, explained variance was
`0.9667`, qacc/qvel exceedance was `0.00272/0.000056`, and there were no raw
action clips or PPO rollbacks. Thus the population-wide collapse was removed
without sacrificing aggregate juggling or survival. However view was only
`0.9395` against `0.96` with a negative final-48 slope. A 1024-lane frozen
paired replay in the exact one-percent mixed environment showed parent/last
main-lane hits `12.053/12.060`, but falling-lane hits
`10.000/9.462`, length `0.679/0.624`, view `0.766/0.757` and qacc exceedance
`0.00883/0.01418`. One-percent sampling therefore protected the aggregate by
making the new family too rare to learn; it is not accepted. The formal V150
launcher now fails closed before GPU or W&B access.

The `p005` bounded variant restarts the immutable V146 parent directly at the
five-percent stage. It is a sample-density ablation only: environment,
reward, gates, PPO and the 160-update protocol are unchanged. It must improve
the separately frozen falling lanes while retaining main-lane hits, survival,
view and safety; aggregate recovery alone is insufficient.

The completed `p005` result is also negative. Its final-48 aggregate
hits/length/full/view were `11.8427/0.9145/0.8321/0.9358`; exact KL was
`0.000660` (run maximum `0.001146`), explained variance was `0.9672`, qacc
exceedance was `0.00284`, and there were no raw-action clips or PPO rollbacks.
Thus aggregate juggling and survival remained strong. In the deterministic
1024-lane same-seed screen, however, the 49 falling lanes changed
parent-to-candidate hits `9.796 -> 9.327`, length `0.701 -> 0.695`, full rate
`0.592 -> 0.551`, view `0.820 -> 0.804`, and qacc exceedance
`0.00866 -> 0.00981`. Main-lane length/full improved, confirming that plain
population-mean PPO still spent most of its gradient on the dominant reset
family. Increasing exposure from one to five percent is therefore not the
repair, and the formal V150 launcher remains fail-closed.

After bounded acceptance and frozen main-domain non-regression only, formal
training uses
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_record_new3_v150_reset_mixture_bridge_from_v146_u7345.sh`.
It must restart from the immutable V146 parent, not the bounded actor, run
only in `pp_gpu1`, have no stage-update cap, and continue the explicitly
authorized online W&B ID `v130g1r1` with `resume=must` and metrics-only offset
`1849556992`. The first V150 point must be `16537714688`; V148/V149 wrote no
online points. V150 remains experimental simulation training and does not
claim that B2/B3 or collision outcomes cover hardware.

## GPU1 V151 Reset-Family Actor-Mass Repair

The preregistered successor is
`goal_d455_sport_taskspace_record_new3_sim2real_fixed_base_ball4g_reset_family_balanced_v151`.
It restarts the immutable V146 checkpoint directly at the five-percent mixed
reset stage; no V148--V150 actor is a source. V151 preserves the V150 reset
environments from probabilities `0.05,0.10,0.20,0.35,0.50,0.75,1.0`, exact
B2, three B2-to-B3 bridges, exact B3, main retention and the final exact V146
proof. The rejected one- and 2.5-percent stages are omitted, giving 64 total
stages with V146 Stages 1--50 unchanged.

V151's only optimization change is
`--reset-family-min-actor-mass 0.15`. If falling-reset rollout rows are
present but contribute less than 15% of the batch, their actor advantages are
weighted to 15% normalized sample mass and the main family is correspondingly
downweighted so mean sample weight remains one. Empty, pure and already
sufficient batches are exact no-ops. Critic returns/value loss remain
population-uniform; the family identity remains telemetry and is absent from
both actor and critic observations. V151 prohibits combining this mechanism
with failure/success focus, hard-lane focus, CMDP or the transactional guard.
Reward, control, observation, physics, contact, DR and all PPO optimizer
parameters are unchanged.

Recovery graduation is separated from deployed-task proof. Mixed/exact B2,
B2-to-B3, exact B3 and main-retention stages use the preregistered V147
evidence-calibrated recovery ceilings. The final stage retains the exact V146
main-task gate. This avoids asking an alternate real-data reset bucket to meet
a main-reset proof while still preventing loss of ordinary juggling and
survival.

The bounded launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_record_new3_v151_stage51_family_balance_probe_from_v146_u7345.sh`.
It is GPU1-only, requires `pp_gpu1`, uses seed `82731`, 1024x128 samples,
offline W&B, LR `1e-5`, KL limit `0.002`, at most 160 updates and worst-family
validation. Acceptance additionally requires a deterministic 1024-lane
same-reset-family replay: falling hits/length/full/view must improve relative
to V146 without material qacc regression, while main-family and aggregate
juggling, survival, view and safety remain non-regressed. Formal training is
fail-closed until this evidence is recorded.

After acceptance only, the formal launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_record_new3_v151_reset_family_balanced_from_v146_u7345.sh`.
It restarts V146, never the probe actor, runs only in `pp_gpu1`, has no stage
update cap, and continues online W&B ID `v130g1r1` with `resume=must`, offset
`1849556992`, and expected first new step `16537714688`.

V151 is rejected by its preregistered paired-family gate. The offline probe
reached the recovery gate at update 79; its final-48 aggregate
hits/length/full/view were `12.0436/0.9153/0.8347/0.9394`, exact KL was
`0.000809` with maximum `0.001997`, explained variance was `0.9653`, qacc
exceedance was `0.00285`, and there were no raw-action clips or PPO
rollbacks. The raw falling time-step fraction was `0.04373`; the implemented
actor mass was exactly `0.15`.

Four deterministic 1024-lane first-episode screens used seeds
`82731,97731,12731,62731`, producing 206 falling and 3890 main lanes. For
V151 last, falling parent-to-candidate hits were `9.8981 -> 9.9612`, length
`0.7313 -> 0.7277`, full rate `0.6262 -> 0.6165`, view
`0.8150 -> 0.8021`, and qacc exceedance `0.00786 -> 0.00836`; every paired
95% bootstrap interval crossed zero. The saved best improved falling hits by
only `0.1748`, held full rate exactly, reduced view by `0.0189`, and raised
main hit-racket VXY and qacc significantly. Thus actor-advantage mass alone
does not establish recovery and tends toward a more aggressive local policy.
The V151 formal launcher remains fail-closed and wrote no online W&B point.

## Fixed-Contact V76 / V77 Factorized-Timing and Recurrent-Stroke Repair (2026-09-08)

The V74/V75 plateau jobs were safely interrupted before this revision. The
new continuation sources are their last complete periodic checkpoints, not
their unsaved terminal stdout rows. V76 resumes only V74 update 2150, true
step `2583191552`, stage 10 `v74_s0_positive_x_grid_timing_bridge`, SHA-256
`d818c5ff0cbd2dc43e36813970210da4848cf25c113dd363073bc5594d40e1c3`.
V77 resumes only V75 update 1050, true step `1142784000`, stage 6
`v75_s1_center_effective_recurrent_credit_bridge`, SHA-256
`e71e6a4e61b5a75ca1c6204352f1ee8814b672943b23851e8d1525b1232ccf8f`.
Both sources retain the complete 80-D actor, 401-D critic, seven-action policy
and Adam state. Curriculum-history resume, optimizer/critic reset,
observation migration, another source profile or a changed control stack fail
closed.

V74's first repair remained incomplete for three independent reasons. Its
3x3 XY evaluation lanes still sampled five reset target-follow blends at
random, so a nominal XY bucket mixed materially different starting distances
and had too few samples to represent its worst case. A diagnostic
`--fixed-blend` override cleared the choices but not their apply flag, causing
the environment constructor to reject the supposedly fixed run. Finally,
the requested `0.52--0.60 s` falling time-to-contact interval exceeded the
approximately `0.482--0.515 s` full ballistic flight supported by the
configured `0.285--0.325 m` apex range, so the executable reset silently
clipped much of the declared timing lesson. Reset also initialized an
otherwise visible ball's cached velocity to zero until the first 90 Hz camera
refresh, producing an artificial initial predicted TTC around `0.06--0.17 s`
before it jumped toward `0.49 s`.

V76 is a one-to-one V74 stage copy except stages 9--10 (zero-based indices
8--9). Those stages deterministically factor evaluation lanes across the
complete 3 x 3 XY grid and all five target-follow blends, and the block gate
computes the worst readiness/arrival cell over XY plus blend. The bridge uses
apex `0.35--0.38 m` and TTC `0.50--0.53 s`; the commit uses apex
`0.30--0.34 m` and TTC `0.45--0.49 s`. Every requested TTC is therefore no
larger than the minimum ballistic full-flight support for its stage. Only
these two stages opt into initializing a visible reset observation with the
actual initialized ball velocity. Historical profiles keep zero velocity at
reset and are numerically unchanged. The deterministic evaluation requires
90 lanes, giving two lanes per 3 x 3 x 5 cell.

V75's plateau is a genuine one-hit optimum: its last rolling window retained
approximately one hit and full 270-step lifetime, while hit3 stayed zero,
mean return horizontal displacement was about `0.078 m` outward and signed
center progress about `-0.078 m`. The fixed-contact outcome constraint that
the gate measures was telemetry-only in this lesson because both its penalty
and bonus weights were zero. The existing launch-Vz shaping was also
restricted to pre-first-hit acquisition, leaving no direct causal signal for
the upward racket stroke before a predicted second contact.

V77 is a one-to-one V75 stage copy with two default-off reward changes on
collision-enabled lessons. First, it activates the existing mean-aggregated
outcome constraint with penalty and bonus weights of at least `0.25`, so PPO
optimizes the same horizontal-return/center criteria used by graduation.
Second, its first three recurrent lessons add a signed, clipped racket-Z
velocity reward only after at least one confirmed hit, only before a valid
predicted downward crossing, only when no hit is pending, and only inside
`100/90/80 ms` windows. Weights are `20/10/5` and the target is `0.50 m/s`;
all later lessons set the new term to zero. This does not alter collision or
hit confirmation, does not pay on the first launch, and cannot reward a raw
contact as a hit.

Focused new and compatibility tests cover deterministic lane indexing,
blend-aware worst-cell aggregation, legacy default-off behavior, reset
velocity warm-start/missing-observation safety, recurrent reward causality and
bounds, stage-diff allowlists, exact stopped checkpoint pins, launcher
ordering and memory-scope forwarding. The expanded applicable regression
suite passed 230 tests; the final focused suite passed 21 tests. Python and
shell syntax checks pass. Physical-CUDA frozen evaluation at 90 lanes showed
the repaired V76 initial TTC entirely inside `0.5005--0.5303 s` and exposed
the true blend tail: blend 0 readiness was about `0.09`, while blends 0.75 and
1.0 were about `0.95--0.97`; some individual 3 x 3 x 5 cells remain zero and
must be learned. Two V77 frozen seeds preserved the one-hit dynamics while
adding about `-0.60` recurrent up-stroke reward and `-1.38` outcome penalty
per episode, proving that both corrective signals reach PPO with the expected
sign. Frozen replay is mechanism evidence, not convergence evidence.

Formal V76 runs only through
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v76_resume_v74_u2150.sh`
in `pp_gpu0`, with 1024 environments by 128 steps, minibatch 16384, four
epochs, LR `1e-4`, gamma `0.9995`, GAE lambda `0.99`, clip `0.10` and target
KL `0.006`. Formal V77 runs only through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v77_resume_v75_u1050.sh`
in `pp_gpu1`, with 512 environments by 256 steps, minibatch 16384, four
epochs, LR `5e-5`, gamma `0.9995`, GAE lambda `0.995`, clip `0.10` and target
KL `0.004`. V77's launcher requires the selected formal V76 CSV to contain
at least 50 `v76_` update rows and a maximum true step of at least
`2589745152`; `training_memory_scope.py` forwards only the explicit
`GPU0_V76_PROGRESS_CSV` evidence path. Both use new run identities, retain
the named cgroup and 78 C GPU guards, and remain experimental,
simulation-only policies with the existing real-camera, new-ball outcome and
formal RMP/PD evidence blockers.

The first V76 integration launch (`...20260908_formal1`) failed closed before

speed, at least `cos(5 deg)` upward normal, a maximum `0.052 m` horizontal
return step, and the registered `1.38--1.42 m` apex band.

V84 adds an opt-in actual-racket-Z target with a non-saturating pseudo-Huber
loss. It rises smoothly over the policy-visible predicted approach, holds an
allowed pure vertical speed through contact, and leaves XY, height, pose,
horizontal-speed and angular-speed constraints active. A bounded downward
retraction follows every pending contact. This also repairs a hidden
multi-contact bug: the historical retraction helper was hard-coded to
`hit_count <= 0`, so a nonzero recurrent retraction weight could never affect
the second or later hit. The new all-hit behavior is separately opt-in and all
older profiles retain the exact first-contact-only default. V84 keeps the
initial falling orbit at the physically reasonable `0.285--0.325 m` relative
apex throughout the course. The inherited late `0.20--0.24 m` reset demanded
roughly twice the active racket impulse at the same final target apex and was
experimentally coupled to excessive horizontal/rotational transients.

with earlier phase compensation averaged `2.625` hits, `0.0606 m/s` contact

reset produced eight physical contacts but zero confirmed hits. Restoring the
matched `0.285--0.325 m` reset recovered `2.875` mean hits; increasing Z

bounds. A hand-fit seven-joint scale worsened horizontal speed to `0.1299
m/s`, proving that independent static joint scaling is not an adequate MIMO
inverse for the delayed RMP/PD transient.

feedforward/MPC controller that optimizes vertical impulse while constraining
contact XY velocity, full angular velocity, pose, height, joint limits and

the memory-safe trainer path; the pinned V86 same-stage exception documented
below exists only for its 2026-09-11 memory-guard interruption.

Both courses project the seven-joint QVEL update before it advances the
persistent policy reference. The resulting boundary remains exactly
`policy q_ref -> recovered RMP -> XML PD`. The hard policy-frame position box
is X `[-0.348, 0.348] m`, Y `[-0.700, -0.280] m`, and Z
`[1.002, 1.120] m`. Orientation is the XYZ-Euler angle of
`R_warm^T R_qref`: roll and pitch are bounded while yaw is entirely absent
from the projection. A 0.5 mm / 0.1 degree inner numerical margin precedes an
exact MJX FK check; an unsafe nonlinear candidate or unfinished linear solve
publishes the preceding safe reference instead. Position, roll/pitch, yaw,
intervention, retained velocity, nonlinear backstop, fallback, and both
q_ref/actual-racket violations are logged separately. A small squared
projection cost rises with the constraint curriculum so PPO learns not to
depend on the shield.

The transition is fixed and cannot be skipped: the first four lessons use
roll/pitch limits `+/-15`, `+/-8`, `+/-5`, and `+/-2` degrees with at least
`40`, `50` where applicable, `60` where applicable, and `80` where applicable
updates before the final limit. The absolute XYZ hard set is active from the
first step because it is the already registered fixed-contact workspace, not
a new shrinking task distribution. V85 retains the complete V83 multi-stage
S0-to-juggling curriculum and applies that four-step orientation homotopy to
its first four collision-off lessons. V86 deliberately removes V84's four
placed-ball pre-acquisition lessons: it repeats the centered causal
falling-contact, hit/survival-only acquisition lesson at each of the four
orientation limits, then restores the quality hinge bridge/commit/strict
sequence and only afterward widens the workspace center -> local -> inner ->
mid -> wide -> full.

The extra reference and candidate FK evaluations increase memory and compute
cost. V85 therefore uses `512 x 128`, minibatch `8192`, four PPO epochs, LR
`1e-4`, clip `0.10`, target KL `0.006`, gamma `0.9995`, and GAE `0.99`.
V86 uses `256 x 256`, minibatch `8192`, four epochs, LR `5e-5`, clip `0.10`,
target KL `0.004`, gamma `0.9995`, and GAE `0.995`. Both retain the 80-D actor,
asymmetric critic with 12 command-history samples, 4.0 g measured ball
interval, fixed base, measured feedback, bounded q_ref, recovered RMP/PD,
convergence and block-validation gates, source snapshots, GPU identity and
temperature checks, and non-overwriting run directories.

Formal ordering is mandatory. `pp_gpu0` starts V85 first. The V86 launcher
requires the selected V85 `curriculum_progress.csv` and independently checks

fallback, PPO rollback/KL instability, hard q_ref violation, or safety-gate
failure; stage advancement additionally retains every registered hit,
survival, motion, view, apex and validation gate.

The earlier paired old-policy experiment remains negative transfer evidence:
directly adding the final constraint modified 94.38% of actions and reduced

for the published policy reference, not yet for actual racket motion, and it

### 2026-09-14 method-level plateau repair: V131 and V132

The formal fixed-contact V129/V130 jobs were stopped independently at V129
stage update 3413 and V130 stage update 3294. Neither stop was caused by the
runtime stack: their last 100-update mean KL values were about `0.00245` and
`0.00185`, explained variance about `0.970` and `0.950`, raw-action clipping
was zero, no recent PPO update rolled back, and neither cgroup recorded a
memory/OOM event. The failure is in the learning method and curriculum
contract.

V129 inherited a valid collision-off prediction-arrival course, but every
collision-on stage removed both the S0 arrival graduation gate and the
explicit vertical-stroke/retraction objective. The actor could therefore buy
hit/apex reward while catastrophically forgetting the prerequisite. At the
stop, its S0 component scores were approximately
`0.631/0.729/0.582/0.423/0.782`, but complete readiness and arrival readiness
were only `0.279/0.260`, far below the passed full-workspace S0 contract
`0.80/0.75`. Dense stationary-Z shaping also remained active through impact,
even though a vertical hit requires nonzero Z velocity. This is not repaired
by more low-X sampling or by relaxing the motion/apex gate.

V130's exact-corner weighting improved first-hit coverage, but it optimized a
falling-contact reset rather than the requested placed-ball problem. Five
frozen blocks all failed; the most recent selected block had reset-bucket
CVaR hit3 about `0.350` against `0.45`. At the stop, S0 complete
readiness/arrival readiness were only about `0.198/0.208`. Historical
placed-ball runs had already shown the deeper failure: the first contact was
learnable, but the policy over-retreated and did not close the next predicted
arrival/stroke loop. Mixing falling resets only changed the initial-state
distribution and did not repair that recurrent controller.

V131 `fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v131` is the new GPU0
continuation. It resumes only the passed V95 full-workspace S0 checkpoint
`14_v95_s0_full_workspace_safe_reset_commit.pkl` at true step `1113522176`,
update 231, SHA-256
`9a0d885c1a9d484e19ef2932449be6e1d89abb02ed9e779c0da8924df39a9ebe`.
It restores actor, critic and Adam moments but starts fresh collision-stage
history. The first 14 S0 stages are behavior-identical registered copies of
V95. Collision is then enabled at center and widened through local, inner,
middle and full workspace only after each gate passes.

Every V131 collision stage keeps a block-evaluated complete arrival gate in
the `80--100 ms` pre-contact window. The smooth vertical stroke begins only
at `80 ms`, follows a cosine ramp to its peak at `20 ms`, and masks only the
contradictory stationary-Z shaping while XY position and pose shaping remain
active. Every physical contact has a bounded `100 ms` downward retraction,
followed by a `300 ms` predicted next-contact recovery window. This makes the
task a single causal loop:

`predict contact -> arrive/settle -> late vertical hit -> retract -> predict
the next contact`.

V131 launches only through
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v131_1024x128_resume_v95_s0.sh`.
Its first-stage preregistered acceptance requires mean hits/hit1 at least
`0.30/0.30`, center arrival readiness at least `0.50`, a frozen block pass,
finite PPO with no rollback, and zero Cartesian-q_ref/qvel hard-set
violations. Actual-plant qacc exceedance remains separately reported rather
than being mislabeled as a q_ref projection constraint. A higher return
without the arrival gate is a failure.

V132 `fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v132` is the new GPU1
from-scratch course and deliberately has no collision-off prerequisite. Every
episode uses `racket_launch`: the ball is placed `1 mm` above the racket, and
the racket pose follows a sampled episode target. The randomized support
widens from local to full workspace while roll/pitch hard constraints tighten
`15 -> 8 -> 5 -> 2 deg`. Launch hold tapers
`120 -> 90 -> 60 -> 30 -> 0 ms`; bounded desired/realized launch credit also
tapers to zero and a `0.5 s` first-hit deadline prevents a hold-reward
loophole. Starting with the first recurrent bridge, V132 uses the same
post-first-hit `80 ms` late stroke, all-hit `100 ms` retraction, `300 ms`
recovery window and block-evaluated arrival retention as V131. Falling-contact
and mixed resets are absent.

Each V132 lesson owns an explicit XY support grid containing its lower edge,
center and upper edge plus every applicable canonical lane. This is required:
intersecting the historical 6-by-6 full-workspace grid with the first local
range leaves only `(0, 0)` and silently turns the intended randomized reset
into a center-only reset. The initial lesson therefore uses the exact 3-by-3
grid `X={-0.05,0,+0.05} m`, `Y={-0.04,0,+0.04} m`; later lessons expand the
grid and the final lesson restores all canonical full-workspace lanes.

V132 launches only through

### 2026-09-15 plateau root fix: V135 and V136

The V133 and V134 formal jobs were stopped after independent, preregistered
plateau audits. GPU0 V133 passed its center recurrent bridge, but then spent
3381 workspace-local updates at approximately `1.96` hits/episode with hit3
exactly zero. The local horizon is `1.0 s`; its falling first contact occurs
about `0.32--0.46 s` after reset and two requested `0.40--0.52 s` adjacent
intervals require at least `1.12--1.50 s`. V133 had accidentally applied a
positive hit3 gate and three-hit completion reward to this structurally
infeasible lesson and every later short-horizon workspace lesson. Its dense

### 2026-09-16 GPU0 exact-arrival method repair: V138

The V137 failure isolates a second objective/gate mismatch rather than a need
for another course. The S0 final/readiness shaping is paid over the broad
`time_to_contact <= 0.16 s` interval created by the 0.08 s final window plus
0.08 s settle lead, while graduation samples the much narrower registered
`0.08--0.10 s` arrival window. An actor can therefore settle after the graded
window, score the broad shaping and reach excellent physical contact, yet fail
the arrival-time conjunction. This is exactly the V137 block evidence.

### 2026-09-16 GPU0 V139 full-cycle exact-corner plateau: V143

The recovered V139 formal run was stopped at reliable periodic checkpoint
update 2405, true step `2088042496`, Stage 23
`v139_s1_workspace_full_cycle`, SHA-256
`850a293c637ff19163d42480c16f75da4d0567cb3deeee29ac5714f15b286aa3`.
The late policy remained globally strong: hit1 about `0.88--0.89`, full
horizon about `0.84--0.85`, counted cadence about `0.480 s`, view about

16 consecutive independent validations retained hit1 exactly zero in the
`x=-0.30 m, y=+0.18 m` cell. This is a real support-tail plateau, not PPO or
global juggling collapse.

The method audit found two coupled defects. The atomic secondary registry did
not contain the stage's declared worst fixed-XY-bin success rate, and the
multi-seed combiner averaged per-seed minima. Thus a globally improving
candidate could commit while the exact failed cell remained zero. Moreover,
continuous full-domain sampling gives the precise outer boundary zero measure,
so more unchanged updates do not allocate a useful actor gradient to it.

lessons one-to-one and resumes the same full-cycle stage with actor, critic and

## Predictive Contact Decomposition V146/V147/V148 (Stage-1 proofs passed)

The implementation contract and failure analysis are in
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/GPU0_GPU1_PREDICTIVE_CONTACT_CURRICULUM_REDESIGN.md`.
The three profiles below are opt-in experiments. They preserve the 80-D actor,
401-D asymmetric critic, measured-QVEL bounded reference, recovered-RMP/PD,
fixed-base XML, 4 g ball interval, contact parameters, observation contract and
Cartesian hard limits of their fixed-contact parents. They do not constitute
training evidence, hardware coverage or a deployable model. V144/V145 builders,
launchers and checkpoint meanings remain unchanged.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v146` is the GPU0
continuation-only course. It accepts exactly the stopped V145 checkpoint at
true step `3257204736`, update/stage-update `7072`, source stage 25
`v145_s1_motion_apex_conjunction_commit`, SHA-256
`7b0c1947f2b41c6076292924280177818fcbb9ad53704ef30a864c67ad366889`.
It restores the 80-D actor, critic and complete Adam moments, starts fresh
curriculum/convergence history, and rejects from-scratch launch, history
resume, optimizer/critic reset, another source identity or transaction guard.
PPO remains `1024 x 128`, minibatch `16384`, 2 epochs, LR `1e-4`,
gamma/GAE `0.9995/0.99`, clip `0.10`, target KL `0.006`, entropy `1e-4`, and
log-std `[-4.0,-2.8]`.

V146 contains exactly 15 stages in this order: five collision-free
arrival-only lessons (`center`, `local`, `inner`, `mid`, `full`), two
arrival-conditioned single-hit lessons, five 1.5 s joint-mixture lessons, one
3 s lesson, and two 6 s lessons. Joint lessons sample reset modes per actual
reset, initially `20/20/60%` arrival/single-hit/recurrent, then `10/10/80%`,
and finally `5/5/90%`. Arrival-only terminates before contact at TTC <=20 ms;
single-hit lanes receive an independently sampled 80--100 ms initial TTC.
The gates include readiness at 100 ms, readiness occupancy over 100--60 ms,
exact episode `P(N>=1/2/3/5/6/12)`, contact occupancy, contact-duration p95
(including terminal right-censored lower bounds) and
physical-edge-to-counted-hit conversion, in addition to inherited
motion, outcome, view and safety gates. In mixed lessons, survival and
full-horizon gates are explicitly conditioned on recurrent reset lanes; the
unconditional rates remain logged. This prevents the intentional arrival-only
and one-hit probes from making registered recurrent `P(N>=k)` targets
mathematically impossible. Contact-duration tails also include the elapsed
lower bound of a contact still active at episode termination, so a persistent
contact cannot disappear merely by never detaching. Block validation consumes
the same raw episode/event quantities; it does not derive survival
probabilities from mean hit count.

For V146/V147 rolling convergence, episode/event gates pool raw numerators and
denominators over the complete current window before computing a probability,
mean or RMS; historical profiles retain their previous rolling calculation.
The registered 20 ms contact-duration p95 gate uses a strict raw-window
`duration > 20 ms` tail fraction below 5%, while the independent block
validation computes the exact p95 from its complete duration-event array.

The held-readiness quantity is explicitly per-episode equal-weight readiness
occupancy in the 100--60 ms window, not a strict all-samples Boolean. Frozen
workspace grids are stage-local and edge-inclusive: center `1x1`,
local/inner `3x3`, mid `4x5`, and full `6x6`. This prevents the historical
coarse grid from collapsing the new local workspace to a center-only cell.
Pooled readiness and worst-cell readiness use separate registered thresholds;
the V146 arrival tail is `0.85/0.70/0.65/0.60/0.55`, while recurrent Stages
10 and 12 require worst-cell hit1 `0.70/0.55`. From the committed single-hit
lesson onward, V146 also registers mean/RMS ball VXY `0.16/0.23 m/s`, RMS
hit-racket VXY `0.105 m/s`, next-anchor error `0.050 m`, and horizontal return
step `0.050 m`; mean hit-racket VXY is explicitly capped at `0.065 m/s`, and
the stronger inherited angular gate remains in force.

V146 has separate bounded-probe, independent Stage-1 proof and formal-course
launchers. The proof launcher is
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v146_stage1_proof_resume_v145_u7072.sh`;
the formal launcher is
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v146_formal_resume_v145_u7072.sh`.
Both restart the exact canonical V145-u7072 source rather than a probe actor.
The formal launcher is uncapped and exposes all 15 stages. Every launcher uses
a new output identity, inherited GPU/host-memory/temperature/checkpoint-hash
preflight, and the explicit GPU0 confirmation/incomplete-evidence
acknowledgement.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v147` is the GPU1 from-scratch
course. It rejects every checkpoint and resume/reset option and uses a random
80-D actor with PPO `1024 x 128`, minibatch `16384`, 4 epochs, LR `5e-5`,
gamma/GAE `0.9995/0.995`, clip `0.10`, target KL `0.004`, entropy `1e-4`, and
log-std `[-4.8,-2.8]`. It contains exactly 13 clean-airborne stages: center and
local acquisition at a 5 degree roll/pitch box, a 3 degree pose commit, five
local-to-full recurrent lessons, two prediction/arrival-shaping lessons, then
3 s and 6 s survival lessons. It has no separate arrival-only stage.
The first prediction bridge activates the existing normalized arrival-window
constraint with weight 5; the commit and all later stages use weight 10. This
is the only new reward-weight transition in V147 and makes the registered
prediction/arrival lessons behavioral rather than instrumentation-only.
Its inner/mid/full recurrent stages require worst-cell hit1
`0.65/0.60/0.55`; the prediction commit independently requires pooled
100--60 ms readiness occupancy `>=0.60` and worst-cell occupancy `>=0.40`.
From clean-hit Stage 2 onward, V147 additionally gates aggregate and first-hit
ball VXY, hit-racket mean/RMS VXY, angular speed, the five contact-quality
components, return trajectory/apex and simultaneous outcome readiness. The
recurrent bridge activates counted-event cadence `0.40--0.52 s`; the pose
commit uses next-anchor `<=0.070 m`, tightened to `<=0.050 m` at recurrent
commit. These are block gates as well as rolling gates, not log-only fields.

V147 replaces policy-controlled placed-ball launch with an analytic separated
descending handoff. Implementation smoke corrected the draft TTC to
0.16--0.21 s: with an approximately 1.095 m contact-center plane and 1.33 m
inbound apex, the available pure-descending flight is only about 0.219 s. The
draft 0.32--0.46 s range placed the handoff ball at roughly 1.61--2.15 m and
terminated on the first policy tick. Horizontal reset velocity is zero in the
first implementation, and vertical position is analytically back-propagated
to cross the registered plane at the sampled TTC with a small negative initial
vertical velocity. The configured 1.33 m value remains the desired post-impact
apex; the actual inbound scripted origin is derived and reported separately.
Collision physics and target apex are unchanged.

V147's retained launcher is the bounded, offline, one-stage probe

It defaults to 16 updates and cannot start before the existing explicit GPU1

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v148` is the corrected GPU1

GPU1 V147 then ran from scratch for 16 updates. Contact occupancy `0.02177`

## GPU0 Predictive Reset-Blend Repair V151

The V149 formal run stopped at update 500 because its periodic same-stage
memory-release reexec supplied both `--trainer-stage-reexec` and
`--resume-curriculum-state`, while the Cartesian argument guard still rejected
all history resume.  This was a launcher/trainer contract defect, not a CUDA,
temperature, host-memory or PPO failure.  V149/V150/V151 now authenticate
same-profile reexec checkpoints, require bounded `stage_history_tail`, restore
actor/critic/Adam, and allow curriculum-state resume only when the trainer's
internal reexec marker is present.  Initial parent resumes and next-stage
reexecs still start fresh per-stage convergence history and remain fail-closed.

The stopped V149 checkpoint is true step `3697737728`, global/stage update
`500`, Stage 4 `v149_g0_arrival_mid_deadline_bridge`, SHA-256
`e0fd77cf4cc70fdd54a8965146ce886000cb0e55fdc4dff44e8dab3b1b7b19c1`.
Its 500-update history is a plateau, not a valid stage boundary.  Over the
late window, aggregate ready@100/arrival/held readiness stayed approximately
`0.709/0.710/0.754`; the independent factorized block repeatedly failed with
zero worst-stratum readiness despite passing global Cartesian and safety
gates.  Frozen paired trajectory replay showed zero ball XY drift, valid
descending prediction and in-view fraction 1.0.  The failure was reset-family
specific: complete target-follow (`blend=1.0`) lanes achieved ready@100
`0.952`, while `blend=0.8` lanes achieved `0.447`; the latter retained about
`0.0218 m` mean XY error and `0.0622 m/s` mean XY speed in the arrival window,
and 47.4% of those lanes had zero arrival readiness.  V149 improved their
braking versus its V146 parent but did not improve XY arrival or held
readiness.  The platform is therefore attributed to solved `blend=1.0`
success credit masking the undertrained residual-motion population, not to the
ball predictor, contact physics, optimizer collapse or a safety limiter.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v151` is the continuation-only
repair.  It accepts only that V149-u500 checkpoint, restores actor, critic and
Adam moments, and starts fresh V151 convergence history.  It changes no
observation, action, control, RMP/PD, XML, collision, hard Cartesian, measured
ball-mass or PPO contract.  Its first three lessons train only reset
`blend=0.8`, remove the center oversampling prior, and keep the full mid
workspace grid: exact-grid TTC `0.28--0.32 s`, exact-grid TTC
`0.22--0.32 s`, then the original jittered TTC `0.16--0.32 s`.  A fourth
lesson restores the original `blend=(0.8,1.0)`, center probability `0.20` and
`0.025 m` within-bin jitter.  Every lesson's independent advancement probe
still covers the complete registered `4 x 5 x 2` XY-by-blend product; the
launcher uses 160 lanes, giving four independent lanes per exact stratum.
After mixed retention, the unchanged V149 deadline commit and full remaining
course continue in order.

`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v151_resume_v149_u500.sh`.
The launcher keeps a 500-update periodic same-stage reexec, pins the source

remains experimental and simulation-only and inherits all unresolved
real-camera, replacement-ball and formal pointwise RMP/PD coverage blockers.

## GPU1 Observable Predictive-Recovery Repair V156

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v156` replaces the stopped V153
post-hit lesson after a component-level audit showed that V153's return rose
while its intended recovery behavior regressed.  Across updates 1--100 versus
701--800, hit1 increased from `0.67769` to `0.76916` and mean return from
`0.51294` to `5.47623`, but full-recovery completion fell from `0.001395` to
`0.000487`; arrival readiness fell from `0.01654` to `0.002504`, and mean
racket VXY/angular speed rose from `0.05319/0.23683` to
`0.07076/0.41784 m/s,rad/s`.  Return was almost uncorrelated with recovery
completion (`r=0.0013`) and strongly anticorrelated with arrival readiness
(`r=-0.9226`).  The gain instead came mainly from hit credit and reduced
outcome penalty.

The root cause was a reference/observability mismatch.  The full-recovery
terminal gate measured racket site-center XY/Z and velocity against the
episode reset `racket_anchor`, which is critic-only privileged state.  The
80-D actor and dense S0 reward instead use the predicted policy contact target
and the racket contact surface.  Moreover, the inherited `0.30 s` post-hit S0
window masked the first roughly `0.10 s` after a normal approximately
`0.40 s` next-contact prediction in a `0.38 s` lesson.

V156 therefore changes only the first active post-hit lesson relative to V153:

- full-recovery XY/Z/velocity use the actor-visible policy contact target and
  the racket contact surface/twist; target validity remains mandatory;
- dense S0 credit begins on the first post-hit tick
  (`fixed_contact_post_hit_s0_window_s=inf`);
- the `0.50` full-recovery, `0.85` hit1, `0.90` edge-to-hit and all trajectory,
  view, Cartesian, qvel and qacc gates remain unchanged;
- every stage has `max_updates=None`, and the launcher hard-sets
  `MAX_STAGE_UPDATES=0`.

V156 does not resume the behaviorally degraded V153-u800 actor.  It restores
the clean V148 Stage-3 actor, critic and Adam moments at true step `125960192`
from `03_v148_g1_pose_box_3deg_commit.pkl`, SHA-256
`3a796a1d4f5c6ca4aa383c25a77be92a8264fdf89ab7301e78d015a0b881a34a`,
and begins fresh convergence history at
`v156_g1_post_hit_predictive_recovery`.  Launch only through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v156_resume_v148_stage3_after_v154_u50.sh`.
The launcher additionally verifies at least 50 new safe V154 updates after
true step `3802595328` before GPU1 may start.

A two-seed, 256-lane-per-seed frozen-policy A/B on physical GPU1 held policy,
reset, physics and observation noise fixed.  For the clean V148 source,
recovery completion changed from `0/512` to `3/512`; for the stopped V153
actor it changed from `1/512` to `4/512`.  Hit1, view, apex, racket motion and
zero qvel/qacc exceedance were preserved.  This is causal evidence that the
new target is observable and reachable without claiming that an untrained
source actor already passes the `0.50` graduation gate.  Full evidence and
commands are in
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/predictive_contact_v156_rootcause_validation_20260919/VALIDATION_REPORT.md`.

The isolated physical-GPU1 one-update PPO probe restored the same clean
actor/critic/Adam state and completed at true step `126091264`: KL/exact KL
were `0.001092/0.001112`, rollback and Cartesian/qvel/qacc violations were
zero, and the memory scope peaked at 8.90 GiB without requesting a stop.  Its
nonzero process exit is the expected result of the diagnostic one-update cap;
the formal launcher remains uncapped.

V156 is experimental and simulation-only and inherits all open real-camera,
replacement-ball outcome and formal pointwise RMP/PD evidence blockers.

## Reproducible Hard-Corner and Recovery-Objective Repairs V159/V160

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v159` supersedes only the
unfinished GPU0 portion of V157.  The stopped V157 checkpoint is update 750,
true step `4261347328`, stage `v157_g0_blend080_capture_commit`, SHA-256
`8c0b195c4f59a2bddd0ca41ae886d617677ff6117a7b6522c9d0bbee129b66e1`.
Two independent 160-lane frozen replays reproduce the same unique zero-ready
cell at target offset `(-0.20,+0.12) m`, reset blend `0.80`: final XY error is
`34.18/32.91 mm`, while Z, pose, VXY and omega remain close to their gates.
Changing only reset blend to `0.85` raises readiness to `0.644/0.681` and
reduces XY error to `17.90/17.06 mm`.  The defect is therefore a sharp
distance/timing capture boundary, not a general pose or safety failure.

The exact target is statically reachable.  Its table FK residual is
`1.369 mm`, target orientation residual `0.141 deg`, nearest joint-limit
margin `0.401 rad`, weighted task-Jacobian minimum singular value `0.0889`
and condition number `9.44`; the Cartesian hard set contains both reset and
target.  Reset-to-target travel is `51.76 mm`.  The joint displacement has a
velocity-only lower bound of `58.75 ms`, but the more relevant independent-
joint rest-to-rest acceleration/velocity bound is `194.83 ms`.  Since the
100 ms readiness deadline leaves only `120--220 ms` in the old
`TTC=0.22--0.32 s` lesson, part of that timing product is physically
infeasible or marginless even though the spatial point is valid.

V159 therefore does not shrink the workspace.  It resumes actor, critic and
Adam moments with fresh convergence history, isolates the reproduced corner
at blends `0.85 -> 0.825 -> 0.80` with `TTC=0.32--0.36 s`, restores the full
workspace at `TTC=0.30--0.36 s`, then compresses to `0.28--0.34 s` before

## Dynamically Invariant GPU1 Recovery Repair V161

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v161` supersedes only V160's

Across 1,556,947 completed episodes it recorded only 105 recovery successes
(`0.00674%`), and about 85% of update batches contained no success.  The late
failure distribution was almost entirely racket-Z workspace termination,
while the post-hit racket surface still had about `0.238 m/s` vertical speed
and `3.27 m/s^2` vertical acceleration.  V160's recovery conjunction did not
include vertical speed, its recovery-specific motion shaping assigned no
vertical-braking cost, and its `-4` failure cost applied only to the roughly
`0.07%` of late episodes that reached truncation.  Early workspace exits were
therefore an unpriced absorbing escape.  Its maximum-only dense cost also
allowed the active gradient to switch between constraint components.  PPO,
joint limits, QVEL/QACC safety and action clipping remained healthy, so this
is a task/terminal-set defect rather than an optimizer or GPU fault.

V161 again restores the clean V148 Stage-3 actor, critic and Adam state; it
does not resume the failed V160 policy.  It replaces the single recovery
lesson with five uncapped lessons.  The first two learn Z/pose/vertical-speed
braking, then three lessons add XY/VXY/omega and monotonically tighten the
full invariant recovery set.  The vertical-speed limit follows
`0.30 -> 0.18 -> 0.18 -> 0.12 -> 0.08 m/s`; the final conjunction also uses
`20 mm` XY, `25 mm` Z, `3 deg` pose, `0.08 m/s` VXY and `0.75 rad/s` angular
speed.  Every unsuccessful terminal event, including workspace or ball-loss
termination, pays `-4`; successful recovery pays `8`.  A smooth mean robust
normalized cost with weight `2` retains simultaneous gradients on every
enabled component, and new telemetry reports post-hit VXY, omega and VZ
quality plus absolute surface VZ.  V160's timeout-only and maximum-only terms
are disabled in these lessons, so costs are not double-counted.  All new
environment fields default off/zero, preserving every V1--V160 path.

The final recovery gate remains `0.50`; bridge gates are `0.20`, `0.30`,
`0.20`, and `0.35`.  Successive hit1/contact-conversion gates rise from
`0.78/0.78` to `0.85/0.90`.  Every stage has no update cap and advances only
through its complete rolling and frozen validation gates.  Launch only
through

## True Cartesian Reset-Distance Repair V162

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v162` supersedes the unfinished
GPU0 V159 continuation. It restores only the last complete V159 checkpoint at
update 1510, true step `4512350208`, stage
`v159_g0_full_workspace_blend080_ttc300_bridge`, SHA-256
`750e4e9c065eca652b7f571427dd4dc22ae24249f78891566bb7bf6f3dc48ae2`.
Actor, critic and Adam moments are restored, while V162 deliberately starts
fresh stage and convergence history. It rejects from-scratch launch, another
source profile/stage/step, optimizer or critic reset, and same-profile resume
without matching V162 history.

The V159 plateau was caused by a reset-course implementation defect rather
than an unreachable workspace point or insufficient PPO updates. Its
hard-corner focus stage narrowed the episode-target range to the singleton
`(-0.20,+0.12) m`. The Cartesian reset requested target-scaled blend 0.8,
`(-0.16,+0.096) m`, but the host reset-IK table was built only over the raw
singleton target domain. Nearest-neighbour lookup therefore snapped the
requested reset back to the target. Frozen replay measured only `1.202 mm`
first-step target error in that alleged blend-0.8 lesson. The later full-
workspace lesson built a wider table and exposed the real approximately
`47.2 mm` acquisition problem; its uniform grid also quantized the requested
blend reset to a neighbour, producing `52.825 mm` first-step error. Thus the
focus lesson's high readiness was invalid evidence: it taught almost-at-target
holding and then changed reset semantics when the target support expanded.

V162 enables a new default-off compatibility switch only for its stages. The
host reset-IK domain is expanded to include every configured target multiplied
by every configured reset blend, and exact target-by-blend knots are inserted
in the lookup table. All V1--V161 configurations retain the old default.
Control, observation, reward, physics, workspace, RMP/PD, PPO and hard
constraints are unchanged. With the repair, the hard-corner first-step
distance is exactly `24.100 mm` at blend 0.9 and `47.200 mm` at blend 0.8 in
both the focused and full-workspace courses.

V162 first relearns the true acquisition distance at blend
`0.90 -> 0.85 -> 0.825 -> 0.80`, then replays a northwest 2-by-2 region, an
upper-left 3-by-3 region, and the complete workspace before returning to the
preserved V159 tail. Its first four TTC ranges are respectively
`0.34--0.38`, `0.34--0.38`, `0.33--0.37`, and `0.32--0.36 s`; full-workspace
reintroduction first retains `0.32--0.36 s` and then commits to
`0.30--0.36 s`. Every stage is uncapped and advances only through its full
rolling and frozen-validation gates. The workspace and strict motion/safety
gates are not weakened.

Two-seed frozen validation found that the source actor remains physically safe
on the corrected blend-0.8 corner (`61.0--65.7%` 100-ms readiness and
`69.4--72.4%` arrival readiness), so the corrected task is feasible but not
already solved. A 35-update PPO probe from the pinned source improved paired
blend-0.9 replay return from `5.472/5.485` to `5.564/5.580`, XY quality from
`0.962/0.963` to `0.979/0.980`, pose quality from `0.713/0.710` to
`0.862/0.856`, VXY quality from `0.793/0.784` to `0.878/0.878`, and angular
quality from `0.896/0.899` to `0.936/0.936`. Joint velocity/acceleration and
Cartesian hard-constraint exceedance remained zero. This probe is evidence
for the repaired gradient path only and is not the formal resume source.

Launch V162 only through
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v162_resume_v159_u1510.sh`.
Detailed root-cause, frozen-replay and PPO-probe evidence is recorded in
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/gpu0_v162_reset_domain_validation_20260920/VALIDATION_REPORT.md`.
V162 remains experimental and simulation-only and inherits every real-camera,
replacement-ball outcome and formal pointwise RMP/PD evidence blocker.

## Joint-Feasible GPU0 XY/Blend/TTC Contract V163

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v163` supersedes only the stopped

`4d8f716f7bacd1fee224e7e4c7c582ba0dce58e886ae8ceaf3b96e4f596bd065`.

V163 fixes the method-level defect exposed by the 2026-09-20 frozen
feasibility audit: target XY, reset distance and TTC are no longer independent
curriculum axes.  A default-off row-major 4-by-5 table registers the minimum
closed-loop TTC for every XY cell at reset blend 0.8.  The table, in X-major
order over `X=(-0.20,-0.10,0.00,0.10)` and
`Y=(-0.12,-0.06,0.00,0.06,0.12) m`, is:

```text
[.28,.26,.28,.30,.36,
 .26,.24,.24,.24,.30,
 .24,.24,.24,.24,.24,
 .30,.24,.24,.24,.26] s
```

Values are the first two-seed frozen ready/arrival TTC with 20 ms margin; the

interpolate between those time floors.  A sampled shorter TTC is raised to the
registered floor.  This represents the normal early-prediction task.  Late
acquisition outside that feasible set is a separate recovery contract and is
not labelled a mandatory normal-arrival PPO failure.

Training samples raw TTC over `0.22--0.36 s`, blend 0.8/1.0 with 80/20 mass,
and all 20 XY cells.  Frozen graduation deterministically covers the complete
`XY x blend x raw-TTC` product at raw TTC
`{.22,.26,.30,.34,.36} s`, applies the same feasibility transform, and
stratifies readiness by actual initial TTC as well as XY and blend.  It needs
exactly 200 lanes.  Thus easy/long samples cannot average away one feasible
boundary stratum.  The bridge uses zero XY jitter and 0.40 worst-stratum
ready/arrival/hold gates; commit adds 10 mm training jitter and raises them to
0.55.  Long 0.34/0.36 s support is present in every lesson.  The later
arrived-hit and recurrent V162 tail is preserved only after this joint
contract passes.  Cartesian hard constraints, 80-D observation, measured-QVEL

## Resolved-Contact/Recurrent-Stroke GPU1 Repair V165

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v165` supersedes only the stopped
V164 recursive-hit lesson.  It restores the V164 update-1100 checkpoint at
true step `1359609856`, stage `v164_g1_recursive_hit3_bridge`, SHA-256
`1551472a5c1a194f3df8cc2f6526638df444fd76c8f457db77762580267404bd`,

curriculum-history resume.

V165 repairs three contracts exposed by the frozen V164 plateau experiment.
First, its contact-conversion denominator contains only contacts that have
been resolved as a counted hit or explicit confirmation failure.  A contact
still awaiting the 350 ms confirmation window when the finite rollout ends is
reported separately as `contact_terminal_pending_fraction`; it is neither a
success nor a false failure.  `P(hit3)`, episode length and truncation remain
independent survival gates, so this accounting change cannot make a
right-censored short episode pass.  All earlier profiles retain the legacy
physical-edge denominator.

Second, V165 restores a smooth recurrent vertical stroke only after two
counted hits (`weight=4`, peak speed `0.35 m/s`, lead `0.12 s`, brake
`0.03 s`, error scale `0.12 m`).  This directly targets the measured third
contact failure mode: nearly stationary racket vertical speed and negligible
post-impact ball lift despite comparable contact offsets.  Third, it applies
the existing direct hit-racket horizontal-speed loss with weight `1`, soft
limit `0.05 m/s`, and scale `0.05 m/s`, aligning optimization with the
unchanged `0.065 m/s` mean-hit-racket-XY graduation gate.

The first lesson requires mean hits `>=2.20`, `P(hit1)>=0.95`,
`P(hit2)>=0.90`, `P(hit3)>=0.50`, resolved contact conversion `>=0.90`,
cadence `0.36--0.52 s`, mean hit apex relative height `0.20--0.29 m`, mean
hit-racket XY speed `<=0.065 m/s`, and all inherited view, Cartesian, joint
and projection-safety gates.  The second lesson raises `P(hit3)` to `0.60`;
the remaining V164 recurrent/wide-horizon lessons follow with the same repaired
reward and accounting semantics.  Control, 80-D observation, RMP/PD,
collision physics, reset distribution, DR and PPO settings are unchanged.
Every stage is uncapped.

Launch only through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v165_resume_v164_u1100.sh`.
The default formal seed is `20261785`; a finite update cap is permitted only
for a separately named diagnostic run and is never used by the formal
`pp_gpu1` launch.  V165 remains experimental, simulation-only and inherits
every V164 evidence blocker.

The bounded 120-update V165 probe is retained as a negative result.  Across
updates 11--30 versus 91--120, mean hit-racket XY speed improved from
`0.06935` to `0.06088 m/s`, but `P(hit3)` fell from `0.5620` to `0.5114` and
resolved conversion fell from `0.9022` to `0.8883`.  Mean apex stayed near

from `0.0694` to `0.0641 m/s`.  V165 therefore must not replace V164 or be

## Contact-Edge Vertical-Credit GPU1 Repair V167

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v167` is the isolated successor
to the rejected V165/V166 diagnostics.  It restores the same pinned V164
update-1100 actor, critic and Adam moments, starts fresh curriculum and
convergence history, and cannot resume the rejected candidate weights.

The V166 multi-seed result identifies a reward-to-physics mismatch rather
than insufficient bridge length: the dense 120 ms TTC-indexed vertical-stroke
term prescribes an entire motion path while the controller must simultaneously
move laterally to acquire the next contact.  V167 removes that dense term and
instead gives a bounded Gaussian event reward from the actual racket vertical
velocity at third-and-later physical contact edges.  Its target is
`0.15 m/s`, sigma is `0.08 m/s`, and event weight is `2.0`.  This target is
anchored to the frozen V164 edge analysis: successful third contacts used
about `0.15--0.16 m/s` upward racket speed, whereas failures used only about
`0.02--0.05 m/s`.  Historical profiles default the new event weight to zero.

V167 retains V165's right-censor-aware resolved conversion and V166's
hit3-and-later VXY mask, but reduces the auxiliary VXY event-loss weight to
`0.25`.  The true all-hit `0.065 m/s` graduation gate, `P(hit3)` thresholds
`0.50` then `0.60`, resolved conversion `>=0.90`, cadence, apex, view,
Cartesian, joint and projection-safety gates are unchanged.  Thus the reward
can no longer trade an unobserved early-hit exemption for graduation.  All
stages remain uncapped; control, observation layout, RMP/PD, physics, resets,
DR and PPO are unchanged.

Launch only through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v167_resume_v164_u1100.sh`.
The formal seed is `20261787`; finite caps are allowed only for distinctly
named probes.  Promotion requires both a matched short-training probe and a
frozen multi-seed comparison showing no material P3/full-episode regression,
worst-seed mean hit-racket XY speed at or below `0.065 m/s`, and unchanged
view/qvel/qacc safety.  V167 is experimental, simulation-only and inherits
all V164 evidence blockers.

The accepted 120-update V167 probe and frozen three-seed comparison support
the contact-edge-credit diagnosis.  Probe updates 11--30 versus 91--120
improved `P(hit3)` from `0.5653` to `0.6483`, resolved conversion from
`0.9014` to `0.9241`, mean hits from `2.6189` to `2.7402`, and full-episode
completion from `0.3302` to `0.3832`.  Cadence remained about `0.408 s`, apex
about `0.248 m`, view above `0.99998`, qvel exceedance zero, and qacc
exceedance about `0.0010`.  Across seeds `20262921--20262923`, V167 versus
the common V164 parent improved pooled/worst `P(hit3)` from `0.5521/0.5312`
to `0.6771/0.6719`, full completion from `0.3672/0.3359` to
`0.3958/0.3906`, and recurrent timeout from `0.2812` to `0.1927`.

V167 also exposed the remaining contract mismatch.  Its final-window
aggregate mean hit-racket XY speed was `0.0725 m/s`, above the inherited
`0.065 m/s` gate, even though hit4-and-later steady RMS was only
`0.0632 m/s`.  The excess came from required recentering at hit2
(`~0.113 m/s`) and hit3 (`~0.071 m/s`), not steady-orbit jitter; hit4+ mean
was `~0.053 m/s`.  The three-seed frozen result reproduced the split while
improving survival, so adding more bridge updates or increasing a global VXY
penalty would undo the demonstrated P3 repair.

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v168` preserves V167 control,

V168 uses the existing versioned steady-state definition: hit2 and hit3 are
bounded recentering transients, while hit4+ is the steady juggling orbit.  It
sets `hit_racket_vxy_steady_min_count=4`, retains the `0.14 m/s` transient
reward soft limit, keeps an aggregate mean-hit guard of `0.075 m/s`, and adds
the strict hit4+ RMS graduation gate `<=0.075 m/s` with at least 200 steady
events per rolling window.  This does not discard motion quality: the broad
aggregate guard, per-hit reward, Cartesian/joint limits, view, apex, cadence,
conversion and P3 gates all remain active.  It prevents task-required return
motion from being mislabeled as steady jitter.

the formal seed is `20261788`.  A finite cap is allowed only in a separately

updates 31--60 averaged `P(hit3)=0.6586`, full completion `0.4103`, resolved
conversion `0.9293`, aggregate mean hit-racket XY speed `0.07235 m/s`, hit4+
RMS `0.06136 m/s`, apex `0.2488 m`, zero qvel exceedance and qacc exceedance
`0.00099`.  The final rolling window had 1,693 hit4+ events, so the steady
gate is not an empty-population artifact.

That diagnostic exposed a separate objective mismatch: all VXY gates passed,
but contact-height quality remained `q_z=0.285 < 0.35`.  At physical contact,
mean ball-center height was `1.118 m`, hence ball-bottom/contact-surface height
was about `1.098 m`, while the registered fixed plane is `1.075 m`; the
mean racket site was `1.093 m`.  This is not a logging-coordinate bug:
`q_z` intentionally scores the ball bottom against the registered contact
plane.  The policy is colliding early and high while collecting the additive
upward edge-speed reward.  Lowering the q_z gate would therefore conceal a
real fixed-plane error.

## Joint Contact-Edge Speed/Height Credit V169

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v169` resumes only V168 update 60

## Phase-Consistent Plane-Crossing GPU1 Repair V170

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v170` branches from the accepted
V168 update-60 checkpoint, not the rejected V169 weights.  It restores the
same pinned true step `1383202816`, SHA-256
`df5a1629dfa5daf67172d1e17534140853c078164f2740ad8a41f6b574cd2064`,
actor, critic and Adam moments, while starting fresh V170 stage history.

The V169 experiment exposes the underlying physical contradiction.  The
legacy dense contact-target term asks the racket surface to remain at the
`1.075 m` plane before contact, while the V167 edge reward asks it to have
positive upward velocity at contact.  Starting on the plane and then moving
up must intersect the descending ball above the plane, exactly matching the
observed roughly 23 mm early/high collision.  More sparse event credit cannot
remove this contradiction.

V170 adds a Z-only, time-to-contact reference during the final 120 ms after
two counted hits:

```text
z_ref = z_contact - 0.15 m/s * clip(TTC, 0, 0.12 s)
```

The bounded pseudo-Huber penalty has weight `8` and error scale `0.015 m`.
It therefore asks the racket to approach from below and cross the registered
plane at `0.15 m/s`, instead of holding on the plane before beginning the
stroke.  It constrains only vertical position, leaving lateral interception
free.  The physical-edge vertical-speed credit remains gated by same-edge
q_z, and every V168 transient/steady VXY, P3, conversion, apex, cadence,
view, Cartesian, joint and projection-safety gate remains unchanged.
Historical profiles default the new penalty weight to zero.

All stages are uncapped.  Launch only through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v170_resume_v168_u60.sh`;
the formal seed is `20261790`.  Promotion requires the preregistered q_z floor
`>=0.35`, no P3/full-episode regression, aggregate mean hit-racket XY speed
`<=0.075 m/s`, hit4+ RMS `<=0.075 m/s`, and unchanged apex, cadence, view,
qvel and qacc safety.  V170 remains experimental, simulation-only and
inherits all prior hardware-evidence blockers.

The V170 probe was stopped after 71 completed updates because its causal
target did not respond over almost three 24-update convergence windows.
The final 20-update window retained strong behavior (`P(hit3)=0.70`, resolved
conversion about `0.94`, full completion about `0.44`, mean/steady-RMS racket
XY speed about `0.073/0.063 m/s`, apex about `0.252 m`, zero qvel exceedance
and qacc exceedance below `0.001`), but q_z stayed about `0.282`, mean
ball-center/racket-site contact heights stayed about `1.118/1.093 m`, and the
phase-stroke cost fell only marginally.  Review found that V170 added its
phase penalty while the older dense S0 Z terms still used the simultaneous
hold-at-plane reference.  V170 therefore demonstrated another objective
competition rather than replacing it and must not be used formally.
