## Coupled Impact-Boundary GPU1 Repair V174

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v174` branches from the same clean
V168 update-60 checkpoint and restores actor, critic and Adam moments with
fresh stage history. It does not resume the negative V169--V173 policies and
does not add another bridge lesson.

The V173 root-cause audit showed that the method had incorrectly split one
mechanically coupled impact boundary into independent contact-height and
fixed-speed objectives. Across 433 recurrent contacts, incoming ball speed
was about `-1.85 m/s`, median effective restitution was `0.775`, and the
policy contacted around surface Z `1.103 m` with racket Vz `0.127 m/s`.
First contacts had the same incoming speed but occurred near `1.077 m` with
racket Vz `0.303 m/s`. For the registered `1.075 m` racket-surface plane,
ball radius and unchanged `1.33 m` target apex, the normal impact equation

```text
v_ball_out = (1 + e) * v_racket - e * v_ball_in
```

requires roughly `0.35 m/s`, not the fixed `0.15 m/s` inferred from the
selection-biased high-contact successes. A frozen full-task intervention
achieved surface Z `1.064--1.068 m`, racket Vz `0.272--0.341 m/s`, and q_z
`0.134--0.180`, proving that the current RMP and joint limits can execute the
boundary. Its `P(hit2)` collapse also proved that Z cannot be repaired alone:
XY tracking and racket tilt motion must be part of the same command.

V174 therefore computes, per lane, the required recurrent racket Vz from the
predicted incoming ball Vz, registered plane, target apex and empirical
effective restitution `0.775`, bounded to `0.20--0.50 m/s`. It uses the same
continuous 240 ms prepare/strike position path, beginning after one counted
hit. The command objective is evaluated after the Cartesian hard projection
with the current surface-point Jacobian and jointly scores:

- XY surface velocity toward the predicted contact target;
- phase-consistent surface Z velocity and Z tracking;
- zero roll/pitch angular velocity during impact preparation.

The physical-edge speed reward uses the pre-impact ball velocity from that
same edge and is multiplied by same-edge q_z. V174 disables both the legacy
fixed-`0.15 m/s` edge reward and warm-pose scalar command objective. Legacy
profiles default the new mode off and remain numerically unchanged.

All stages are uncapped. Launch only through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v174_resume_v168_u60.sh`;
the formal seed is `20261794`. A bounded mechanism probe must first show
causal improvement in post-projection task-twist cost, actual edge Vz and q_z
without losing `P(hit3)`, resolved conversion, lateral/tilt quality, apex,
view or safety. Higher return alone is not acceptance. V174 remains
experimental, simulation-only and inherits all hardware-evidence blockers.

The bounded 120-update V174 mechanism probe is negative and must not be
promoted. From its first to final 20-update windows, mean return changed
`-1.869 -> -3.041`, mean hits `2.614 -> 2.540`, `P(hit3)`
`0.591 -> 0.509`, resolved conversion `0.932 -> 0.894`, and q_z
`0.300 -> 0.313`. Physical ball-center/racket-site contact height remained
`1.117/1.092 m`. Although total task-twist cost fell `0.808 -> 0.788`, this
was entirely compensatory: XY cost fell `1.233 -> 1.169` and tilt cost fell
`0.348 -> 0.320`, while the required Z cost worsened `3.801 -> 3.887`.
V174's arithmetic mean therefore did not represent the conjunctive collision
boundary.

## From-Scratch Non-Compensable Impact GPU1 Course V175

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v175` is a new from-scratch
15-stage course. It must not restore a V168--V174 actor, critic, optimizer,
log standard deviation or curriculum history. A frozen full-task intervention
audit against V168 update 60 found that the action needed to enter the desired
impact boundary was a median `68.5--71.4` policy standard deviations away;
only `1.95--2.50%` of active samples were within 3 sigma. This is direct
evidence that trust-region PPO cannot discover the different hybrid stroke
from the converged high-contact limit cycle by local continuation.

V175 changes the method at its origin. The random actor sees the same
collision-derived fixed-plane impact law on its first clean airborne hit and
on every recurrent hit. The impact objective begins at `hit_count=0`, avoiding
an unobserved hit-count mode switch in the 80-D actor. It uses the empirical
restitution `0.775`, solves a bounded `0.20--0.50 m/s` racket Vz target from
incoming ball Vz and the `1.33 m` apex, and follows one continuous 210 ms
prepare/120 ms strike path. Legacy fixed-`0.15 m/s`, pre-hit launch,
warm-Jacobian command and smooth-stroke objectives are disabled.

The executable XY, Z and roll/pitch task-twist pseudo-Huber components are
aggregated by `max`, not mean. This makes the impact objective
non-compensable: improving XY or tilt cannot hide a failed Z stroke. Historical
profiles retain the default `mean` behavior and are numerically unchanged.
Resolved contact conversion, free-flight survival, stick/failed-hit penalties
and max-aggregated outcome constraints are active before recurrence is judged.

The course order is causal ability, not another continuation bridge: three
single-hit clean-airborne lessons, direct hit2 bridge/commit, direct hit3
bridge/commit, then the unchanged-domain V168 recurrent/workspace/horizon
tail. Every stage requires q_z `>=0.50` and the other four physical contact
quality components `>=0.35`, plus its direct hit, conversion, cadence, apex,
motion, view and safety gates. Every stage has `max_updates=None`.

Before formal training, run exactly one bounded first-stage method proof via
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v175_proof.sh` (seed
`20261795`, at most 260 updates). It must pass rolling and independent block
validation with `P(hit1)>=0.60`, resolved conversion `>=0.85`, q_z `>=0.50`,
the remaining quality components `>=0.35`, contact occupancy `<=0.03`, p95
contact duration `<=20 ms`, no hard-set regression, and a causal improvement
in Z task-twist/contact height. If it fails, do not create a parameter-tuned
successor; the next method must provide a demonstrated/analytic stroke or a
nonlocal exploration mechanism.

Only after that proof passes may the uncapped formal course start through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v175_from_scratch.sh`
(seed `20261796`) in `pp_gpu1`. V175 remains experimental, simulation-only and
inherits every prior RMP/PD, camera and physical-ball evidence blocker.

The bounded V175 proof is negative and the formal launcher is therefore
fail-closed. It completed all 260 updates without graduating. From the first
to the final 20-update windows, mean hits improved `0.002 -> 0.863` and
resolved edge-to-hit conversion improved to `0.863`; q_z, q_pose, q_omega and
q_offset also passed their preregistered floors. The sole persistent physical
quality failure was q_vxy `0.078 < 0.35` (final convergence value `0.077`). A
frozen 64-environment replay measured mean hit racket XY speed `0.109 m/s`;
all 16 traced contact edges had racket world-Y velocity between
`-0.117` and `-0.099 m/s`. Thus V175 repaired the local-exploration failure
and learned a reliable first collision, but selected a systematic lateral
sweep rather than a stable contact.

This failure is not a request for V176 reward tuning. The max aggregation is
non-compensable only among commanded XY/Z/tilt errors at the same active time;
the total PPO return still trades delayed physical quality against hit,
survival and failure-avoidance reward. Its dense signal measures the
post-projection commanded task twist, while the gate measures the delayed
RMP/plant's actual racket twist. In a representative trace, physical contact
occurred at episode step 36 and was not resolved as a confirmed hit until step
103. No immediate contact-edge racket-vxy penalty was active. The
instantaneous proportional XY reference also has no acceleration/braking
preview: actual XY speed rose from `0.050 m/s` at TTC `0.15--0.22 s` to
`0.203 m/s` at TTC `0.05--0.10 s`, then remained `0.152 m/s` during the final
`5--50 ms`, although the target was only `0.095 m/s`.

The method-level root cause is therefore the absence of a feasibility-
generating, plant-aware contact trajectory and an optimizer-level constraint
on actual edge state. A hard graduation gate cannot repair a scalar objective
after optimization. The next admissible experiment must first demonstrate
one of: (1) analytic/demonstrated dynamically feasible stroke initialization,
(2) a trajectory/action parameterization or safety projection that
structurally bounds actual contact XY speed, or (3) constrained RL with a
separate constraint critic/dual variable. It must not be another bridge or
scalar-weight sweep. Full evidence is recorded in
`outputs/rl_sim/gpu1_v175_postmortem_20260920/ROOT_CAUSE_REPORT.md`.

## Actual-Plant Constrained GPU1 Continuation V176

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v176` is a continuation-only
method successor to the negative V175 proof. It resumes exactly the V175
update-260 checkpoint (step `34078720`, SHA-256
`da301e766c98fd873a5424676a80f74cdad56ca2e8ca28066ed8f90df0830afd`),
including the 80-D actor, 401-D reward critic and Adam moments. It starts
fresh stage/convergence history and appends zero-output cost-value heads plus
dual variables; resetting the actor, reward critic or optimizer is forbidden.

The feasibility premise is measured rather than assumed. The existing
non-learning V4 witness under the same recovered-RMP/PD and hard joint limits
produced two quality contacts with racket VXY `0.02139/0.03355 m/s` and zero
qvel/qacc exceedance. It does not prove long-horizon juggling, but it rules out
the claim that the V175 `0.109 m/s` sweep is forced by this plant or by the
joint limits. V176 does not deploy that witness or add a second planner.

V176 copies all 15 V175 stage configurations byte-for-byte. It changes only
the PPO optimization problem through `--cmdp-cost-mode
fixed_contact_quality`. Six independently predicted costs are used:

1. measured contact-point VXY above a finite-braking envelope during the last
   `0.12 s` before predicted contact;
2. immediate physical-edge q_z shortfall;
3. immediate physical-edge q_pose shortfall;
4. immediate physical-edge q_vxy shortfall;
5. immediate physical-edge q_omega shortfall;
6. immediate physical-edge q_offset shortfall.

The braking envelope is
`0.05 m/s + 1.0 m/s^2 * max(TTC - 0.025 s, 0)`. The 25 ms latency allowance
is the registered 18--19 ms RMP output delay plus one 5 ms policy interval,
rounded upward. Excess is normalized by `0.05 m/s`. Contact floors remain
exactly `(0.50,0.35,0.35,0.35,0.35)`. Each dual limit is `0.05`; initial
duals are `(0.50,0.10,0.10,0.50,0.10,0.10)`, cost GAE lambda is `0.97`, dual
learning rate is `0.05`, and dual maximum is `4.0`. Dual observations are
means over active braking/contact samples, not all rollout steps, so rare
contact violations cannot be diluted by no-event time. Cost GAE still carries
the physical violation backward to causal actions. Historical V65 terminal
CMDP behavior and channel identities are unchanged.

The immediate edge metrics use the already cached physical-contact snapshot.
They do not wait roughly 335 ms for V175's pending contact to resolve, and the
approach cost evaluates delayed plant output (`racket_contact_point_vxy`), not
the post-projection command target. This repairs the measurement, timing and
optimizer layers together while leaving reward, control stack, observations,
physics, resets and gates unchanged.

Run exactly one bounded 180-update mechanism proof with
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v176_cmdp_proof.sh`.
The bound covers the unchanged Stage-1 `min_updates=160` plus its 16-update
convergence hold (earliest possible graduation is update 175); the prior
120-update bound was structurally incapable of invoking block validation.
Acceptance requires Stage 1 to pass both rolling and independent block gates:
hit1 `>=0.60`, resolved conversion `>=0.85`, q_z `>=0.50`, the remaining
quality components `>=0.35`, occupancy `<=0.03`, p95 contact duration
`<=20 ms`, and no hard-set regression. The approach-vxy and q_vxy costs/duals
must be finite and show causal reduction. A failed proof ends this method;
there is no parameter sweep or repeat.

Only a positive machine-readable acceptance report permits the uncapped
formal launcher
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v176_cmdp_resume_v175.sh`
in `pp_gpu1`. V176 is experimental, simulation-only and inherits all physical
camera, ball-outcome and formal RMP/PD coverage blockers.

## Atomic Single-Impact GPU0 Continuation V177

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v177` supersedes only the stopped
V163 GPU0 `v163_g0_arrived_hit_bridge` run. It restores the last clean
update-2500 archive at true step `5760155648`, SHA-256
`46fa8751bbb1b6e99b08ab8de72478e9c96ffb565440cc32f760aef20bdbea10`,
including the 80-D actor, 401-D critic and Adam moments, and starts fresh V177
stage/convergence history. It rejects from-scratch launch, another source
identity, optimizer/critic reset, curriculum-history migration, and an update
cap.

V177 repairs the physical event contract rather than adding another proxy
bridge. A raw racket-ball `in_contact` rising edge, the cached racket/contact
state, and the resulting launch must belong to one atomic impact. If that
impact does not reach the qualified launch boundary within 150 ms, the episode
terminates as a failed hit. If the ball separates far and long enough to
re-arm and then contacts the racket again while the first impact is pending,
the episode terminates as a pending-hit recontact. The second impact can never
provide outgoing velocity while inheriting the first impact's low VXY/omega,
position or pose. Conversion uses raw physical edges, while logical and raw
edges, timeout failure and pending recontact remain separately logged. Legacy
profiles retain their historical merged-pending behavior by default.

The inherited scalar smooth-stroke target is removed. It started only 80 ms
before predicted contact while the measured RMP/PD response consumed roughly
50--65 ms, leaving the first physical impact almost passive. V177 instead
uses the existing continuous phase stroke with a 210 ms preparation interval
and 120 ms impact lead, plus the registered collision-consistent surface-twist
target (`e_eff=0.775`, required racket Vz bounded to `0.20--0.50 m/s`). The
task-twist cost uses worst-component aggregation and an immediate first-edge
Vz reward; vertical stationary S0 shaping remains suppressed during the
stroke. Control, actor/critic observation layouts, bounded-reference RMP/PD,
physics, DR, reset support, Cartesian hard constraints and PPO settings remain
the V163 contract.

The first lesson uses the unchanged V163 local arrived-hit support, but gates
true single-impact hit1 and raw-edge conversion before the unchanged physical
commit. Every later V163 joint/workspace/horizon lesson is retained in order
with the same atomic event and plant-timing contract. All ten stages are
uncapped. Launch only through
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v177_resume_v163_u2500.sh`.
V177 remains experimental and simulation-only and inherits every V163
real-camera, replacement-ball outcome and formal RMP/PD evidence blocker.

and starts at `v178_g1_true_hit2_bridge`. The actor, reward critic, log
standard deviation, their Adam moments and the global Adam step are preserved
exactly. Because the cost target semantics change, only the six-channel cost
critic, its Adam leaves and the six dual variables are reset. V178 rejects a
different source, observation migration, task critic/optimizer reset,
curriculum-history migration on the initial resume, or an update cap in the
formal run.

The V176 failure was an optimizer-contract mismatch, not insufficient bridge
difficulty. V176 evaluated its five contact-quality constraints on every raw
physical edge, including contacts that never produced a qualified upward
launch, while graduation evaluated quality only on counted, rewardable hits.
Its normalized positive-shortfall cost with a `0.05` limit was also much
stricter than the declared mean-quality gate. Consequently the q_z dual could
keep rising after every graduation quality gate already passed. The optimizer
then improved clean-looking failed contacts: contact-edge q_z rose and its
shortfall fell while edge-to-hit conversion, hit1 and hit2 collapsed. This
explains why lowering a dual, changing another reward, or inserting another
course bridge would treat the symptom while preserving the causal conflict.

V178 copies all 15 V176 stage configurations byte-for-byte and changes only
the PPO cost contract through `--cmdp-cost-mode
fixed_contact_gate_aligned`. The approach-VXY channel remains the same
immediate, delayed-plant braking envelope. Each contact-quality channel is
active only on `rewardable_hit`, and consumes the same
`fixed_contact_q_{z,pose,vxy,omega,offset}_sum` event values used by the
rolling and block graduation gates. Its event cost is exactly `1-q`, with
limits `(0.50,0.65,0.65,0.65,0.65)` for quality floors
`(0.50,0.35,0.35,0.35,0.35)`. Therefore each dual feasibility condition
`mean(cost) <= limit` is algebraically identical to the corresponding
graduation condition `mean(q) >= floor`. Cost GAE still propagates a resolved
successful-contact cost backward to its causal actions; failed contacts are
penalized by the unchanged failed-hit/task objective and cannot masquerade as
quality successes. All initial duals are zero because the pinned source
already passed the declared quality gates.

Run exactly one bounded 80-update causal proof with
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v178_gate_aligned_proof.sh`.
Against the pinned source and V176's first 80 Stage-4 updates, its final
24-update window must have hit1 `>=0.90`, hit2 `>=0.25`, resolved conversion
`>=0.90`, q_z `>=0.50`, each other contact component `>=0.35`, occupancy
`<=0.03`, p95 contact duration `<=20 ms`, finite KL/explained variance and no
hard-set regression. This is one preregistered mechanism test, not a parameter
sweep. A negative result requires returning to the causal model, not repeated
threshold/reward edits.

Only a positive machine-readable acceptance report permits the uncapped
formal launcher
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v178_gate_aligned_resume_v176_u34.sh`
in `pp_gpu1`. V178 is experimental, simulation-only and inherits all physical
camera, replacement-ball outcome and formal RMP/PD coverage blockers.

## Executable Arrival-to-Impact GPU0 Continuation V179

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v179` supersedes only the stopped
V177 run at global/stage update `7680`, true step `6766788608`, checkpoint
SHA-256 `795a266f6dc0d183c0c7dc59a93752c24dcc1132974ff505b58f94fc3cd36c09`.
It restores the 80-D actor, 401-D critic, log standard deviation, Adam moments
and global optimizer step, but deliberately starts fresh V179 stage and
convergence history at `v179_g0_executable_single_impact_bridge`. It rejects
from-scratch launch, another source identity, optimizer/critic reset,
curriculum-history migration and any formal update cap.

The V177 plateau was not a workspace-reachability failure. The reset placed
the falling ball only `80--100 ms` from contact, inside a reference whose
preparation began `210 ms` before contact and whose upward strike began
`120 ms` before contact. At the same observed TTC the arrival objective asked
the racket to remain on the contact plane while the stroke reference asked it
to be `16--20 mm` below it. With the measured `50--65 ms` RMP/PD response,
there was no action history from which the actor could generate the required
upward edge velocity. This caused a nearly passive first impact even when XY,
pose and workspace feasibility were acceptable.

V179 changes the causal episode history, not task difficulty. Every falling
reset and arrived-hit sample starts at `0.28--0.36 s` TTC. The policy first
gets a real arrival interval, is scored for holding the contact pose during
`0.24--0.28 s`, and then follows one continuous `0.24 s` down/up stroke with
`0.12 s` impact lead. The equality `prepare = 2 * lead` makes the two position
branches meet continuously. A new graduation metric scores the actual cached
first-edge racket Vz against the collision-derived target; contact alone can
no longer pass. The first bridge/commit require edge-Vz score `>=0.50/0.60`
as well as arrival/hold, conversion, return, view and hard-safety gates. The
complete ten-stage V177 course remains in order and every stage is uncapped.
Control, observations, RMP/PD, physics, DR and Cartesian constraints are
unchanged.

Run one bounded 60-update proof through
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v179_proof_resume_v177_u7680.sh`.
Only a positive machine-readable acceptance report permits the uncapped
formal launcher
`run_gpu0_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v179_resume_v177_u7680.sh`.
V179 remains experimental, simulation-only and inherits all V177 evidence
blockers.

## Target-Aligned Recurrent GPU1 Continuation V180

`fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v180` supersedes only the stopped
V178 run at global/stage update `3500`, true step `970719232`, checkpoint
SHA-256 `6249c51af2a7c3459374d839d487da3ea081c8cdd858cc67eaa395afb91b3d10`.
It restores the 80-D actor, 401-D reward critic, log standard deviation, task
Adam moments and global optimizer step. Because the constrained objective
changes, only the old six cost heads, their Adam leaves and dual state are
replaced once by a reviewed five-channel cost state. Initial and same-profile
resume contracts are distinct and fail closed.

The V178 plateau was caused by inconsistent task definitions. The return
objective asked for a bounded step from the actual contact point toward the
workspace center, while its `5 cm` next-contact penalty and graduation gate
measured distance to the random episode anchor. As workspace support widened,
the same physical return could be rewarded by one target and rejected by the
other. In addition, the optimizer constrained five marginal mean quality
values, while graduation required one simultaneous seven-condition event;
the duals could be feasible even when the probability of a genuinely usable
second hit approached zero. First-hit successes then concealed failure of the
recurrent controller.

V180 makes reward, telemetry, rolling/block graduation and constraints use
the same bounded workspace-center next-contact target. Its five CMDP channels
are delayed-plant approach-VXY excess, joint all-ready failure on all
rewardable hits, joint all-ready failure on recurrent hits, target error on
all rewardable hits, and target error on recurrent hits. The recurrent event
population is explicitly `hit_count >= 2`; both its joint-ready probability
and target error have separate stage gates. The old marginal-quality CMDP is
not migrated. All 15 V178 stages remain in order and uncapped; control,
observations, physics, reset support, reward weights and task PPO settings are
otherwise unchanged.

Run one bounded 80-update proof through
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v180_proof_resume_v178_u3500.sh`.
Only a positive machine-readable acceptance report permits the uncapped
formal launcher
`run_gpu1_fixed_contact_plane_vision_robust_qvel_rmp_v180_resume_v178_u3500.sh`.
The current launcher additionally requires the active V181 progress CSV to
prove at least 50 new `1024 x 128` optimizer updates beyond step `6766788608`;
the ordering constraint is therefore executable rather than procedural text.
V180 remains experimental, simulation-only and inherits all V178 physical
evidence blockers.

## Simplified Fixed-Plane From-Scratch V1

The current opt-in simplification is one method with two independent run
identities:

- `fixed_plane_minimal_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v1`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_minimal_qvel_rmp_v1.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_minimal_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v1`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_minimal_qvel_rmp_v1.sh`.

Both profiles must start from random initialization. They must reject a
checkpoint/curriculum resume, optimizer or critic reset, CMDP, a mass interval
other than `[0.0039, 0.0041] kg`, a stacked actuator/filter/planner path, and
ad-hoc launcher arguments. GPU0 and GPU1 use byte-equivalent method configs
apart from the stage identity; device and seed provide independent repeats.

The preserved control boundary is the reviewed 80-D fixed-contact actor and
7-D QVEL action at 200 Hz, measured `q/dq`, persistent bounded `q_ref`, hard
Cartesian reference projection, recovered RMP `recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2` at
1 kHz, XML PD and native MJX contact. Fixed base and the exact 4.0 g singleton
ball override remain. There is no actuator filter, inverse compensation,
tracking planner, second controller or post-RMP simulated delay.

V1 deliberately removes the experimental complexity accumulated by the
V146--V181 continuations and by the unlaunched plant-aware residual draft:

- the simulation high-ball history predictor is disabled, and noiseless
  simulation ball state is sampled directly at 200 Hz;
- the next contact target is always a step from the actual contact point
  toward workspace center, capped at `0.050 m`; episode-anchor return is not
  a selectable V1 objective;
- absolute target apex is provisionally fixed at the higher retained value
  `1.40 m`, with a `1.34--1.46 m` graduation band pending a separate height
  decision;
- CMDP cost critics, dual variables and migration are prohibited;
- analytic stroke phases, impact-task-twist/edge-Vz teachers, the 110-D
  nominal-plus-residual action path, scripted launch and reset mixtures are
  absent;
- stochastic contact, RMP/PD, mount, observation and missed-publication DR
  are absent. `domain_randomization=True` exists only to replace the legacy
  XML ball with the exact `0.004 kg` singleton and consistent inertia.

The scalar reward has only the fixed-contact building blocks: continuous
contact-readiness component scores, one bounded confirmed-hit credit, smooth
contact quality, the joint apex/centerward-return score, post-hit survival,
action magnitude/delta regularization and explicit failed-impact penalty.
There is no `all-ready` conjunction reward, adaptive event bundle, completion
bonus, phase teacher or recurrent combo reward. Physical quality components,
raw edge conversion, apex, next-target error, motion and hard-safety values
remain diagnostics and graduation guardrails rather than CMDP channels.

The complete curriculum contains exactly four uncapped, same-domain lessons:

1. `center_single`: 1 s, centered falling-contact reset, terminate after one
   confirmed hit;
2. `center_recurrent`: 3 s, same centered task without hit termination;
3. `local_recurrent`: 3 s, expand only to the local XY support;
4. `full_workspace_recurrent`: 6 s, expand only to the full registered XY
   support and require recurrent survival.

Every stage uses one falling-contact reset family, a physically realizable
`0.28--0.36 s` reset-to-contact interval, the same reward/control/physics and
self-domain block validation. No stage may force advancement at an update cap.
The launchers are preflight-only unless the corresponding GPU confirmation
and incomplete-evidence acknowledgement are set. Repository implementation,
syntax and CPU smoke checks are not convergence evidence; no GPU training is
authorized or started by this registration alone.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V1

The goal-conditioned successor to the minimal ablation is registered as two
independent random-initialization runs:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v1`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v1.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v1`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v1.sh`.

Both use the same 200 Hz direct measured bounded-QVEL -> recovered-RMP
`recovered_rmp_rmpmd_v2` -> XML-PD boundary, fixed base, native contact and
exact 4.0 g ball as the minimal V1 course. They must start from scratch and
reject CMDP, checkpoint/curriculum resume, stacked control paths, an incorrect
mass interval, or a missing/failed reachability report. GPU identity and seed
are the only intended differences between the two courses.

The fixed racket contact surface is `z=1.025 m`, using the repaired finite-mesh
surface convention (local X is the 1 mm half-thickness axis). The actor is 96-D:
the preserved 80-D fixed-contact prefix plus desired post-impact ball velocity,
desired racket contact velocity, absolute desired apex, measured
`dq(t)-dq(t-1)`, ball-observation age and the launch-to-steady progress scalar.
Actual racket linear and angular velocities remain present in the 80-D prefix.
There is no high-ball predictor, phase/impact teacher, CMDP, scripted stroke,
actuator filter, inverse compensation, second planner or broad stochastic DR.

One actor-visible goal schedule controls geometry, observation, hit
confirmation and reward. Before any confirmed hit the target apex is `1.10 m`;
after one it is `1.275 m`; after two it is the nominal `1.45 m` steady orbit.
The hit that changes the schedule is rewarded against its pre-contact goal, so
launch and steady objectives are never active on the same event. Hit-quality
and survival confirmation floors are respectively 0.025 m and 0.050 m below
the active target, with explicit clearance floors above the contact center.
This replaces the inherited fixed 0.23 m relative-height gate, which otherwise
rejects the deliberately low launch and prevents the transition.

The four uncapped lessons are placed-ball launch, centered two-hit transition,
centered steady juggling, and local steady juggling over only `+/-0.05 m` X by
`+/-0.04 m` Y. Reset places a stationary ball 1 mm above the racket; there is
no kinematic hold or scripted launch. Every next-contact target moves at most
0.050 m toward workspace center and never returns to an episode anchor.

The required no-learning GPU reachability evidence is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v1_reachability_audited_20260921/reachability_report.json`.
It passed reset geometry, the 1.10 m placed-ball launch, and the separate
1.45 m descending-orbit return through the exact RMP/PD stack. Two launch
witnesses reached predicted apex `1.1033--1.1142 m`; three steady witnesses
reached `1.4352--1.4646 m`. A steady witness stayed inside the registered
measured surface-Z range (`1.00692--1.11903 m`), used at most 29.9% of joint
velocity limits, and had 0.794% joint-sample acceleration exceedance with a
1.0043 maximum ratio. The report records physical GPU1 UUID and hashes of the
screen, goal contract, environment and trainer; the trainer recomputes those
hashes and every lane gate before launch. This is reachability evidence, not learned-policy
convergence or hardware coverage. No PPO run is started by this registration.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V2

V1 remains immutable. Its repaired successors are independent random-start
courses:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v2`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v2.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v2`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v2.sh`.

V2 preserves the 96-D actor, 1.025 m contact plane, 1.10 -> 1.275 -> 1.45 m
confirmed-hit goal schedule, exact 4.0 g nominal ball, direct simulated ball
state, bounded centerward next-contact target, Cartesian projection and the
single measured-QVEL -> recovered-RMP -> XML-PD stack. It still has no
high-ball predictor, TTC/impact teacher, CMDP, actuator filter, second planner
or broad DR.

The changes repair four V1 convergence blockers. The physical hit debounce is
0.16 s, below the approximately 0.212 s return period of the 1.10 m launch.
The placed ball is held racket-relative for 0.12 s while policy actions remain
live, giving the measured RMP/PD loop time to form its own launch rather than
injecting a scripted stroke. Contact-quality credit blends its weighted mean
and weakest component equally; positive event credit is likewise gated by
contact and return joint quality. The previously computed but discarded
task-aligned cadence, racket-horizontal-speed, full-angular-speed, plane and
flatness terms are enabled with a bounded 65% event-penalty budget; the
inherited fixed-lift auxiliary is zeroed because the actor-visible apex target
already supplies the phase-correct objective.

The five uncapped lessons are placed launch, centered two-hit transition,
centered steady juggling, a `+/-0.025 m` X by `+/-0.020 m` Y bridge, and the
final `+/-0.050 m` X by `+/-0.040 m` Y task. Stage 2 uses the physically
compatible 0.16--0.28 s launch cadence; steady lessons use 0.46--0.64 s around
0.575 s. Frozen exact-bin gates require three hits in the bridge and six hits
in the final workspace. Validation now computes and transactionally protects
the six-hit per-bin rate instead of raising on the registered V1/V2 gate.
Every lesson rejects joint-velocity exceedance and limits joint-acceleration
exceedance to 2%.

Both courses remain from-scratch, experimental and simulation-only. They
require a version-matched, hashed GPU reachability report and the same mass and
RMP-output evidence as V1. Reachability and bounded PPO-smoke evidence are
recorded separately; neither is full curriculum convergence or hardware
coverage.

The 2026-09-21 bounded learnability experiments reject V2 as the course to
promote. A 240-update GPU1 random-start run learned a valid deterministic
one-hit launch (`256/256` first hits), but stochastic training remained near
`0.395` hits/episode against the registered `0.70` gate. Its deterministic
mean still contacted with `0.168 m/s` racket XY speed against the `0.080 m/s`
gate. A separate from-scratch `max_log_std=-1.0` run reached only about
`0.486` rolling hit probability by update 120 and therefore showed that a
global low-variance policy starves early discovery rather than repairing it.
These are negative V2 results; they do not authorize weakening the final
physical-quality target.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V3

V1 and V2 remain immutable. Their experimental V3 successors are:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v3`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v3.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v3`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v3.sh`.

V3 changes no observation, reset, physics, ball/contact parameter, Cartesian
constraint, action meaning, bounded-reference equation or RMP/PD setting. It
splits V2's first lesson into two same-domain lessons. `launch_acquisition`
keeps the unconstrained training exploration and uses an evidence-backed
`0.35` stochastic first-hit handoff gate. `launch_precision` then applies a
stage-local `max_log_std=-1.0`, restores the original `0.080/0.120 m/s`
mean/RMS racket-XY gates, and raises both the dense approach and hit-event
racket-XY penalty weights to `2.0`; its bounded event-penalty budget is 90%.
Every later lesson retains that exploration ceiling and quality reward. A CLI
ceiling can only make the stage ceiling stricter, never weaken it. Existing
profiles have no stage-local exploration semantics.

The resulting six uncapped lessons are launch acquisition, launch precision,
two-hit transition, centered steady juggling, local XY bridge and final local
steady juggling. Advancement remains convergence- and block-validation-based;
there is no forced update cap. V3 requires a schema-V3 hashed GPU reachability
report even though its physical reachability contract is intentionally
identical to V2. Frozen-log-std A/B, reachability and bounded course-switch
tests are diagnostic evidence only. Full six-stage, multi-seed convergence is
still required before V3 can be called converged, released, or deployable.

### V3 repair and bounded convergence evidence (2026-09-21)

The first V3 formal-gate diagnostic exposed two additional fail-closed
contract defects. First, the acquisition lesson was still using the precision
lesson's five `0.30` contact-quality floors and `1.130 m` apex ceiling. The
learned stochastic launch reached the intended `0.35` hit handoff but missed
only horizontal-velocity quality (`0.1891 < 0.20`) and the apex ceiling by
about 1.4 mm. V3 acquisition alone now uses bridge-quality floors
`[0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.20, 0.20]` and a `1.135 m` ceiling. Precision and all
later lessons retain their stricter gates.

Second, generic reset-bucket validation treated a fixed center reset as
missing evidence because none of its nine reset metadata fields varied. The
validator now distinguishes three states: no reset fields present fails
closed; fields present and varying require the existing per-bin/CVaR gates;
fields present but constant are a single aggregate reset population and pass
the bucket partition gate vacuously while all aggregate physical gates remain
mandatory. The block at update 131 before this repair had mean hits `0.3976`
and passed its physical gates, but was rejected only by that false bucket
failure. A regression test protects constant-support pass and missing-field
failure separately.

The final one-seed, reduced-size GPU1 first-lesson run is
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v3_gpu1_s1_bucket_gatefix_seed20262302_20260921`.
It used 256 environments, 64 rollout steps, two PPO epochs and the normal
independent 256-lane/1200-step stochastic block. It converged at update 127 /
true step 2,080,768. Rolling mean hits/hit1 were `0.3751/0.3753`; rolling
mean/RMS hit-racket XY speed were `0.1399/0.1612 m/s`; mean absolute apex was
`1.13038 m`. The independent block passed with mean hits/hit1
`0.4043/0.4043`, mean/RMS hit-racket XY speed `0.1405/0.1626 m/s`, apex
`1.13016 m`, zero QVEL exceedance and `0.000527` QACC exceedance. It reported
nine reset fields present, zero varying fields and a passing reset-bucket
contract. This proves that the repaired acquisition lesson and advancement
path are executable for this seed; it does not prove the five subsequent
lessons or the formal 1024x128 launcher converge.

The launchers now reference version-matched reports generated from final
source hashes:

- V1: `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v1_reachability_bucket_gatefix_retry_20260921`;
- V2: `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v2_reachability_bucket_gatefix_20260921`;
- V3: `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v3_reachability_bucket_gatefix_20260921`.

All three reports passed launch and steady probes on CUDA. The first V1
attempt under the same source hash failed its launch lane screen and is
preserved as negative numerical-sensitivity evidence; the fixed-seed retry
passed with three launch and three steady witnesses. Reachability remains a
preflight witness, not learned convergence or hardware coverage. The relevant
27 V1/V2/V3/ball-frame regression tests passed. V3 remains experimental and
simulation-only until all six lessons pass independent validation across
multiple seeds and the unresolved RMP/PD, camera and ball-outcome evidence
gates are closed.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V4 (Evidence-Blocked)

V1--V3 remain immutable. Their opt-in V4 successors are:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v4`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v4.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v4`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v4.sh`.

V4 repairs the V3 Stage-2 reward/gate mismatch and the direct two-hit to
six-second steady-course cliff without changing the 96-D actor observation,
bounded measured-QVEL reference, recovered RMP/PD, fixed-base 4.0 g physics,
reset geometry, apex route or final workspace. Confirmed-hit event credit in
Stages 2--8 is gated entirely by the weakest contact/return component; the
event-penalty budget is 98%, and approach/contact racket-XY penalty weights
are both 2.0. Stage 1 remains the proven stochastic acquisition lesson.
Stages 2--3 cap policy log standard deviation at -1.5, the explicit three-hit
lesson uses -1.75, and recurrent lessons use -2.0. Stage 1 uses stochastic
independent validation; Stages 2--8 validate the deterministic policy mean.

The resulting eight uncapped lessons are launch acquisition, launch
precision, two-hit transition, explicit three-hit steady entry, a
three-second center steady bridge, center steady, local XY bridge and final
local steady. This avoids asking a two-hit policy to immediately satisfy a
six-second 1.45 m orbit. The CLI and validation-runtime cache resolve the
validation policy per stage; historical profiles with no stage override keep
their original global validation semantics.

V4 also tightens preflight evidence. The steady probe uses the final steady
stage rather than the launch-stage termination contract. It records only the
first physical contact and first confirmed hit, excludes post-termination
steps from safety fractions, records raw edge ball/racket Z and VZ, and tests
the full `3 x 3` local XY grid. The trainer recomputes every cell from lane
apex, joint safety, target XY and all five same-event contact components at
`q >= 0.45`; it does not trust report-level pass flags.

The final fixed-seed GPU1 report is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v4_quality_reachability_20260922/reachability_report.json`.
It uses the final source hashes and is deliberately negative: placed-ball
launch is reachable, but all nine steady quality cells fail. All 1,728 steady
lanes produced a physical contact edge, four became confirmed returns and one
had an apex inside 1.425--1.475 m. The four confirmed returns passed pose,
racket-VXY, angular-speed and offset quality at 0.45, but none passed q_z.
The best apex-compatible event had apex `1.469 m`, racket VXY `0.0325 m/s`
and quality approximately `[0.0022, 0.6025, 0.8100, 0.9914, 0.9929]`; its
surface contact was `1.0524 m`, 27.4 mm above the 1.025 m target. Stronger
height compensation removed the usable outgoing impulse instead of producing
a joint-quality witness.

The V4 launcher therefore remains fail-closed and no long PPO run is
authorized or started. V4 is useful reviewed code and negative mechanism
evidence, not a converged course. The next method change must provide a
dynamically feasible plant-aware stroke or another demonstrated mechanism
that jointly satisfies fixed-plane height and outgoing impulse while retaining
low lateral/rotational contact motion; another scalar reward or gain sweep is
not sufficient.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V5 (Directional Small Workspace)

V4 and its failed wide-workspace evidence remain immutable. The opt-in V5
successors are:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v5`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v5.sh`;

  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v5.sh`.

V5 preserves all eight V4 lessons, the 96-D actor and asymmetric critic,
bounded measured-QVEL reference, recovered RMP/PD, fixed-base 4.0 g physics,
reset/launch/apex route, reward, PPO settings and deterministic-validation
semantics. It changes only the last two episode-target supports because the
strict V4 screen demonstrated that the symmetric `+/-0.05 m` by `+/-0.04 m`
workspace contains fixed-pose cells that cannot jointly meet contact height,
pose, horizontal speed, angular speed, centering, apex and joint-safety gates.
Stage 7 uses X `[0, 0.003125] m` and Y `[-0.01, 0] m`; Stage 8 uses X
`[0, 0.00625] m` and Y `[-0.02, 0] m`. Both remain two-dimensional and include
the nominal workspace center `(0, 0)`, so the existing at-most-5-cm
centerward next-contact target is unchanged.

The V5 strict preflight grid is X `{0, 0.003125, 0.00625} m` by Y
`{-0.02, -0.01, 0} m`. The exploratory fixed-seed GPU0 report
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v4_quality_reachability_20260922/reachability_report_attempt26_strict_reachable_workspace_gpu0.json`
passed all nine cells with 29 same-event witnesses. Across those witnesses,
QVEL and QACC exceed fractions were both zero, maximum QVEL utilization was
`0.3183`, maximum diagnostic QACC ratio was `0.9152`, and the minimum five
contact-quality components were approximately
`[0.6291, 0.7184, 0.4530, 0.5346, 0.8110]`. This exploration report predates
the V5 trainer hash and is not a launch credential. The launcher accepts only
the version-5 schema regenerated from final source hashes under
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v5_reachability_20260922/reachability_report.json`.

V5 remains experimental and simulation-only. A passing reachability report
proves only one-contact action-space/plant feasibility. It does not prove PPO
convergence, multi-impact contraction, Sim2Real coverage, or hardware safety.
Formal training uses 1024 environments and starts from random initialization;
all eight stages must pass rolling and independent validation without forced
advancement before the method can be called converged.

The final version-5 reachability credential is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v5_reachability_20260922/reachability_report.json`
(SHA-256
`2794b9eac721b3a957a56cecd9fc9d09d6cd64c4c9a4a309c67d08e1f2fba871`).
Its recomputed `3 x 3` directional grid passed all nine cells with 34
same-event witnesses and zero winner QVEL/QACC exceedance. A one-update,
1024-environment smoke run also completed before formal launch.

The stopped GPU0 formal run is
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v5_gpu0_formal_seed20262501_20260922_054939`
(offline W&B ID `eg7akfpp`). It uses 1024 environments and seed `20262501`.
Stage 1 completed at global update 111 without forced advancement: its
independent 6,914-episode block measured mean hits and hit-1 rate `0.97946`,
mean hit-racket XY speed `0.04701 m/s`, mean absolute apex `1.11508 m`, and
contact-edge-to-hit conversion `0.97946`; every enabled block-validation gate
passed. Stages 2 and 3 subsequently passed after 115 and 203 updates.

The run was stopped in Stage 4,
`fplc_v5_gpu0_s4_three_hit_steady_entry`, after 2,773 Stage-4 updates (3,202
global updates and 419,692,544 environment steps). Stage-4 mean hits reached
exactly `2.000`, but `hit3_rate` was exactly zero in every update and the
convergence hold remained `0/24`. Frozen deterministic screening of the
Stage-3 final actor, five Stage-4 archives, best and last checkpoints produced
exactly two hits in all cases. The representative third physical contact had
incoming ball vertical velocity `-2.842 m/s` but downward racket velocity
`-0.238 m/s`; it launched the ball to only about `1.144 m`, after which the
racket crossed the `1.002 m` lower Z boundary.

The review found a course discontinuity because Stage 3 terminates before the
actor ever acts from `hit_count == 2`, no active recurrent vertical-stroke
credit despite the actor-visible contact-velocity target, an inherited
workspace-penalty flag that leaves racket-Z exits unpenalized, a Stage-4
cadence lower bound incompatible with the launch transition, and entropy
collapse from `-5.5` to about `-13.6`. The full evidence and required V6
changes are recorded in
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v5_stage4_plateau_review_20260922/PLATEAU_ROOT_CAUSE_REPORT.md`.
V5 is therefore a negative multi-impact result and must not be resumed or
represented as converged. The GPU1 V5 launcher has the same parameterization
with a different seed, so it remains deliberately idle; a second seed cannot
repair these structural defects.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V6 (Recurrent-Stroke Repair)

V1--V5 and their evidence remain immutable. The opt-in V6 successors are:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v6`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v6.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v6`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v6.sh`.

V6 is a from-scratch nine-stage course. It preserves V5's 96-D actor,
asymmetric critic, direct measured bounded-QVEL reference, recovered RMP/PD,
fixed-base 4.0 g physics, placed-ball reset, 1.025 m fixed surface, 1.10 m
launch apex, 1.45 m steady apex, directional local workspace, no predictor,
no CMDP and no stochastic DR. It must reject checkpoint resume and may not be
called a continuation of the failed V5 actor.

The structural repair is confined to the failed transition and boundary
credit. Stage 3 is now a 2.4 s post-second-hit exposure lesson and does not
terminate on hit 2, so the actor receives on-policy samples with
`hit_count == 2`. Stage 4 first asks only for mean hits 2.05 and hit-3 rate
0.10 with relaxed conversion/quality gates. Stage 5 restores the stricter
mean-hits 2.20 and hit-3-rate 0.40 entry. Cadence reward and cadence graduation
are disabled through Stage 5 because no steady post-third-hit interval exists
before that boundary. Stages 6--9 retain the V5 steady and directional
workspace sequence.

From Stage 3 onward, the policy receives one causal desired-stroke objective:
a smooth target-error penalty that rises to `+0.55 m/s` during the final
120 ms before predicted contact, reaches that target with 40 ms remaining,
and holds it until the physical edge. It activates only after two confirmed
hits and uses actor-visible state; it does not force the collision, add a
hidden phase teacher or change the observation. A small q-z-gated reward
measures the realized racket vertical speed at the physical contact edge. The
initially considered positive linear pre-contact reward was rejected by frozen
replay because it could reward late downward motion; its weight is therefore
exactly zero in V6.

All stages enable the existing racket-Z terminal penalty and add an 8 mm
inner, normalized quadratic Z barrier with weight 20. The physical and
Cartesian hard limits remain the V5 interval `[1.002, 1.120] m`. A 4 mm
command inset failed four directional grid cells and a 1 mm inset failed one,
so neither is promoted: the soft barrier supplies pre-boundary gradient
without deleting feasible actions. V6 also uses entropy coefficient 0.001,
global minimum log standard deviation -3.0, and a -1.5 per-stage maximum
through the third-hit entry instead of collapsing exploration at the novel
state boundary.

The final fail-closed reachability credential is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v6_reachability_final_20260922/reachability_report.json`
(SHA-256
`b0ef45b676bb269497f29c549665f9498d3d3829d98c1bff3bf0f832b385d703`).
It is bound to the final trainer/environment/screen source hashes and passed
placed launch, steady return and every cell of the V5 directional 3 x 3
quality grid. The trainer's validator independently recomputed all nine cells
and passed.

Frozen deterministic replay used the failed V5 final actor for 256 paired
episodes under the final V6 Stage-3 environment. As required, the old actor
still produced exactly two hits in every episode and hit-3 rate zero. Unlike
V5, all 256 racket-Z exits incurred the terminal penalty (mean -14.70); the
new soft barrier averaged -0.197 and the incorrect recurrent stroke incurred
mean smooth-stroke penalty -1.042. The rejected linear reward remained zero,
while the q-z-gated edge reward was only +0.0186. Thus the repaired signals
identify the known failure without falsely claiming the frozen policy is
fixed. Evidence is under
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v6_frozen_ablation_smooth_softbarrier_20260922/`.

The stopped GPU0 seed-`20262601`, 1024-environment run is
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v6_gpu0_formal_seed20262601_20260922_120353`
(offline W&B `ux75eya8`). Stages 1 and 2 passed rolling and independent block
validation after 116 and 115 updates. Stage 3 initially observed hit-2 rate
0.0625, but PPO drove it to exactly zero by update 14 and it remained zero
through the stop at Stage-3 update 64/global update 295. Mean hits converged to
1.0, edge-to-confirmed-hit conversion to about 0.50, entropy fell to -4.01,
and neither the post-hit2 stroke objective nor a third hit could remain active.

This is a second, earlier method failure: V6 made a newly confirmed second hit
responsible for the complete difficult third-hit tail, including the smooth
error and Z-terminal loss, while a one-hit failure avoided that liability.
The final V6 frozen two-hit actor returned -26.35 under this objective versus
about -7.33 for the learned one-hit Stage-3 policy. V6 therefore learned to
avoid its handoff state. The run was stopped at the preregistered update-60
failure audit plus four save-alignment updates. V6 is a negative result; do
not resume it or launch GPU1 V6.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V7 (Phase-Separated Handoff Credit)

V7 preserves V6 and its negative evidence. Its opt-in profiles are:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v7`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v7.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v7`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v7.sh`.

V7 changes no observation, action, control stack, physics, reset, apex target,
workspace, boundary signal, DR or PPO setting. It expands the course to ten
stages and changes only transition sequencing and reward credit. Stage 3 first
reacquires the V5-proven two-hit transition with the 1.8 s horizon, transition
cadence and termination exactly at hit 2; no post-hit2 objective is active.
Stage 4 then removes that termination, preserves the hit-2 graduation gate,
and collects post-second-hit samples without yet requiring hit 3. Stages 5
and 6 retain V6's relaxed and strict third-hit gates; Stages 7--10 preserve
the steady/workspace tail.

The V6 negative smooth cost is disabled in every V7 stage. Stage 4 onward uses
a bounded positive reciprocal-pseudo-Huber score for matching the same causal
`+0.55 m/s` VZ target during the last 120 ms. It is zero outside the valid
post-hit2 crossing window and cannot make entering that state worse than
avoiding hit 2. A once-per-episode confirmed-hit2 handoff credit is introduced
only to offset the newly exposed tail liability, then tapered from 20 to 12,
6 and 0 over Stages 4--7. The full Z terminal penalty and soft barrier remain
active, so the bridge does not hide an unsafe boundary exit.

Frozen 256-episode replay of the same failed V5 two-hit actor verifies the
credit arithmetic. Every episode retained exactly two hits and the -14.70 Z
terminal penalty. Handoff credit was exactly +20 once per episode, positive
smooth credit averaged +0.503, the old smooth penalty was exactly zero, and
mean total return changed from V6's -26.35 to -4.96. This makes a valid second
hit preferable to the observed V6 one-hit failure without falsely converting
the old actor into a third-hit policy. Evidence is under
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v7_frozen_ablation_20260922/`.

The final V7 reachability credential is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v7_reachability_20260922/reachability_report.json`
(SHA-256
`166464247e5c38b8683345c29055f5932eb5462b4200a0e1aca9d847c0c56759`).
It passed launch, steady return, all 9/9 directional cells and the trainer's
hash-bound recomputation. The focused V1--V4/V6/V7 suite passed 33 tests.

The stopped formal GPU0 run is
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v7_gpu0_formal_seed20262701_20260922_131039`
(offline W&B `1031w6oe`), with 1024 environments and random initialization.
Stages 1 and 2 passed rolling plus independent validation after 120 and 115
updates. Stage 3 briefly observed hit-2 rate 0.0119 at update 2, fell to zero
by update 15 and remained zero through the stop at Stage-3 update 65/global
update 300. Mean hits converged to 1.0, edge-to-confirmed-hit conversion fell
to about 0.499, and entropy fell to -4.246. This reproduces the one-hit local
optimum on a different seed even though V7 removed the V6 post-hit2 liability.
The V5/V7 Stage-3 objectives are otherwise numerically identical on the
observed lanes; V5's success was therefore seed-sensitive rather than a
robustly learnable transition. V7 is a negative result. Do not resume it or
launch GPU1 V7.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle From-Scratch V8 (Shaped Acquisition, Unshaped Retention)

V8 preserves V1--V7 and their evidence. Its opt-in profiles are:

- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v8`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v8.sh`;
- `fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu1_v8`, launched only by
  `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v8.sh`.

V8 changes no observation, action, controller, plant, physics, reset, apex,
workspace, boundary, DR or PPO contract. It has eleven stages. Stages 1--2
preserve V7 exactly. Stage 3 is a temporary recurrent-upstroke acquisition
bridge: only after the first confirmed hit, with a valid descending-plane
prediction, no pending contact and `0 < TTC <= 0.12 s`, it adds
`8 * clip(racket_vz / 0.55, -1, 1) * dt`. The per-step term is bounded to
`[-0.04,+0.04]`, gives zero credit for waiting, penalizes downward motion and
cannot activate before the first hit. Its graduation gate requires mean hits
1.15 and hit-2 rate 0.20 after at least 80 updates and 16 consecutive passing
windows.

Stage 4 removes that temporary reward exactly and restores V7's original
two-hit gate: mean hits 1.45, hit-2 rate 0.55, the complete cadence/apex/
contact-quality constraints, at least 180 updates, 24 passing windows and
independent deterministic self-validation. Thus later training cannot advance
on a policy that only exploits the shaping term. V7 Stages 4--10 then remain
in order as V8 Stages 5--11, including positive post-hit2 exposure, tapered
handoff credit, third-hit lessons and steady/workspace lessons.

The hash-bound V8 reachability report is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v8_reachability_20260922/reachability_report.json`
(SHA-256
`42bd279170c050f0ed8f6be2eae29426dfc40c110ca935d65282921daf5ffdb3`).
It passed GPU execution, placed launch, steady return, all 9/9 directional
quality cells and the trainer's independent source-hash recomputation. The
focused V1--V8 suite passed 37 tests. V8 remains experimental and
simulation-only until Stage 3 acquisition, Stage 4 unshaped retention,
post-hit2 exposure, hit 3 and all later stages pass their registered gates.

The formal GPU0 V8 run
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v8_gpu0_formal_seed20262801_20260922_141908`
(1024 environments, seed `20262801`, offline W&B `bvzd9ww4`) passed Stages 1
and 2 at updates 118 and 115. Stage 3 solved hit two immediately and retained
about 0.99 hit-2 rate, but its rolling hit-racket VXY reached
`0.1967/0.2703 m/s` mean/RMS at the stop at Stage-3 update 137, versus the
`0.08/0.12 m/s` gate. Unlike V5's unshaped trace, it did not trend down after
update 100. V8's acquisition gate was self-locking because strict precision
was required before the conflicting temporary reward could be removed. V8 is
a negative result; do not resume it or launch GPU1 V8.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle V12 (Pinned V9-S5 Third-Hit Experiment)

V12 corrects the V10/V11 experimental confound. Its opt-in profiles are
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v12` and the configuration-equivalent
GPU1 identity. V12 is continuation-only; the reviewed GPU0 launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v12_resume_v9_s5.sh`.
It restores only the passed V9 Stage-5 checkpoint
`05_fplc_v9_gpu0_s5_post_second_hit_positive_exposure.pkl`, SHA-256
`8d76e630d12467fc19f9bf7feaa848335ad457db9b5a241f5dc62e5b57555020`,
at step `82,444,288`, global update `629`, Stage-5 update `95`, and starts a
fresh V12 Stage-6 convergence window. Actor, 417-D asymmetric critic and Adam
moments (`t=19434`) must all be restored; another checkpoint, from-scratch

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle V14 (Dynamic Incoming-Speed Limit Cycle)

V14 replaces V13's stage-specific `0.81 -> 0.55 m/s` scalar targets with one
causal per-lane impact law. Its profiles are
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v14` and the configuration-equivalent
GPU1 identity. V14 changes observation/reward semantics and is therefore
from-scratch only; V9--V13 checkpoints, curriculum history, actor/critic and
Adam state are rejected. The reviewed GPU0 launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v14.sh`
and fixes 1024 environments, seed `20263201`, the 96-D actor, 417-D
asymmetric critic and the existing measured-QVEL -> bounded qref -> recovered
RMP/PD action path. It does not add another controller, predictor, CMDP or
stochastic DR layer.

For signed predicted incoming ball velocity `v_in`, absolute target apex
`z_apex`, contact ball-center height `z_c=1.045 m`, gravity magnitude `g`, and
effective normal restitution `e=0.665`, the single active target is

```text
v_ball,out* = sqrt(2*g*(z_apex-z_c))
v_racket,z* = (v_ball,out* + e*v_in)/(1+e)
```

The actor observes the same executable target used by dense stroke and
physical-edge reward. Raw and executable targets and clipping are separately
logged. The executable target is bounded to `[0,0.90] m/s`; clipping never
silently changes the apex goal. The ideal phase values are launch `0.62358`,
transition-1 `0.86051`, transition-2 `0.84415`, and steady `0.56687 m/s`.
They are diagnostics only: every lane is recomputed online from its own
predicted incoming velocity.

Exactly one apex objective is active at a time. Confirmed hit counts
`0/1/>=2` select absolute apex `1.10/1.275/1.45 m`. The placed-ball launch
keeps its matched `0.624 m/s` launch objective; from the first confirmed hit
onward the old recurrent fixed-speed reward is zero. The dynamic target drives
a continuous pre-contact Z reference: over the last `0.20 s`, the racket
descends at most `15 mm` and returns to the `1.025 m` plane with the requested
contact speed. Its full target envelope is `1.010--1.025 m`, inside the
Cartesian hard set. This resolves the launch/steady reward conflict while
allowing one to two contacts to reach the nominal orbit.

V14 preserves the complete twelve-stage V12 gate route but applies the same
dynamic law in every stage so actor semantics never change. Stages 1--2 teach
the placed launch; Stages 3--5 acquire and retain the second contact; Stages
6--8 acquire the third contact/steady entry; Stages 9--12 extend centered and
local-workspace survival. Advancement remains convergence- and independent
block-validation-gated with no forced stage cap.

The final hash-bound GPU0 report is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v14_reachability_c1_robust4_contract_20260922/reachability_report.json`
(SHA-256
`517e735a84fc868fc12441d9c46219df4e42c04c2569160149f10b1023636486`).
It records CUDA GPU UUID `GPU-91f9b105-f5c8-b00e-de70-39d3ee1ce7b4`, passes
reset, placed launch, the 1.45 m steady orbit, the dynamic four-phase law and
the `1.010--1.025 m` reference envelope. All 9/9 directional XY cells pass
without relaxing apex, quality or safety thresholds; V14 additionally
requires at least two independent witnesses per cell, with observed counts
`6/3/30/6/3/26/6/7/2`. The trainer independently recomputed source hashes and
lane evidence. The complete V1--V14 regression had 61 passing tests; the
additional double-witness fail-closed regression also passed. V14 remains
experimental and simulation-only until PPO completes all rolling and block
gates; reachability evidence is not convergence evidence.

The formal GPU0 run is
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v14_seed20263201_20260922_223315`
(offline W&B `j2t2ip6d`). Stage 1 converged without gate relaxation at update
124 and entered `fplc_v14_gpu0_s2_launch_precision`: final rolling hit1 was
`0.976`, rolling apex_abs `1.125 m` inside the registered `1.070--1.135 m`
band, racket VXY mean/RMS `0.07/0.07 m/s`, and edge conversion `0.976`.
The Stage-1 checkpoint SHA-256 is
`ebcc3920d4f1525dc473136aba4b14703631fe5e6a633dd27f49b62f5e6a015b`.
This is positive launch-course evidence only, not evidence that recurrent
Stages 3--12 converge. GPU1 remains idle pending a distinct preregistered
parameter hypothesis.

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle V15--V20 (Invariant Objective and Gradual Apex)

V15--V18 are preserved negative from-scratch diagnostics. They kept the V14
dynamic incoming-speed collision inverse but exposed the complete six-second
launch-to-steady objective from update 1, with fixed-plane, apex, horizontal
motion and racket angular-quality shaping active throughout. V16 removed the
Stage-1 maximum-log-std cap; V17 disabled a logged-only native-contact-edge
VXY term that was found not to contribute to total reward; V18 reduced the
confirmed-hit negative-event budget from `0.98` to `0.65`. The same-seed
50-update V18 probe nevertheless collapsed to zero hits while improving
return by reducing Cartesian projection cost. These experiments reject a
random-init full-horizon route: the dominant gradient selects safe/no-contact
behavior before sparse recurrent success appears.

V19 preserves the V18 reward, reset, physics, observation and control domain,
but introduces causal success boundaries: one hit, two hits, three hits, then
the full six-second horizon. Run
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v19_gpu0_probe_seed20263301_20260923` passed Stage 1
at update 91 (rolling hit1 about `0.9495`) and Stage 2 at update 115 (rolling
mean hits `1.946`, next-contact anchor error about `0.04 m`). Stage 3 was
stopped after 82 updates because hit3 and hit3 events were zero in every
update, while mean hits stayed about `1.958` and horizontal quality continued
to improve. This is positive evidence for causal prefix credit assignment and
negative evidence for V19's coarse `1.10 -> 1.275 -> 1.45 m` apex schedule.

V20 is the opt-in successor. Its profiles are
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v20` and the configuration-equivalent
GPU1 identity; both reject resume checkpoints and use a random 96-D actor,
417-D asymmetric critic, measured-QVEL persistent bounded reference and the
unchanged recovered-RMP/PD path. The reviewed launchers are
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v20.sh`
and `pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu1_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v20.sh`.
They fix 1024 environments and seeds `20263401/20263402`. GPU1 remains idle
until GPU0 demonstrates a distinct positive hit3/height result.

V20 changes only the hit-conditioned apex transition relative to V19. The
single target progresses over four confirmed-hit intervals as
`1.10, 1.1875, 1.275, 1.3625, 1.45 m`; thereafter it remains exactly
`1.45 m`. Under the registered ideal incoming velocities, the associated
racket-VZ targets are `0.6236, 0.5891, 0.6077, 0.6502, 0.6958`, then
`0.5669 m/s` steady. Actual targets are still recomputed per lane from signed
incoming ball VZ and the requested apex. None of the ideal phases reaches the
registered `0.90 m/s` execution cap.

The seven-stage course expands only the causal success boundary and gates:
Stages 1--5 terminate after 1/2/3/4/5 confirmed hits, followed by a full-
horizon acquisition stage and a centered limit-cycle stage. Every stage uses
the same six-second physical horizon, reward coefficients, reset, physics,
observations, action semantics and transition count. Fixed-plane, apex,
ball/racket VXY, complete racket-angular-speed, contact-quality and anchor
shaping are active from Stage 1. Thus each prefix extends one final behavior;
there is no low-apex pretraining objective to unlearn. Prefix stages retain
uncapped maximum log standard deviation; the cap `-1.5` begins only after the
five-hit steady target has been exposed.

The final V20 GPU0 reachability report is

`1bc3277c1d7beaf9ea00b3547087c0f8a7c21e317fcc8fae89899b8372a8e8dd`;

The formal V20 GPU0 run

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle V22 (Nonbinding Measured-Error Envelope)

`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v22` is a GPU0-only opt-in
continuation from the same pinned, independently passed V20 Stage-5
checkpoint and optimizer state as V21. It copies all 14 V21 lessons, PPO,
reward, reset, observation, physics, RMP/PD and Cartesian projection
settings. The only control change is the seven-joint measured-q reference
error horizon from `(18,19,19,18,18,18,18) ms` to `10 s` per joint. For the
pinned XML, the maximum full joint-range / velocity-limit duration is
`1.459 s`; therefore the `q_measured +/- v_max*T` interval cannot clip a
reference already inside the hard joint-position limits. The persistent
`q_ref(t+1)=q_ref(t)+v_policy*5 ms` integrator, normalized action and
joint-QVEL limits remain in force, as do the Cartesian projector, its
nonlinear FK backstop, RMP/PD and the observed `q_ref-q_measured` suffix.
This is not the released GPU0-QVEL/GPU1-QACC command-state actuator path.

The preregistered diagnostic witness is the V20 Stage-6 projected 5-cycle
reference audit
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/periodic_projected_reference_audit_v1_gpu0_seed20263507_20260923/report.json`.
All six successful 5-cycle lanes use <0.36 normalized action, but the old
18/19 ms measured-error window is exceeded for 305--325 steady ticks per
lane; the maximum required horizons are 35.38 ms (joint 4) and 24.90 ms
(joint 6). This proves only that V21 cannot reproduce those exact joint
references. It does not prove V22 PPO convergence or remove the need to
check accumulated reference error, actual racket workspace, qvel/qacc,
apex, hits and survival. The earlier synthetic QVEL tracker reached 5/6
5-cycle passes at 2x horizon versus 0/6 at the original horizon; neither
is a trained-policy result.

The V22 analytic-controller reachability screen is a retained negative
diagnostic: launch passed, but 0/640 steady lanes reached a valid hit
(`.../fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v22_center_reachability_20260923_negative.json`).
That screen's fixed tracking controller was tuned for the old anti-windup
window and is not the policy action-path upper bound. The same frozen V20-S5
actor, 16 matched reset lanes and 1200 steps instead yielded V21/V22 first-
episode mean hits `3.9375/4.9375`, hit6 `0/16 vs 5/16` lanes, actual Cartesian
workspace violations `0/0`, qvel exceedance `0/0`, and qacc exceedance
`0.00522/0.00988` (fraction of evaluated samples). This is positive but
small-sample simulation evidence, not PPO convergence or hardware safety.

V22 requires a current-code-hashed frozen-policy V21/V22 control-pair report
with hit6, workspace, qvel, qacc and projection-fallback gates; it does not
use the failed analytic-controller screen as a PPO launch gate. Its reviewed
launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v22_resume_v20_s5.sh`;
it preserves 1024 environments, the pinned source/XML SHA, fresh Stage-6
history and the explicit experimental-DR acknowledgment. During training,
require hit6/height improvement without regression in workspace, limits,
view, contact quality or survival. GPU1 remains idle.


A same-seed, same-reset-qpos repeat with the final trainer hash failed the
predeclared control-pair gate: V21/V22 mean hits were `4.0000/4.4375`,
but hit6 was `0/16` in both groups; V22 qacc exceedance was `0.00993`

Consequently the reviewed V22 launcher remains evidence-blocked and no
formal V22 PPO run should start from this result. The first replay's hit6

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle V23 (Rapid Steady, Full Horizon From Stage 1)

`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v23` is an opt-in, from-scratch GPU0
course. It inherits V22's nonbinding measured-q reference-error envelope,
persistent bounded-QVEL reference integration, Cartesian hard projection,
recovered RMP/PD, 96-D actor, placed-ball reset, ball/contact physics and
local workspace.
No V20/V22 actor, critic or optimizer state is imported. All four stages
run the full 6 s horizon; `terminate_after_confirmed_hits=0` from Stage 1.
The first-hit and recurrent-hit timeout values are also zero. V23 alone
uses `episode_phase_stagger_min_frac=1.0` so the trainer's first-reset
phase staggering cannot create shortened, falsely successful episodes.
Physical failure and the genuine 1200-step time limit remain active.

The one invariant per-impact absolute-apex schedule is hit 1/2/3/4+ =
`1.10 / 1.249 / 1.40 / 1.45 m`. Each stage uses the same reward and
physics; only graduation gates and exploration caps change. The active
scheduled target drives the incoming-ball-VZ collision inverse, actor
progress observation, native confirmed-hit quality reward and new bounded
per-impact apex event reward. The latter adds a broad 80 mm and narrow
25 mm Gaussian about the active target and penalizes overshoot, so the
early low-apex solution cannot receive the late 1.45 m credit. Hit-4+
apex-band, actual contact-surface-height error, racket VXY RMS and full
racket-angular-speed RMS are logged and required for later-stage graduation
both on rolling training episodes and the independent block evaluation.
Stage 1 can be passed on launch acquisition, but it never ends an episode
at hit 1; Stage 4 requires repeat survival and late-impact quality.

The nominal same-height ballistic calculation at ball-centre contact
`z=1.045 m`, gravity `9.8 m/s²` and effective restitution `0.665` gives
required post-launch racket VZ `0.7863 / 0.7856 / 0.6386 / 0.5669 m/s`
for hits 2/3/4/steady, below the existing `0.90 m/s` target cap.
This is a feasibility calculation, not a learned-policy outcome.
The reused physical GPU0 RMP/PD+projector five-cycle report is
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/periodic_bounded_qvel_v1_gpu0_h2p0_seed20263508_20260923/report.json`,
SHA-256 `cde0f70415a70512252c151c8d1dc0092e8aef732d2795764da8e599ce5ae8db`.
It passed five of six steady lanes at 1.44 m target. Among passing
lanes, the best worst-of-five VXY was `0.01277 m/s`; the best
worst-of-five full angular speed was `0.07343 rad/s` in a different
lane. These are demonstrated values, not global minima, and do not prove
the launch-to-hit-4 transition or PPO convergence. No redundant new
periodic-motion sweep was performed.

The reviewed launcher is
`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v23.sh`.
It fixes 1024 environments and seed `20263523`, requires the pinned report,
measured 4 g mass interval, RMP replay, physical GPU0 UUID and explicit
experimental-DR acknowledgment, and refuses an existing output directory.
V23 remains simulation-only; training acceptance requires hit-indexed
apex outcomes, survival, actual contact height, VXY/omega, view and safety
with no regression. A five-cycle reference witness alone is not evidence
of learned transition, stable juggling or hardware readiness.

The 2026-09-23 bounded GPU0 code-path audit is recorded in
`pingpong_controller/outputs/rl_sim/fixed_plane_limit_cycle_v23_rapid_steady_review_20260923.md`.
The final 32-env/32-step/one-update smoke reached a finite optimizer update
on CUDA GPU0 with zero artificially shortened episodes; it exited only
because the deliberately imposed one-update cap was unconverged.
Earlier bounded attempts exposed and corrected undefined no-hit telemetry,

## Fixed-Plane Limit-Cycle V24 (Subfloor Lift and Motion-Quality Bridge)

`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v24` is an opt-in, from-scratch
successor to the stopped V23 run. It preserves V23's 96-D actor, measured
persistent QVEL integration with the nonbinding measured-error envelope,
Cartesian projector, recovered RMP/PD, placed-ball reset, native contact,
workspace, six-second full horizon, and per-hit absolute-apex targets
`1.10 / 1.249 / 1.40 / 1.45 m`. It never imports the V23 checkpoint as a
training parent, and V23's four-stage profile remains unchanged.

V23 was stopped at update 424 after a prolonged Stage-1 plateau: mean hits
`1.876`, mean absolute apex `1.185 m`, and hit-3 rate zero since update
187. Its frozen update-420 checkpoint is
`fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_gpu0_v23_seed20263523_20260923_formal1/mjx_curriculum_last.pkl`,
SHA-256 `04d14864792efada573ce80fa1d6bfbfbfa4c8ab65a3e212a0acd74ae30c157f`.
On a matched 16-lane, first-episode GPU0 native-contact replay, every lane
had two confirmed hits followed by a third physical impact whose predicted
apex averaged `1.1595 m`. Those subfloor impacts earned no V23 rapid-steady
apex reward. The dominant bottleneck is therefore third-impact lift and
survival, not the absence of a third contact. Increasing the old hit-event
racket-VXY penalty alone would be ineffective because its event budget is
already clipped.

V24 enables a new reward only on a recurrent subfloor launch with a
scheduled target at least 1.40 m: a nonnegative linear bridge from zero at
ball-centre contact height to the existing scheduled-apex Gaussian reward
at the survival threshold. It leaves the confirmed-hit and low-survival
reward paths unchanged, avoids paying for an event with no physical contact,
and is opt-in only. The effective dense pre-contact racket-VXY reward weight
rises `0.10 -> 0.30`, the dense low-angular reward weight `0.10 -> 0.20`,
and angular-stability penalty weight `0.50 -> 0.75`. No control limits,
action scaling, contact geometry or high-apex target are relaxed.

Six full-horizon lessons, rather than four, separate launch-pair,
third-lift, third-confirm, fourth-entry, steady-quality and full-commit.
The reward contract remains invariant across all six; only graduation
metrics and the final exploration cap vary. Stage 2 requires nonzero
third-hit probability, Stage 3 requires sustained third confirmation,
Stage 4 introduces the hit-4 apex/plane/motion gate, and Stages 5--6
tighten the late-hit apex band, racket VXY/omega and long survival.
All advancement still requires rolling and independent block evaluation;
there is no forced update cap or per-hit termination. Stage 6 retains
the 1.43 m hit-4+ apex floor, 1.45 m schedule, fixed-plane contact and
low-horizontal/low-angular-motion gates.

`pingpong_controller/tools/rl_sim/run_gpu0_fixed_plane_limit_cycle_qvel_rmp_v24.sh`.
It fixes 1024 environments, seed `20263524`, physical GPU0 UUID
`GPU-91f9b105-f5c8-b00e-de70-39d3ee1ce7b4`, the existing hash-bound
five-cycle reachability report and experimental-DR acknowledgments.
V24 is simulation-only. The V24 native-contact replay established that
third-impact subfloor events receive the new reward while V23 does not.
Strict per-lane V23/V24 trajectory parity is not a valid GPU acceptance gate:
two V23 replays of the same checkpoint and reset seed themselves disagreed
on five first-episode outcomes after tiny first-step numerical differences.
Both paired reports are retained as negative evidence for that proposed
test, not as evidence of a changed controller. The bounded CUDA GPU smoke,
profile regressions and source/launcher audit are the code-path launch
gates. They do not prove third/fourth-hit learning or real-robot readiness.
